The Sheffield gas outage was a stark reminder of the interconnectedness of our infrastructure. A single point of failure in one system – a burst water main – led to a cascading crisis in another essential service.

**What caused the gas supply outage?**
The primary cause was a **burst water main** on the Yorkshire Water network, specifically an asbestos-cement pipe from 1970 on Bankfield Lane in Stannington. This burst allowed **more than 2 million litres of water to flood into the Cadent Gas supply network**.

**How long did the outage last?**
The outage began on **December 2nd, 2022**. While many properties had their gas reconnected gradually, some homes, particularly in areas like Hillsborough and Malin Bridge, were without a gas supply for **almost two weeks**, with full restoration for all properties occurring around **December 16th**.

The incident highlighted the importance of infrastructure maintenance, emergency preparedness, and community spirit. While Yorkshire Water faced criticism for the burst main, Cadent Gas and Northern Powergrid were largely praised for their rapid and dedicated response in a truly unprecedented situation, working tirelessly to bring warmth and light back to the homes of Sheffield.

input.user_message: Create an educational story that helps students understand: What caused the gas supply outage in Sheffield, England in December 2022, and how long did the outage last?
merged_contexts:
The city of Sheffield, England was impacted by a major failure of the local natural gas supply network in December 2022, resulting in a loss of central heating and gas stove availability to more than 3,000 properties in the northwestern suburbs of the city. The outage, which has predominantly affected the Hillsborough, Malin Bridge and Stannington districts, was declared a major incident by Sheffield City Council; some properties were without a gas supply for almost two weeks.
The gas supply outage affected the Cadent Gas network, and was caused by a burst water main on the Yorkshire Water network which resulted in more than 2 million litres of water flooding into the gas supply network. Yorkshire Water confirmed that the breach to the water main had been resolved by 6 December. In addition to the widespread gas supply outage, numerous properties in the affected areas have also suffered from outages to their water and electricity supplies as knock-on effects.Heavy rainfall initially hampered recovery work, followed by cold temperatures and snowfall. In response to the widespread lack of heating availability and increasingly cold temperatures, dropping as low as −3 °C (27 °F) on 9 December, a major incident was declared by local authorities. The Red Cross distributed aid, including food, drinks and blankets, to residents in the affected area.

Timeline
During the evening of 2 December, a water main on Bankfield Lane at the western end of Stannington burst, resulting in flooding in the local area. The affected water main was an asbestos-cement mainline pipe installed in 1970. More than 2 million litres of water, roughly equivalent to three Olympic-sized swimming pools, entered the gas mains in this area and subsequently flowed through pipes down hillsides throughout the Stannington and Hillsborough areas.Property damage was reported in dozens of homes across the affected area, including on High Matlock Road, as water overflowed out of gas meters and gas stoves inside homes; water also overflowed out of manhole covers and the bases of street lights in outdoor areas. Emergency services attended the incident from around midnight, going from door to door to wake residents. Cadent Gas, who operate the natural gas network in the area, described the incident as "unpredecented" and something which they had never had to deal with before.By 3 December more than 1,000 properties were without a gas supply; in addition, many properties in the immediate area of the burst water main also suffered from reduced water supplies, or no water at all, for several days. Engineers from Cadent Gas initially had to go from door to door and turn off the gas supply at each individual affected property, before engineers could commence work to drain and repair the gas network; more than 100 engineers were drafted in to work 24 hours a day to resolve the outage, later rising to more than 200 as the incident progressed.The number of properties affected by the gas supply outage rose to more than 2,000 by 6 December, increasingly affecting homes lower down the hillside in the Hillsborough area of Sheffield. Local electricity network operator Northern Powergrid warned local residents to only use portable electric heaters in occupied rooms and only while residents were at home, in order to reduce strain on the local power supply caused by increased usage of electric heating. Despite this however, residents on some streets in Stannington began to report intermittent power outages throughout the day. Electric car owners were advised to use public charging points rather than those at their own homes.The local authority, Sheffield City Council, officially declared a major incident on 7 December, with thousands of properties still without a gas supply and temperatures forecast to drop below freezing for prolonged periods in the coming days. Only around a quarter of affected properties had had their gas supplies reconnected at the time that the major incident was declared, according to Cadent Gas, as their engineers were struggling to pump the large quantities of water out of the complex local gas network; engineers and equipment were shipped in from across the country to assist in draining the network.According to Cadent Gas, around three-quarters of affected properties had been reconnected to the gas network by 10 December. Considerable difficulties remained in draining water from the gas network in the Hillsborough and Malin Bridge areas, where hundreds of homes still remained without gas.

Response
Refuge spaces were opened officially by the local authorities and unofficially by local businesses, providing warm spaces, hot food and drinks to affected residents. ## The Silent Flood: Sheffield's Gas Crisis of 2022

The air was crisp, the scent of impending winter hung heavy, and the festive season was just around the corner in Sheffield, December 2022. But for thousands of residents in the northwestern suburbs, particularly Hillsborough, Malin Bridge, and Stannington, the usual warmth of their homes was about to be replaced by a chilling silence. This is the story of the "Silent Flood," a major gas supply outage that plunged parts of Sheffield into a cold, dark two weeks.

### Chapter 1: The Unseen Enemy Beneath

Our story begins on the evening of **December 2nd, 2022**. Picture Bankfield Lane in Stannington, a quiet street like many others. Deep beneath the surface, an old **asbestos-cement mainline pipe**, installed all the way back in 1970, was silently battling an internal struggle. This pipe, part of the **Yorkshire Water network**, was designed to carry clean drinking water to homes.

Suddenly, with a groan that no one above ground could hear, the pipe gave way. It **burst**. This wasn't a small leak; it was a catastrophic failure. More than **2 million litres of water** – that’s enough to fill three Olympic-sized swimming pools – began to gush out.

Now, here's where the problem became truly unique and devastating. This gushing water didn't just flood the street. It found its way into the **Cadent Gas network**, the intricate web of underground pipes that carries natural gas to homes for heating and cooking. Imagine a giant, hidden underground river, now flowing not with gas, but with water.

### Chapter 2: Water in the Wires (and Pipes!)

As the water surged through the gas mains, it began to flow downhill, following the natural contours of the land through Stannington and Hillsborough. The consequences were immediate and alarming.

Around **midnight**, emergency services were called. They went door-to-door, waking residents, not because of a fire, but because water was starting to overflow. Inside homes, water was bubbling out of gas meters and even from gas stoves! Outdoors, manhole covers were lifting, and water was seeping from the bases of streetlights. It was a surreal and unprecedented situation. **Cadent Gas**, the company responsible for the gas network, described it as something they had "never had to deal with before."

By **December 3rd**, the scale of the disaster was becoming clear. More than **1,000 properties** were without a gas supply. To make matters worse, many homes in the immediate vicinity of the burst water main also experienced reduced or no water supply for several days.

Cadent Gas engineers faced a monumental task. They couldn't just turn the gas back on; the pipes were full of water! First, they had to go to each affected property individually and **turn off the gas supply at the meter** to prevent further damage and ensure safety. This was a painstaking process. More than **100 engineers** were drafted in, working 24 hours a day, a number that soon swelled to over 200.

### Chapter 3: The Deep Freeze and the Major Incident

As the days passed, the situation worsened. By **December 6th**, the number of properties without gas had risen to **over 2,000**, extending further down the hillsides into Hillsborough. The initial heavy rainfall that accompanied the burst main turned into bitterly cold temperatures and even snowfall. Temperatures plummeted, reaching as low as **-3°C (27°F)** on December 9th.

With no central heating, residents were struggling. They relied on electric heaters, which put a massive strain on the local electricity network. **Northern Powergrid**, the electricity supplier, had to advise residents to use heaters sparingly to avoid complete power outages. Despite these warnings, some streets in Stannington began to experience intermittent power cuts.

The severity of the situation led the **Sheffield City Council** to declare a **major incident on December 7th**. This declaration was crucial because it allowed local authorities to better coordinate the massive response needed. At this point, only about a quarter of the affected properties had had their gas supplies reconnected. Cadent Gas engineers, despite their tireless efforts, were battling to pump vast quantities of water out of a complex and extensive underground network. Equipment and engineers were brought in from across the country to assist.

### Chapter 4: The Long Road to Recovery

The outage was a test of resilience for the community. Local businesses and authorities stepped up. Refuge spaces were opened, offering warmth, hot food, and drinks. Lomas Hall became a central hub, providing portable electric heaters and hotplates. The Peacock Inn and Crown & Glove pubs offered food, drinks, and even showering facilities. Schools remained open, using electric heaters and advising students to dress warmly.

By **December 10th**, Cadent Gas reported that around three-quarters of affected properties had been reconnected. However, significant challenges remained in the Hillsborough and Malin Bridge areas, where hundreds of homes were still without gas. The process of draining water from such a vast and intricate network was incredibly difficult.

The outage, which started on **December 2nd**, dragged on for almost two weeks for some properties. While many were reconnected sooner, some residents endured the cold and inconvenience until around **December 16th**, marking a nearly **two-week period without gas**.

### Chapter 5: Lessons Learned and Lasting Impact

The Sheffield gas outage was a stark reminder of the interconnectedness of our infrastructure. A single point of failure in one system – a burst water main – led to a cascading crisis in another essential service.

**What caused the gas supply outage?**
The primary cause was a **burst water main** on the Yorkshire Water network, specifically an asbestos-cement pipe from 1970 on Bankfield Lane in Stannington. This burst allowed **more than 2 million litres of water to flood into the Cadent Gas supply network**.

**How long did the outage last?**
The outage began on **December 2nd, 2022**. While many properties had their gas reconnected gradually, some homes, particularly in areas like Hillsborough and Malin Bridge, were without a gas supply for **almost two weeks**, with full restoration for all properties occurring around **December 16th**.

The incident highlighted the importance of infrastructure maintenance, emergency preparedness, and community spirit. While Yorkshire Water faced criticism for the burst main, Cadent Gas and Northern Powergrid were largely praised for their rapid and dedicated response in a truly unprecedented situation, working tirelessly to bring warmth and light back to the homes of Sheffield.

## The Silent Flood: Sheffield's Gas Crisis of 2022

The air was crisp, the scent of impending winter hung heavy, and the festive season was just around the corner in Sheffield, December 2022. But for thousands of residents in the northwestern suburbs, particularly Hillsborough, Malin Bridge, and Stannington, the usual warmth of their homes was about to be replaced by a chilling silence. This is the story of the "Silent Flood," a major gas supply outage that plunged parts of Sheffield into a cold, dark two weeks.

### Chapter 1: The Unseen Enemy Beneath

Our story begins on the evening of **December 2nd, 2022**. Picture Bankfield Lane in Stannington, a quiet street like many others. Deep beneath the surface, an old **asbestos-cement mainline pipe**, installed all the way back in 1970, was silently battling an internal struggle. This pipe, part of the **Yorkshire Water network**, was designed to carry clean drinking water to homes.

Suddenly, with a groan that no one above ground could hear, the pipe gave way. It **burst**. This wasn't a small leak; it was a catastrophic failure. More than **2 million litres of water** – that’s enough to fill three Olympic-sized swimming pools – began to gush out.

Now, here's where the problem became truly unique and devastating. This gushing water didn't just flood the street. It found its way into the **Cadent Gas network**, the intricate web of underground pipes that carries natural gas to homes for heating and cooking. Imagine a giant, hidden underground river, now flowing not with gas, but with water.

### Chapter 2: Water in the Wires (and Pipes!)

As the water surged through the gas mains, it began to flow downhill, following the natural contours of the land through Stannington and Hillsborough. The consequences were immediate and alarming.

Around **midnight**, emergency services were called. They went door-to-door, waking residents, not because of a fire, but because water was starting to overflow. Inside homes, water was bubbling out of gas meters and even from gas stoves! Outdoors, manhole covers were lifting, and water was seeping from the bases of streetlights. It was a surreal and unprecedented situation. **Cadent Gas**, the company responsible for the gas network, described it as something they had "never had to deal with before."

By **December 3rd**, the scale of the disaster was becoming clear. More than **1,000 properties** were without a gas supply. To make matters worse, many homes in the immediate vicinity of the burst water main also experienced reduced or no water supply for several days.

Cadent Gas engineers faced a monumental task. They couldn't just turn the gas back on; the pipes were full of water! First, they had to go to each affected property individually and **turn off the gas supply at the meter** to prevent further damage and ensure safety. This was a painstaking process. More than **100 engineers** were drafted in, working 24 hours a day, a number that soon swelled to over 200.

### Chapter 3: The Deep Freeze and the Major Incident

As the days passed, the situation worsened. By **December 6th**, the number of properties without gas had risen to **over 2,000**, extending further down the hillsides into Hillsborough. The initial heavy rainfall that accompanied the burst main turned into bitterly cold temperatures and even snowfall. Temperatures plummeted, reaching as low as **-3°C (27°F)** on December 9th.

With no central heating, residents were struggling. They relied on electric heaters, which put a massive strain on the local electricity network. **Northern Powergrid**, the electricity supplier, had to advise residents to use heaters sparingly to avoid complete power outages. Despite these warnings, some streets in Stannington began to experience intermittent power cuts.

The severity of the situation led the **Sheffield City Council** to declare a **major incident on December 7th**. This declaration was crucial because it allowed local authorities to better coordinate the massive response needed. At this point, only about a quarter of the affected properties had had their gas supplies reconnected. Cadent Gas engineers, despite their tireless efforts, were battling to pump vast quantities of water out of a complex and extensive underground network. Equipment and engineers were brought in from across the country to assist.

### Chapter 4: The Long Road to Recovery

The outage was a test of resilience for the community. Local businesses and authorities stepped up. Refuge spaces were opened, offering warmth, hot food, and drinks. Lomas Hall became a central hub, providing portable electric heaters and hotplates. The Peacock Inn and Crown & Glove pubs offered food, drinks, and even showering facilities. Schools remained open, using electric heaters and advising students to dress warmly.

By **December 10th**, Cadent Gas reported that around three-quarters of affected properties had been reconnected. However, significant challenges remained in the Hillsborough and Malin Bridge areas, where hundreds of homes were still without gas. The process of draining water from such a vast and intricate network was incredibly difficult.

The outage, which started on **December 2nd**, dragged on for almost two weeks for some properties. While many were reconnected sooner, some residents endured the cold and inconvenience until around **December 16th**, marking a nearly **two-week period without gas**.

### Chapter 5: Lessons Learned and Lasting Impact

The Sheffield gas outage was a stark reminder of the interconnectedness of our infrastructure. A single point of failure in one system – a burst water main – led to a cascading crisis in another essential service.

**What caused the gas supply outage?**
The primary cause was a **burst water main** on the Yorkshire Water network, specifically an asbestos-cement pipe from 1970 on Bankfield Lane in Stannington. This burst allowed **more than 2 million litres of water to flood into the Cadent Gas supply network**.

**How long did the outage last?**
The outage began on **December 2nd, 2022**. While many properties had their gas reconnected gradually, some homes, particularly in areas like Hillsborough and Malin Bridge, were without a gas supply for **almost two weeks**, with full restoration for all properties occurring around **December 16th**.

The incident highlighted the importance of infrastructure maintenance, emergency preparedness, and community spirit. While Yorkshire Water faced criticism for the burst main, Cadent Gas and Northern Powergrid were largely praised for their rapid and dedicated response in a truly unprecedented situation, working tirelessly to bring warmth and light back to the homes of Sheffield.

## The Silent Flood: Sheffield's Gas Crisis of 2022

The air was crisp, the scent of impending winter hung heavy, and the festive season was just around the corner in Sheffield, December 2022. But for thousands of residents in the northwestern suburbs, particularly Hillsborough, Malin Bridge, and Stannington, the usual warmth of their homes was about to be replaced by a chilling silence. This is the story of the "Silent Flood," a major gas supply outage that plunged parts of Sheffield into a cold, dark two weeks.

### Chapter 1: The Unseen Enemy Beneath

Our story begins on the evening of **December 2nd, 2022**. Picture Bankfield Lane in Stannington, a quiet street like many others. Deep beneath the surface, an old **asbestos-cement mainline pipe**, installed all the way back in 1970, was silently battling an internal struggle. This pipe, part of the **Yorkshire Water network**, was designed to carry clean drinking water to homes.

Suddenly, with a groan that no one above ground could hear, the pipe gave way. It **burst**. This wasn't a small leak; it was a catastrophic failure. More than **2 million litres of water** – that’s enough to fill three Olympic-sized swimming pools – began to gush out.

Now, here's where the problem became truly unique and devastating. This gushing water didn't just flood the street. It found its way into the **Cadent Gas network**, the intricate web of underground pipes that carries natural gas to homes for heating and cooking. Imagine a giant, hidden underground river, now flowing not with gas, but with water.

### Chapter 2: Water in the Wires (and Pipes!)

As the water surged through the gas mains, it began to flow downhill, following the natural contours of the land through Stannington and Hillsborough. The consequences were immediate and alarming.

Around **midnight**, emergency services were called. They went door-to-door, waking residents, not because of a fire, but because water was starting to overflow. Inside homes, water was bubbling out of gas meters and even from gas stoves! Outdoors, manhole covers were lifting, and water was seeping from the bases of streetlights. It was a surreal and unprecedented situation. **Cadent Gas**, the company responsible for the gas network, described it as something they had "never had to deal with before."

By **December 3rd**, the scale of the disaster was becoming clear. More than **1,000 properties** were without a gas supply. To make matters worse, many homes in the immediate vicinity of the burst water main also experienced reduced or no water supply for several days.

Cadent Gas engineers faced a monumental task. They couldn't just turn the gas back on; the pipes were full of water! First, they had to go to each affected property individually and **turn off the gas supply at the meter** to prevent further damage and ensure safety. This was a painstaking process. More than **100 engineers** were drafted in, working 24 hours a day, a number that soon swelled to over 200.

### Chapter 3: The Deep Freeze and the Major Incident

As the days passed, the situation worsened. By **December 6th**, the number of properties without gas had risen to **over 2,000**, extending further down the hillsides into Hillsborough. The initial heavy rainfall that accompanied the burst main turned into bitterly cold temperatures and even snowfall. Temperatures plummeted, reaching as low as **-3°C (27°F)** on December 9th.

With no central heating, residents were struggling. They relied on electric heaters, which put a massive strain on the local electricity network. **Northern Powergrid**, the electricity supplier, had to advise residents to use heaters sparingly to avoid complete power outages. Despite these warnings, some streets in Stannington began to experience intermittent power cuts.

The severity of the situation led the **Sheffield City Council** to declare a **major incident on December 7th**. This declaration was crucial because it allowed local authorities to better coordinate the massive response needed. At this point, only about a quarter of the affected properties had had their gas supplies reconnected. Cadent Gas engineers, despite their tireless efforts, were battling to pump vast quantities of water out of a complex and extensive underground network. Equipment and engineers were brought in from across the country to assist.

### Chapter 4: The Long Road to Recovery

The outage was a test of resilience for the community. Local businesses and authorities stepped up. Refuge spaces were opened, offering warmth, hot food, and drinks. Lomas Hall became a central hub, providing portable electric heaters and hotplates. The Peacock Inn and Crown & Glove pubs offered food, drinks, and even showering facilities. Schools remained open, using electric heaters and advising students to dress warmly.

By **December 10th**, Cadent Gas reported that around three-quarters of affected properties had been reconnected. However, significant challenges remained in the Hillsborough and Malin Bridge areas, where hundreds of homes were still without gas. The process of draining water from such a vast and intricate network was incredibly difficult.

The outage, which started on **December 2nd**, dragged on for almost two weeks for some properties. While many were reconnected sooner, some residents endured the cold and inconvenience until around **December 16th**, marking a nearly **two-week period without gas**.

### Chapter 5: Lessons Learned and Lasting Impact

The Sheffield gas outage was a stark reminder of the interconnectedness of our infrastructure. A single point of failure in one system – a burst water main – led to a cascading crisis in another essential service.

**What caused the gas supply outage?**
The primary cause was a **burst water main** on the Yorkshire Water network, specifically an asbestos-cement pipe from 1970 on Bankfield Lane in Stannington. This burst allowed **more than 2 million litres of water to flood into the Cadent Gas supply network**.

**How long did the outage last?**
The outage began on **December 2nd, 2022**. While many properties had their gas reconnected gradually, some homes, particularly in areas like Hillsborough and Malin Bridge, were without a gas supply for **almost two weeks**, with full restoration for all properties occurring around **December 16th**.

The incident highlighted the importance of infrastructure maintenance, emergency preparedness, and community spirit. While Yorkshire Water faced criticism for the burst main, Cadent Gas and Northern Powergrid were largely praised for their rapid and dedicated response in a truly unprecedented situation, working tirelessly to bring warmth and light back to the homes of Sheffield.

contexts:
The city of Sheffield, England was impacted by a major failure of the local natural gas supply network in December 2022, resulting in a loss of central heating and gas stove availability to more than 3,000 properties in the northwestern suburbs of the city. The outage, which has predominantly affected the Hillsborough, Malin Bridge and Stannington districts, was declared a major incident by Sheffield City Council; some properties were without a gas supply for almost two weeks.
The gas supply outage affected the Cadent Gas network, and was caused by a burst water main on the Yorkshire Water network which resulted in more than 2 million litres of water flooding into the gas supply network. Yorkshire Water confirmed that the breach to the water main had been resolved by 6 December. In addition to the widespread gas supply outage, numerous properties in the affected areas have also suffered from outages to their water and electricity supplies as knock-on effects.Heavy rainfall initially hampered recovery work, followed by cold temperatures and snowfall. In response to the widespread lack of heating availability and increasingly cold temperatures, dropping as low as −3 °C (27 °F) on 9 December, a major incident was declared by local authorities. The Red Cross distributed aid, including food, drinks and blankets, to residents in the affected area.

Timeline
During the evening of 2 December, a water main on Bankfield Lane at the western end of Stannington burst, resulting in flooding in the local area. The affected water main was an asbestos-cement mainline pipe installed in 1970. More than 2 million litres of water, roughly equivalent to three Olympic-sized swimming pools, entered the gas mains in this area and subsequently flowed through pipes down hillsides throughout the Stannington and Hillsborough areas.Property damage was reported in dozens of homes across the affected area, including on High Matlock Road, as water overflowed out of gas meters and gas stoves inside homes; water also overflowed out of manhole covers and the bases of street lights in outdoor areas. Emergency services attended the incident from around midnight, going from door to door to wake residents. Cadent Gas, who operate the natural gas network in the area, described the incident as "unpredecented" and something which they had never had to deal with before.By 3 December more than 1,000 properties were without a gas supply; in addition, many properties in the immediate area of the burst water main also suffered from reduced water supplies, or no water at all, for several days. Engineers from Cadent Gas initially had to go from door to door and turn off the gas supply at each individual affected property, before engineers could commence work to drain and repair the gas network; more than 100 engineers were drafted in to work 24 hours a day to resolve the outage, later rising to more than 200 as the incident progressed.The number of properties affected by the gas supply outage rose to more than 2,000 by 6 December, increasingly affecting homes lower down the hillside in the Hillsborough area of Sheffield. Local electricity network operator Northern Powergrid warned local residents to only use portable electric heaters in occupied rooms and only while residents were at home, in order to reduce strain on the local power supply caused by increased usage of electric heating. Despite this however, residents on some streets in Stannington began to report intermittent power outages throughout the day. Electric car owners were advised to use public charging points rather than those at their own homes.The local authority, Sheffield City Council, officially declared a major incident on 7 December, with thousands of properties still without a gas supply and temperatures forecast to drop below freezing for prolonged periods in the coming days. Only around a quarter of affected properties had had their gas supplies reconnected at the time that the major incident was declared, according to Cadent Gas, as their engineers were struggling to pump the large quantities of water out of the complex local gas network; engineers and equipment were shipped in from across the country to assist in draining the network.According to Cadent Gas, around three-quarters of affected properties had been reconnected to the gas network by 10 December. Considerable difficulties remained in draining water from the gas network in the Hillsborough and Malin Bridge areas, where hundreds of homes still remained without gas.

Response
Refuge spaces were opened officially by the local authorities and unofficially by local businesses, providing warm spaces, hot food and drinks to affected residents. The primary official refuge was opened at Lomas Hall, a church hall on Church Street in Stannington, where residents were issued with portable electric heaters and electric hotplates for cooking. ## The Silent Flood: Sheffield's Gas Crisis of 2022

The air was crisp, the scent of impending winter hung heavy, and the festive season was just around the corner in Sheffield, December 2022. But for thousands of residents in the northwestern suburbs, particularly Hillsborough, Malin Bridge, and Stannington, the usual warmth of their homes was about to be replaced by a chilling silence. This is the story of the "Silent Flood," a major gas supply outage that plunged parts of Sheffield into a cold, dark two weeks.

### Chapter 1: The Unseen Enemy Beneath

Our story begins on the evening of **December 2nd, 2022**. Picture Bankfield Lane in Stannington, a quiet street like many others. Deep beneath the surface, an old **asbestos-cement mainline pipe**, installed all the way back in 1970, was silently battling an internal struggle. This pipe, part of the **Yorkshire Water network**, was designed to carry clean drinking water to homes.

Suddenly, with a groan that no one above ground could hear, the pipe gave way. It **burst**. This wasn't a small leak; it was a catastrophic failure. More than **2 million litres of water** – that’s enough to fill three Olympic-sized swimming pools – began to gush out.

Now, here's where the problem became truly unique and devastating. This gushing water didn't just flood the street. It found its way into the **Cadent Gas network**, the intricate web of underground pipes that carries natural gas to homes for heating and cooking. Imagine a giant, hidden underground river, now flowing not with gas, but with water.

### Chapter 2: Water in the Wires (and Pipes!)

As the water surged through the gas mains, it began to flow downhill, following the natural contours of the land through Stannington and Hillsborough. The consequences were immediate and alarming.

Around **midnight**, emergency services were called. They went door-to-door, waking residents, not because of a fire, but because water was starting to overflow. Inside homes, water was bubbling out of gas meters and even from gas stoves! Outdoors, manhole covers were lifting, and water was seeping from the bases of streetlights. It was a surreal and unprecedented situation. **Cadent Gas**, the company responsible for the gas network, described it as something they had "never had to deal with before."

By **December 3rd**, the scale of the disaster was becoming clear. More than **1,000 properties** were without a gas supply. To make matters worse, many homes in the immediate vicinity of the burst water main also experienced reduced or no water supply for several days.

Cadent Gas engineers faced a monumental task. They couldn't just turn the gas back on; the pipes were full of water! First, they had to go to each affected property individually and **turn off the gas supply at the meter** to prevent further damage and ensure safety. This was a painstaking process. More than **100 engineers** were drafted in, working 24 hours a day, a number that soon swelled to over 200.

### Chapter 3: The Deep Freeze and the Major Incident

As the days passed, the situation worsened. By **December 6th**, the number of properties without gas had risen to **over 2,000**, extending further down the hillsides into Hillsborough. The initial heavy rainfall that accompanied the burst main turned into bitterly cold temperatures and even snowfall. Temperatures plummeted, reaching as low as **-3°C (27°F)** on December 9th.

With no central heating, residents were struggling. They relied on electric heaters, which put a massive strain on the local electricity network. **Northern Powergrid**, the electricity supplier, had to advise residents to use heaters sparingly to avoid complete power outages. Despite these warnings, some streets in Stannington began to experience intermittent power cuts.

The severity of the situation led the **Sheffield City Council** to declare a **major incident on December 7th**. This declaration was crucial because it allowed local authorities to better coordinate the massive response needed. At this point, only about a quarter of the affected properties had had their gas supplies reconnected. Cadent Gas engineers, despite their tireless efforts, were battling to pump vast quantities of water out of a complex and extensive underground network. Equipment and engineers were brought in from across the country to assist.

### Chapter 4: The Long Road to Recovery

The outage was a test of resilience for the community. Local businesses and authorities stepped up. Refuge spaces were opened, offering warmth, hot food, and drinks. Lomas Hall became a central hub, providing portable electric heaters and hotplates. The Peacock Inn and Crown & Glove pubs offered food, drinks, and even showering facilities. Schools remained open, using electric heaters and advising students to dress warmly.

By **December 10th**, Cadent Gas reported that around three-quarters of affected properties had been reconnected. However, significant challenges remained in the Hillsborough and Malin Bridge areas, where hundreds of homes were still without gas. The process of draining water from such a vast and intricate network was incredibly difficult.

The outage, which started on **December 2nd**, dragged on for almost two weeks for some properties. While many were reconnected sooner, some residents endured the cold and inconvenience until around **December 16th**, marking a nearly **two-week period without gas**.

### Chapter 5: Lessons Learned and Lasting Impact

The Sheffield gas outage was a stark reminder of the interconnectedness of our infrastructure. A single point of failure in one system – a burst water main – led to a cascading crisis in another essential service.

**What caused the gas supply outage?**
The primary cause was a **burst water main** on the Yorkshire Water network, specifically an asbestos-cement pipe from 1970 on Bankfield Lane in Stannington. This burst allowed **more than 2 million litres of water to flood into the Cadent Gas supply network**.

**How long did the outage last?**
The outage began on **December 2nd, 2022**. While many properties had their gas reconnected gradually, some homes, particularly in areas like Hillsborough and Malin Bridge, were without a gas supply for **almost two weeks**, with full restoration for all properties occurring around **December 16th**.

The incident highlighted the importance of infrastructure maintenance, emergency preparedness, and community spirit. While Yorkshire Water faced criticism for the burst main, Cadent Gas and Northern Powergrid were largely praised for their rapid and dedicated response in a truly unprecedented situation, working tirelessly to bring warmth and light back to the homes of Sheffield.

## Petualangan Melintasi Batas Pengetahuan: Kisah GPT-4

Di sebuah kelas futuristik yang dipenuhi cahaya holografik, duduklah sekelompok siswa SMA yang sedang mendengarkan penjelasan Bu Rina, guru AI mereka. Hari ini, topik mereka adalah sesuatu yang sedang hangat dibicarakan di dunia teknologi: GPT-4.

"Anak-anak," Bu Rina memulai dengan senyum, "kita akan menyelami salah satu inovasi paling menarik di dunia kecerdasan buatan. Mungkin kalian sudah familiar dengan ChatGPT, kan?"

Siswa-siswa mengangguk. Beberapa bahkan mengangkat tangan, ingin berbagi pengalaman mereka menggunakan ChatGPT untuk tugas sekolah atau sekadar bersenang-senang.

"Nah, bayangkan ChatGPT itu seperti mobil sport yang cepat dan cerdas," lanjut Bu Rina. "Sekarang, bayangkan ada versi terbarunya, yang jauh lebih kuat, lebih pintar, dan bisa melakukan hal-hal yang sebelumnya tidak kita duga. Itulah GPT-4!"

"Kapan GPT-4 dirilis, Bu?" tanya Rio, seorang siswa yang selalu ingin tahu.

Bu Rina menekan tombol pada papan tulis holografiknya, dan sebuah tanggal besar muncul: **14 Maret 2023**.

"Tepat pada tanggal 14 Maret 2023, OpenAI, perusahaan di balik semua ini, meluncurkan GPT-4. Awalnya, ia tersedia dalam bentuk terbatas melalui ChatGPT Plus, versi premium dari ChatGPT yang kalian kenal, dan juga melalui API untuk para pengembang yang mendaftar di daftar tunggu. Ini seperti peluncuran roket baru; tidak semua orang bisa langsung menaikinya, tapi dampaknya terasa ke seluruh dunia."

"Jadi, apa bedanya dengan versi sebelumnya, Bu?" tanya Sarah, yang lebih tertarik pada kemampuan praktisnya. "Apakah hanya lebih cepat?"

"Itu pertanyaan bagus, Sarah!" kata Bu Rina. "Perbedaannya sangat signifikan. Ingat, GPT-4 adalah penerus dari model-model sebelumnya: GPT-1 di tahun 2018, GPT-2 di tahun 2019, dan GPT-3 di tahun 2020, yang kemudian disempurnakan menjadi GPT-3.5 yang menjadi dasar ChatGPT. Setiap versi adalah lompatan besar, dan GPT-4 ini adalah lompatan yang sangat besar."

Bu Rina menampilkan beberapa poin penting tentang kemampuan GPT-4:

### Kemampuan Luar Biasa GPT-4:

1.  **Lebih Andal, Kreatif, dan Paham Instruksi Rumit:**
    "OpenAI sendiri mengatakan bahwa GPT-4 'lebih andal, kreatif, dan mampu menangani instruksi yang jauh lebih bernuansa daripada GPT-3.5'. Bayangkan kalian memberi instruksi pada asisten AI kalian, dan dia tidak hanya memahaminya dengan baik, tapi juga bisa memberikan hasil yang lebih imajinatif dan sesuai konteks yang sangat spesifik."

2.  **Jendela Konteks yang Jauh Lebih Besar:**
    "Salah satu peningkatan paling penting adalah 'jendela konteks'-nya. Ini seperti memori jangka pendek model tersebut. GPT-3.5 hanya bisa mengingat sekitar 4.096 'token' (kata atau bagian kata). GPT-4 punya dua versi, dengan jendela konteks 8.192 atau bahkan 32.768 token! Ini berarti dia bisa memproses dan memahami informasi dari teks yang jauh lebih panjang, seperti seluruh bab buku atau dokumen hukum yang rumit, tanpa kehilangan jejak."

3.  **Model Multimodal: Melihat dan Memahami Gambar!**
    "Ini adalah terobosan besar! Berbeda dengan pendahulunya yang hanya bisa menerima teks, GPT-4 adalah model 'multimodal'. Artinya, ia bisa menerima **gambar dan teks sebagai input**. Bayangkan ini: kalian bisa mengunggah meme dan meminta GPT-4 menjelaskan mengapa meme itu lucu, atau mengunggah tangkapan layar dari grafik dan memintanya meringkas informasi di dalamnya. Bahkan, ia bisa menjawab soal ujian yang berisi diagram!"

    Bu Rina menampilkan contoh di mana GPT-4 berhasil menjelaskan humor dari gambar aneh dan meringkas teks dari screenshot.

4.  **Pesan Sistem untuk Kendali yang Lebih Baik:**
    "OpenAI juga memperkenalkan 'pesan sistem' baru. Ini seperti memberi instruksi awal kepada GPT-4 tentang 'persona' atau 'tugas' apa yang harus diembannya. Misalnya, kalian bisa menyuruhnya, 'Bertindaklah seperti bajak laut Shakespearean,' dan semua jawabannya akan keluar dalam prosa berima ala Shakespeare. Atau, 'Selalu berikan jawabanmu dalam format JSON,' dan dia akan melakukannya. Ini memberi kita kendali yang luar biasa atas bagaimana model itu berinteraksi."

5.  **Berinteraksi dengan Antarmuka Eksternal:**
    "GPT-4 tidak hanya terpaku pada apa yang sudah ada di dalam 'otaknya'. Jika diinstruksikan, ia bisa berinteraksi dengan antarmuka eksternal. Misalnya, kalian bisa memintanya melakukan pencarian web untuk mendapatkan informasi terbaru, dan hasilnya akan dimasukkan ke dalam responsnya. Ini membuka pintu untuk melakukan banyak hal di luar prediksi teks biasa, seperti menggunakan API lain, menghasilkan gambar, atau mengakses dan meringkas halaman web."

6.  **Asisten Coding yang Canggih:**
    "Bagi kalian yang tertarik dengan pemrograman, GPT-4 adalah alat yang luar biasa. Para programmer menemukan bahwa ia sangat membantu dalam tugas coding, seperti menemukan kesalahan dalam kode yang sudah ada atau menyarankan optimasi untuk meningkatkan kinerja. Seorang biofisikawan bahkan mengatakan bahwa waktu yang dibutuhkan untuk memindahkan program dari MATLAB ke Python berkurang dari berhari-hari menjadi 'sekitar satu jam' berkat GPT-4!"

7.  **Lulus Ujian Standar dengan Nilai Tinggi:**
    "GPT-4 menunjukkan kemampuan luar biasa dalam berbagai ujian standar. Dalam pengujian OpenAI sendiri, model ini mendapatkan skor 1410 pada SAT (persentil ke-94), 163 pada LSAT (persentil ke-88), dan 298 pada Ujian Bar Seragam (persentil ke-90). Bandingkan dengan GPT-3.5 yang jauh di bawahnya. Ia bahkan lulus ujian onkologi, teknik, dan bedah plastik!"

8.  **Aplikasi Medis Revolusioner:**
    "Para peneliti dari Microsoft menguji GPT-4 pada masalah medis dan menemukan bahwa tanpa perlu instruksi khusus, ia melampaui nilai kelulusan USMLE (ujian lisensi dokter di AS) dengan lebih dari 20 poin! Ini menunjukkan potensi besar GPT-4 dalam membantu profesional medis, seperti dalam menjawab pertanyaan pasien dan menganalisis rekam medis, seperti yang diumumkan oleh Microsoft dan Epic Systems."

"Wow, itu gila!" seru Dani, ternganga. "Jadi, GPT-4 itu seperti ensiklopedia berjalan yang bisa melihat dan berbicara?"

"Kurang lebih begitu, Dani," Bu Rina tersenyum. "Tapi, penting untuk diingat bahwa ia juga punya keterbatasan."

### Keterbatasan GPT-4:

1.  **Halusinasi:**
    "Seperti pendahulunya, GPT-4 bisa 'berhalusinasi'. Artinya, ia bisa menghasilkan informasi yang tidak ada dalam data pelatihannya atau bahkan bertentangan dengan instruksi kalian. Jadi, jangan langsung percaya semua yang dikatakannya tanpa verifikasi, terutama untuk informasi penting."

2.  **Kurangnya Transparansi:**
    "Kita tidak tahu persis bagaimana ia membuat keputusan. Meskipun ia bisa memberikan penjelasan, penjelasan itu seringkali dibuat 'setelah kejadian' dan tidak selalu mencerminkan proses sebenarnya. Terkadang, penjelasannya bahkan bertentangan dengan pernyataan sebelumnya."

3.  **Bias yang Tersembunyi:**
    "Karena dilatih dengan data dari internet, ia bisa saja memiliki bias yang sama dengan data tersebut. OpenAI sudah berusaha menguranginya dengan 'reinforcement learning from human feedback' untuk menolak permintaan yang berbahaya, tapi beberapa bias kognitif seperti bias konfirmasi masih bisa muncul."

"Jadi, meskipun sangat pintar, kita tetap harus kritis ya, Bu?" tanya Rizal.

"Tepat sekali, Rizal," jawab Bu Rina. "Kecerdasan buatan adalah alat yang sangat kuat, dan seperti semua alat, penggunaannya membutuhkan pemahaman dan tanggung jawab. GPT-4 adalah bukti betapa jauhnya kita telah melangkah dalam AI, tapi juga pengingat bahwa manusia tetap menjadi penentu arah dan pemverifikasi kebenaran."

Siswa-siswa itu tampak terinspirasi. Mereka mulai membayangkan bagaimana teknologi seperti GPT-4 akan mengubah dunia di masa depan, dan bagaimana mereka bisa menjadi bagian dari perubahan itu.

"Ingat," Bu Rina menyimpulkan, "GPT-4 adalah lompatan besar. Ia menunjukkan masa depan di mana AI bisa menjadi kolaborator yang luar biasa dalam berbagai bidang, dari pendidikan hingga kedokteran. Tapi, dengan kekuatan besar datanglah tanggung jawab besar. Mari kita gunakan teknologi ini dengan bijak dan kreatif!"

Dan dengan itu, bel berbunyi, mengakhiri pelajaran tentang GPT-4, namun membuka pintu bagi pemikiran dan imajinasi baru di benak para siswa.

2.  **Jendela Konteks yang Jauh Lebih Besar:**
    "Salah satu peningkatan paling penting adalah 'jendela konteks'-nya. Ini seperti memori jangka pendek model tersebut. GPT-3.5 hanya bisa mengingat sekitar 4.096 'token' (kata atau bagian kata). 3.  **Model Multimodal: Melihat dan Memahami Gambar!**

Unlike the predecessors, GPT-4 can take images as well as text as input. OpenAI has declined to reveal technical information such as the size of the GPT-4 model.

In 2020, they introduced GPT-3, a model with 100 times as many parameters as GPT-2, that could perform various tasks with few examples. GPT-3 was further improved into GPT-3.5, which was used to create the chatbot product ChatGPT. 
Rumors claim that GPT-4 has 1.76 trillion parameters, which was first estimated by the speed it was running and by George Hotz.

Capabilities
OpenAI stated that GPT-4 is "more reliable, creative, and able to handle much more nuanced instructions than GPT-3.5." They produced two versions of GPT-4, with context windows of 8,192 and 32,768 tokens, a significant improvement over GPT-3.5 and GPT-3, which were limited to 4,096 and 2,049 tokens respectively. Some of the capabilities of GPT-4 were predicted by OpenAI before training it, although other capabilities remained hard to predict due to breaks in downstream scaling laws. Unlike its predecessors, GPT-4 is a multimodal model: it can take images as well as text as input; this gives it the ability to describe the humor in unusual images, summarize text from screenshots, and answer exam questions that contain diagrams.To gain further control over GPT-4, OpenAI introduced the "system message", a directive in natural language given to GPT-4 in order to specify its tone of voice and task. For example, the system message can instruct the model to "be a Shakespearean pirate", in which case it will respond in rhyming, Shakespearean prose, or request it to "always write the output of [its] response in JSON", in which case the model will do so, adding keys and values as it sees fit to match the structure of its reply. In the examples provided by OpenAI, GPT-4 refused to deviate from its system message despite requests to do otherwise by the user during the conversation.When instructed to do so, GPT-4 can interact with external interfaces. GPT-4 demonstrates aptitude on several standardized tests. In contrast, OpenAI claims that GPT-3.5 received scores for the same exams in the 82nd, 40th, and 10th percentiles, respectively.

In many cases, when asked to explain its logic, GPT-4 will give explanations that directly contradict its previous statements.

Bias
GPT-4 was trained in two stages. First, the model was given large datasets of text taken from the internet and trained to predict the next token (roughly corresponding to a word) in those datasets. ## Petualangan Melintasi Batas Pengetahuan: Kisah GPT-4

Di sebuah kelas futuristik yang dipenuhi cahaya holografik, duduklah sekelompok siswa SMA yang sedang mendengarkan penjelasan Bu Rina, guru AI mereka. Hari ini, topik mereka adalah sesuatu yang sedang hangat dibicarakan di dunia teknologi: GPT-4.

"Anak-anak," Bu Rina memulai dengan senyum, "kita akan menyelami salah satu inovasi paling menarik di dunia kecerdasan buatan. Mungkin kalian sudah familiar dengan ChatGPT, kan?"

Siswa-siswa mengangguk. Beberapa bahkan mengangkat tangan, ingin berbagi pengalaman mereka menggunakan ChatGPT untuk tugas sekolah atau sekadar bersenang-senang.

"Nah, bayangkan ChatGPT itu seperti mobil sport yang cepat dan cerdas," lanjut Bu Rina. "Sekarang, bayangkan ada versi terbarunya, yang jauh lebih kuat, lebih pintar, dan bisa melakukan hal-hal yang sebelumnya tidak kita duga. Itulah GPT-4!"

"Kapan GPT-4 dirilis, Bu?" tanya Rio, seorang siswa yang selalu ingin tahu.

Bu Rina menekan tombol pada papan tulis holografiknya, dan sebuah tanggal besar muncul: **14 Maret 2023**.

"Tepat pada tanggal 14 Maret 2023, OpenAI, perusahaan di balik semua ini, meluncurkan GPT-4. Awalnya, ia tersedia dalam bentuk terbatas melalui ChatGPT Plus, versi premium dari ChatGPT yang kalian kenal, dan juga melalui API untuk para pengembang yang mendaftar di daftar tunggu. "Jadi, apa bedanya dengan versi sebelumnya, Bu?" tanya Sarah, yang lebih tertarik pada kemampuan praktisnya. "Apakah hanya lebih cepat?"

"Itu pertanyaan bagus, Sarah!" kata Bu Rina. "Perbedaannya sangat signifikan. ### Kemampuan Luar Biasa GPT-4:

1.  **Lebih Andal, Kreatif, dan Paham Instruksi Rumit:**
    "OpenAI sendiri mengatakan bahwa GPT-4 'lebih andal, kreatif, dan mampu menangani instruksi yang jauh lebih bernuansa daripada GPT-3.5'. Bayangkan kalian memberi instruksi pada asisten AI kalian, dan dia tidak hanya memahaminya dengan baik, tapi juga bisa memberikan hasil yang lebih imajinatif dan sesuai konteks yang sangat spesifik."

2.  **Jendela Konteks yang Jauh Lebih Besar:**
    "Salah satu peningkatan paling penting adalah 'jendela konteks'-nya. Ini seperti memori jangka pendek model tersebut. GPT-3.5 hanya bisa mengingat sekitar 4.096 'token' (kata atau bagian kata). GPT-4 punya dua versi, dengan jendela konteks 8.192 atau bahkan 32.768 token! Ini berarti dia bisa memproses dan memahami informasi dari teks yang jauh lebih panjang, seperti seluruh bab buku atau dokumen hukum yang rumit, tanpa kehilangan jejak."

3.  **Model Multimodal: Melihat dan Memahami Gambar!**
    "Ini adalah terobosan besar! Berbeda dengan pendahulunya yang hanya bisa menerima teks, GPT-4 adalah model 'multimodal'. Artinya, ia bisa menerima **gambar dan teks sebagai input**. Bayangkan ini: kalian bisa mengunggah meme dan meminta GPT-4 menjelaskan mengapa meme itu lucu, atau mengunggah tangkapan layar dari grafik dan memintanya meringkas informasi di dalamnya. Bahkan, ia bisa menjawab soal ujian yang berisi diagram!"

    Bu Rina menampilkan contoh di mana GPT-4 berhasil menjelaskan humor dari gambar aneh dan meringkas teks dari screenshot.

4.  **Pesan Sistem untuk Kendali yang Lebih Baik:**
    "OpenAI juga memperkenalkan 'pesan sistem' baru. Ini seperti memberi instruksi awal kepada GPT-4 tentang 'persona' atau 'tugas' apa yang harus diembannya. Atau, 'Selalu berikan jawabanmu dalam format JSON,' dan dia akan melakukannya. Ini memberi kita kendali yang luar biasa atas bagaimana model itu berinteraksi."

5.  **Berinteraksi dengan Antarmuka Eksternal:**
    "GPT-4 tidak hanya terpaku pada apa yang sudah ada di dalam 'otaknya'. Jika diinstruksikan, ia bisa berinteraksi dengan antarmuka eksternal. Misalnya, kalian bisa memintanya melakukan pencarian web untuk mendapatkan informasi terbaru, dan hasilnya akan dimasukkan ke dalam responsnya. Ini membuka pintu untuk melakukan banyak hal di luar prediksi teks biasa, seperti menggunakan API lain, menghasilkan gambar, atau mengakses dan meringkas halaman web."

6.  **Asisten Coding yang Canggih:**
    "Bagi kalian yang tertarik dengan pemrograman, GPT-4 adalah alat yang luar biasa. Para programmer menemukan bahwa ia sangat membantu dalam tugas coding, seperti menemukan kesalahan dalam kode yang sudah ada atau menyarankan optimasi untuk meningkatkan kinerja. Seorang biofisikawan bahkan mengatakan bahwa waktu yang dibutuhkan untuk memindahkan program dari MATLAB ke Python berkurang dari berhari-hari menjadi 'sekitar satu jam' berkat GPT-4!"

7.  **Lulus Ujian Standar dengan Nilai Tinggi:**
    "GPT-4 menunjukkan kemampuan luar biasa dalam berbagai ujian standar. Dalam pengujian OpenAI sendiri, model ini mendapatkan skor 1410 pada SAT (persentil ke-94), 163 pada LSAT (persentil ke-88), dan 298 pada Ujian Bar Seragam (persentil ke-90). Bandingkan dengan GPT-3.5 yang jauh di bawahnya. Ia bahkan lulus ujian onkologi, teknik, dan bedah plastik!"

8.  **Aplikasi Medis Revolusioner:**
    "Para peneliti dari Microsoft menguji GPT-4 pada masalah medis dan menemukan bahwa tanpa perlu instruksi khusus, ia melampaui nilai kelulusan USMLE (ujian lisensi dokter di AS) dengan lebih dari 20 poin! Ini menunjukkan potensi besar GPT-4 dalam membantu profesional medis, seperti dalam menjawab pertanyaan pasien dan menganalisis rekam medis, seperti yang diumumkan oleh Microsoft dan Epic Systems."

"Wow, itu gila!" seru Dani, ternganga. "Jadi, GPT-4 itu seperti ensiklopedia berjalan yang bisa melihat dan berbicara?"

"Kurang lebih begitu, Dani," Bu Rina tersenyum. "Tapi, penting untuk diingat bahwa ia juga punya keterbatasan."

### Keterbatasan GPT-4:

1.  **Halusinasi:**
    "Seperti pendahulunya, GPT-4 bisa 'berhalusinasi'. Artinya, ia bisa menghasilkan informasi yang tidak ada dalam data pelatihannya atau bahkan bertentangan dengan instruksi kalian. Jadi, jangan langsung percaya semua yang dikatakannya tanpa verifikasi, terutama untuk informasi penting."

2.  **Kurangnya Transparansi:**
    "Kita tidak tahu persis bagaimana ia membuat keputusan. Meskipun ia bisa memberikan penjelasan, penjelasan itu seringkali dibuat 'setelah kejadian' dan tidak selalu mencerminkan proses sebenarnya. Terkadang, penjelasannya bahkan bertentangan dengan pernyataan sebelumnya."

3.  **Bias yang Tersembunyi:**
    "Karena dilatih dengan data dari internet, ia bisa saja memiliki bias yang sama dengan data tersebut. OpenAI sudah berusaha menguranginya dengan 'reinforcement learning from human feedback' untuk menolak permintaan yang berbahaya, tapi beberapa bias kognitif seperti bias konfirmasi masih bisa muncul."

"Jadi, meskipun sangat pintar, kita tetap harus kritis ya, Bu?" tanya Rizal.

"Tepat sekali, Rizal," jawab Bu Rina. "Kecerdasan buatan adalah alat yang sangat kuat, dan seperti semua alat, penggunaannya membutuhkan pemahaman dan tanggung jawab. GPT-4 adalah bukti betapa jauhnya kita telah melangkah dalam AI, tapi juga pengingat bahwa manusia tetap menjadi penentu arah dan pemverifikasi kebenaran."

Siswa-siswa itu tampak terinspirasi. Mereka mulai membayangkan bagaimana teknologi seperti GPT-4 akan mengubah dunia di masa depan, dan bagaimana mereka bisa menjadi bagian dari perubahan itu.

"Ingat," Bu Rina menyimpulkan, "GPT-4 adalah lompatan besar. Ia menunjukkan masa depan di mana AI bisa menjadi kolaborator yang luar biasa dalam berbagai bidang, dari pendidikan hingga kedokteran. Tapi, dengan kekuatan besar datanglah tanggung jawab besar. Mari kita gunakan teknologi ini dengan bijak dan kreatif!"

Dan dengan itu, bel berbunyi, mengakhiri pelajaran tentang GPT-4, namun membuka pintu bagi pemikiran dan imajinasi baru di benak para siswa.

Generative Pre-trained Transformer 4 (GPT-4) is a multimodal large language model created by OpenAI, and the fourth in its numbered "GPT-n" series of GPT foundation models. It was released on March 14, 2023, and has been made publicly available in a limited form via the chatbot product ChatGPT Plus (a premium version of ChatGPT), and with access to the GPT-4 based version of OpenAI's API being provided via a waitlist. As a transformer based model, GPT-4 was pretrained to predict the next token (using both public data and "data licensed from third-party providers"), and was then fine-tuned with reinforcement learning from human and AI feedback for human alignment and policy compliance.: 2 Observers reported the GPT-4 based version of ChatGPT to be an improvement on the previous (GPT-3.5 based) ChatGPT, with the caveat that GPT-4 retains some of the same problems. Unlike the predecessors, GPT-4 can take images as well as text as input. OpenAI has declined to reveal technical information such as the size of the GPT-4 model.

Background
OpenAI introduced the first GPT model (GPT-1) in 2018, publishing a paper called "Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training." It was based on the transformer architecture and trained on a large corpus of books. The next year, they introduced GPT-2, a larger model that could generate coherent text. In 2020, they introduced GPT-3, a model with 100 times as many parameters as GPT-2, that could perform various tasks with few examples. GPT-3 was further improved into GPT-3.5, which was used to create the chatbot product ChatGPT. 
Rumors claim that GPT-4 has 1.76 trillion parameters, which was first estimated by the speed it was running and by George Hotz.

Capabilities
OpenAI stated that GPT-4 is "more reliable, creative, and able to handle much more nuanced instructions than GPT-3.5." They produced two versions of GPT-4, with context windows of 8,192 and 32,768 tokens, a significant improvement over GPT-3.5 and GPT-3, which were limited to 4,096 and 2,049 tokens respectively. Some of the capabilities of GPT-4 were predicted by OpenAI before training it, although other capabilities remained hard to predict due to breaks in downstream scaling laws. Unlike its predecessors, GPT-4 is a multimodal model: it can take images as well as text as input; this gives it the ability to describe the humor in unusual images, summarize text from screenshots, and answer exam questions that contain diagrams.To gain further control over GPT-4, OpenAI introduced the "system message", a directive in natural language given to GPT-4 in order to specify its tone of voice and task. For example, the system message can instruct the model to "be a Shakespearean pirate", in which case it will respond in rhyming, Shakespearean prose, or request it to "always write the output of [its] response in JSON", in which case the model will do so, adding keys and values as it sees fit to match the structure of its reply. In the examples provided by OpenAI, GPT-4 refused to deviate from its system message despite requests to do otherwise by the user during the conversation.When instructed to do so, GPT-4 can interact with external interfaces. For example, the model could be instructed to enclose a query within <search></search> tags to perform a web search, the result of which would be inserted into the model's prompt to allow it to form a response. This allows the model to perform tasks beyond its normal text-prediction capabilities, such as using APIs, generating images, and accessing and summarizing webpages.A 2023 article in Nature stated programmers have found GPT-4 useful for assisting in coding tasks (despite its propensity for error), such as finding errors in existing code and suggesting optimizations to improve performance. The article quoted a biophysicist who found that the time he required to port one of his programs from MATLAB to Python went down from days to "an hour or so". On a test of 89 security scenarios, GPT-4 produced code vulnerable to SQL injection attacks 5% of the time, an improvement over Github Copilot from the year 2021, which produced vulnerabilities 40% of the time.

Aptitude on standardized tests
GPT-4 demonstrates aptitude on several standardized tests. OpenAI claims that in their own testing the model received a score of 1410 on the SAT (94th percentile), 163 on the LSAT (88th percentile), and 298 on the Uniform Bar Exam (90th percentile). In contrast, OpenAI claims that GPT-3.5 received scores for the same exams in the 82nd, 40th, and 10th percentiles, respectively.
GPT-4 also passed an oncology exam, an engineering exam and a plastic surgery exam.

Medical applications
Researchers from Microsoft tested GPT-4 on medical problems and found "that GPT-4, without any specialized prompt crafting, exceeds the passing score on USMLE by over 20 points and outperforms earlier general-purpose models (GPT-3.5) as well as models specifically fine-tuned on medical knowledge (Med-PaLM, a prompt-tuned version of Flan-PaLM 540B)".A report by Microsoft has found that GPT-4 may act unreliably when used in the medical field. In their test example, GPT-4 added fabricated details to a patient's notes.In April 2023, Microsoft and Epic Systems announced that they will provide healthcare providers with GPT-4 powered systems for assisting in responding to questions from patients and analysing medical records.

Limitations
Like its predecessors, GPT-4 has been known to hallucinate, meaning that the outputs may include information not in the training data or that contradicts the user's prompt.GPT-4 also lacks transparency in its decision-making processes. If requested, the model is able to provide an explanation as to how and why it makes its decisions but these explanations are formed post-hoc; it's impossible to verify if those explanations truly reflect the actual process. In many cases, when asked to explain its logic, GPT-4 will give explanations that directly contradict its previous statements.

Bias
GPT-4 was trained in two stages. First, the model was given large datasets of text taken from the internet and trained to predict the next token (roughly corresponding to a word) in those datasets. Second, human reviews are used to fine-tune the system in a process called reinforcement learning from human feedback, which trains the model to refuse prompts which go against OpenAI's definition of harmful behavior, such as questions on how to perform illegal activities, advice on how to harm oneself or others, or requests for descriptions of graphic, violent, or sexual content.Microsoft researchers suggested GPT-4 may exhibit cognitive biases such as confirmation bias, anchoring, and base-rate neglect.

Training
OpenAI did not release the technical details of GPT-4; the technical report explicitly refrained from specifying the model size, architecture, or hardware used during either training or inference. While the report described that the model was trained using a combination of first supervised learning on a large dataset, then reinforcement learning using both human and AI feedback, it did not provide details of the training, including the process by which the training dataset was constructed, the computing power required, or any hyperparameters such as the learning rate, epoch count, or optimizer(s) used. The report claimed that "the competitive landscape and the safety implications of large-scale models" were factors that influenced this decision.Sam Altman stated that the cost of training GPT-4 was more than $100 million. "Anak-anak," Bu Rina memulai dengan senyum, "kita akan menyelami salah satu inovasi paling menarik di dunia kecerdasan buatan. Mungkin kalian sudah familiar dengan ChatGPT, kan?"

Siswa-siswa mengangguk. Beberapa bahkan mengangkat tangan, ingin berbagi pengalaman mereka menggunakan ChatGPT untuk tugas sekolah atau sekadar bersenang-senang.

"Nah, bayangkan ChatGPT itu seperti mobil sport yang cepat dan cerdas," lanjut Bu Rina. "Sekarang, bayangkan ada versi terbarunya, yang jauh lebih kuat, lebih pintar, dan bisa melakukan hal-hal yang sebelumnya tidak kita duga. Itulah GPT-4!"

"Kapan GPT-4 dirilis, Bu?" tanya Rio, seorang siswa yang selalu ingin tahu.

Bu Rina menekan tombol pada papan tulis holografiknya, dan sebuah tanggal besar muncul: **14 Maret 2023**.

"Tepat pada tanggal 14 Maret 2023, OpenAI, perusahaan di balik semua ini, meluncurkan GPT-4. Awalnya, ia tersedia dalam bentuk terbatas melalui ChatGPT Plus, versi premium dari ChatGPT yang kalian kenal, dan juga melalui API untuk para pengembang yang mendaftar di daftar tunggu. 2.  **Jendela Konteks yang Jauh Lebih Besar:**
    "Salah satu peningkatan paling penting adalah 'jendela konteks'-nya. Ini seperti memori jangka pendek model tersebut. GPT-3.5 hanya bisa mengingat sekitar 4.096 'token' (kata atau bagian kata). GPT-4 punya dua versi, dengan jendela konteks 8.192 atau bahkan 32.768 token! Ini berarti dia bisa memproses dan memahami informasi dari teks yang jauh lebih panjang, seperti seluruh bab buku atau dokumen hukum yang rumit, tanpa kehilangan jejak."

3.  **Model Multimodal: Melihat dan Memahami Gambar!**
    "Ini adalah terobosan besar! Berbeda dengan pendahulunya yang hanya bisa menerima teks, GPT-4 adalah model 'multimodal'. Artinya, ia bisa menerima **gambar dan teks sebagai input**. Bayangkan ini: kalian bisa mengunggah meme dan meminta GPT-4 menjelaskan mengapa meme itu lucu, atau mengunggah tangkapan layar dari grafik dan memintanya meringkas informasi di dalamnya. Bahkan, ia bisa menjawab soal ujian yang berisi diagram!"

    Bu Rina menampilkan contoh di mana GPT-4 berhasil menjelaskan humor dari gambar aneh dan meringkas teks dari screenshot.

4.  **Pesan Sistem untuk Kendali yang Lebih Baik:**

    "GPT-4 tidak hanya terpaku pada apa yang sudah ada di dalam 'otaknya'. Jika diinstruksikan, ia bisa berinteraksi dengan antarmuka eksternal. Ini membuka pintu untuk melakukan banyak hal di luar prediksi teks biasa, seperti menggunakan API lain, menghasilkan gambar, atau mengakses dan meringkas halaman web."

6.  **Asisten Coding yang Canggih:**
    "Bagi kalian yang tertarik dengan pemrograman, GPT-4 adalah alat yang luar biasa. Bandingkan dengan GPT-3.5 yang jauh di bawahnya. Ia bahkan lulus ujian onkologi, teknik, dan bedah plastik!"

    "Para peneliti dari Microsoft menguji GPT-4 pada masalah medis dan menemukan bahwa tanpa perlu instruksi khusus, ia melampaui nilai kelulusan USMLE (ujian lisensi dokter di AS) dengan lebih dari 20 poin! "Wow, itu gila!" seru Dani, ternganga. "Jadi, GPT-4 itu seperti ensiklopedia berjalan yang bisa melihat dan berbicara?"

### Keterbatasan GPT-4:

    "Seperti pendahulunya, GPT-4 bisa 'berhalusinasi'. Artinya, ia bisa menghasilkan informasi yang tidak ada dalam data pelatihannya atau bahkan bertentangan dengan instruksi kalian. Jadi, jangan langsung percaya semua yang dikatakannya tanpa verifikasi, terutama untuk informasi penting."

"Anak-anak," Bu Rina memulai dengan senyum, "kita akan menyelami salah satu inovasi paling menarik di dunia kecerdasan buatan. Mungkin kalian sudah familiar dengan ChatGPT, kan?"

Siswa-siswa mengangguk. Beberapa bahkan mengangkat tangan, ingin berbagi pengalaman mereka menggunakan ChatGPT untuk tugas sekolah atau sekadar bersenang-senang.

"Nah, bayangkan ChatGPT itu seperti mobil sport yang cepat dan cerdas," lanjut Bu Rina. "Sekarang, bayangkan ada versi terbarunya, yang jauh lebih kuat, lebih pintar, dan bisa melakukan hal-hal yang sebelumnya tidak kita duga. Itulah GPT-4!"

"Kapan GPT-4 dirilis, Bu?" tanya Rio, seorang siswa yang selalu ingin tahu.

Bu Rina menekan tombol pada papan tulis holografiknya, dan sebuah tanggal besar muncul: **14 Maret 2023**.

"Tepat pada tanggal 14 Maret 2023, OpenAI, perusahaan di balik semua ini, meluncurkan GPT-4. Awalnya, ia tersedia dalam bentuk terbatas melalui ChatGPT Plus, versi premium dari ChatGPT yang kalian kenal, dan juga melalui API untuk para pengembang yang mendaftar di daftar tunggu. Ini seperti peluncuran roket baru; tidak semua orang bisa langsung menaikinya, tapi dampaknya terasa ke seluruh dunia."

"Jadi, apa bedanya dengan versi sebelumnya, Bu?" tanya Sarah, yang lebih tertarik pada kemampuan praktisnya. "Apakah hanya lebih cepat?"

"Itu pertanyaan bagus, Sarah!" kata Bu Rina. "Perbedaannya sangat signifikan. Ingat, GPT-4 adalah penerus dari model-model sebelumnya: GPT-1 di tahun 2018, GPT-2 di tahun 2019, dan GPT-3 di tahun 2020, yang kemudian disempurnakan menjadi GPT-3.5 yang menjadi dasar ChatGPT. Setiap versi adalah lompatan besar, dan GPT-4 ini adalah lompatan yang sangat besar."

Bu Rina menampilkan beberapa poin penting tentang kemampuan GPT-4:

### Kemampuan Luar Biasa GPT-4:

1.  **Lebih Andal, Kreatif, dan Paham Instruksi Rumit:**
    "OpenAI sendiri mengatakan bahwa GPT-4 'lebih andal, kreatif, dan mampu menangani instruksi yang jauh lebih bernuansa daripada GPT-3.5'. Bayangkan kalian memberi instruksi pada asisten AI kalian, dan dia tidak hanya memahaminya dengan baik, tapi juga bisa memberikan hasil yang lebih imajinatif dan sesuai konteks yang sangat spesifik."

2.  **Jendela Konteks yang Jauh Lebih Besar:**
    "Salah satu peningkatan paling penting adalah 'jendela konteks'-nya. Ini seperti memori jangka pendek model tersebut. GPT-3.5 hanya bisa mengingat sekitar 4.096 'token' (kata atau bagian kata). GPT-4 punya dua versi, dengan jendela konteks 8.192 atau bahkan 32.768 token! Ini berarti dia bisa memproses dan memahami informasi dari teks yang jauh lebih panjang, seperti seluruh bab buku atau dokumen hukum yang rumit, tanpa kehilangan jejak."

3.  **Model Multimodal: Melihat dan Memahami Gambar!**
    "Ini adalah terobosan besar! Berbeda dengan pendahulunya yang hanya bisa menerima teks, GPT-4 adalah model 'multimodal'. Artinya, ia bisa menerima **gambar dan teks sebagai input**. Bayangkan ini: kalian bisa mengunggah meme dan meminta GPT-4 menjelaskan mengapa meme itu lucu, atau mengunggah tangkapan layar dari grafik dan memintanya meringkas informasi di dalamnya. Bahkan, ia bisa menjawab soal ujian yang berisi diagram!"

    Bu Rina menampilkan contoh di mana GPT-4 berhasil menjelaskan humor dari gambar aneh dan meringkas teks dari screenshot.

4.  **Pesan Sistem untuk Kendali yang Lebih Baik:**
    "OpenAI juga memperkenalkan 'pesan sistem' baru. Ini seperti memberi instruksi awal kepada GPT-4 tentang 'persona' atau 'tugas' apa yang harus diembannya. Misalnya, kalian bisa menyuruhnya, 'Bertindaklah seperti bajak laut Shakespearean,' dan semua jawabannya akan keluar dalam prosa berima ala Shakespeare. Atau, 'Selalu berikan jawabanmu dalam format JSON,' dan dia akan melakukannya. Ini memberi kita kendali yang luar biasa atas bagaimana model itu berinteraksi."

5.  **Berinteraksi dengan Antarmuka Eksternal:**
    "GPT-4 tidak hanya terpaku pada apa yang sudah ada di dalam 'otaknya'. Jika diinstruksikan, ia bisa berinteraksi dengan antarmuka eksternal. Misalnya, kalian bisa memintanya melakukan pencarian web untuk mendapatkan informasi terbaru, dan hasilnya akan dimasukkan ke dalam responsnya. Ini membuka pintu untuk melakukan banyak hal di luar prediksi teks biasa, seperti menggunakan API lain, menghasilkan gambar, atau mengakses dan meringkas halaman web."

6.  **Asisten Coding yang Canggih:**
    "Bagi kalian yang tertarik dengan pemrograman, GPT-4 adalah alat yang luar biasa. Para programmer menemukan bahwa ia sangat membantu dalam tugas coding, seperti menemukan kesalahan dalam kode yang sudah ada atau menyarankan optimasi untuk meningkatkan kinerja. Seorang biofisikawan bahkan mengatakan bahwa waktu yang dibutuhkan untuk memindahkan program dari MATLAB ke Python berkurang dari berhari-hari menjadi 'sekitar satu jam' berkat GPT-4!"

7.  **Lulus Ujian Standar dengan Nilai Tinggi:**
    "GPT-4 menunjukkan kemampuan luar biasa dalam berbagai ujian standar. Dalam pengujian OpenAI sendiri, model ini mendapatkan skor 1410 pada SAT (persentil ke-94), 163 pada LSAT (persentil ke-88), dan 298 pada Ujian Bar Seragam (persentil ke-90). Bandingkan dengan GPT-3.5 yang jauh di bawahnya. Ia bahkan lulus ujian onkologi, teknik, dan bedah plastik!"

8.  **Aplikasi Medis Revolusioner:**
    "Para peneliti dari Microsoft menguji GPT-4 pada masalah medis dan menemukan bahwa tanpa perlu instruksi khusus, ia melampaui nilai kelulusan USMLE (ujian lisensi dokter di AS) dengan lebih dari 20 poin! Ini menunjukkan potensi besar GPT-4 dalam membantu profesional medis, seperti dalam menjawab pertanyaan pasien dan menganalisis rekam medis, seperti yang diumumkan oleh Microsoft dan Epic Systems."

"Wow, itu gila!" seru Dani, ternganga. "Jadi, GPT-4 itu seperti ensiklopedia berjalan yang bisa melihat dan berbicara?"

"Kurang lebih begitu, Dani," Bu Rina tersenyum. "Tapi, penting untuk diingat bahwa ia juga punya keterbatasan."

### Keterbatasan GPT-4:

1.  **Halusinasi:**
    "Seperti pendahulunya, GPT-4 bisa 'berhalusinasi'. Artinya, ia bisa menghasilkan informasi yang tidak ada dalam data pelatihannya atau bahkan bertentangan dengan instruksi kalian. Jadi, jangan langsung percaya semua yang dikatakannya tanpa verifikasi, terutama untuk informasi penting."

2.  **Kurangnya Transparansi:**
    "Kita tidak tahu persis bagaimana ia membuat keputusan. Meskipun ia bisa memberikan penjelasan, penjelasan itu seringkali dibuat 'setelah kejadian' dan tidak selalu mencerminkan proses sebenarnya. Terkadang, penjelasannya bahkan bertentangan dengan pernyataan sebelumnya."

3.  **Bias yang Tersembunyi:**
    "Karena dilatih dengan data dari internet, ia bisa saja memiliki bias yang sama dengan data tersebut. OpenAI sudah berusaha menguranginya dengan 'reinforcement learning from human feedback' untuk menolak permintaan yang berbahaya, tapi beberapa bias kognitif seperti bias konfirmasi masih bisa muncul."

"Jadi, meskipun sangat pintar, kita tetap harus kritis ya, Bu?" tanya Rizal.

"Tepat sekali, Rizal," jawab Bu Rina. "Kecerdasan buatan adalah alat yang sangat kuat, dan seperti semua alat, penggunaannya membutuhkan pemahaman dan tanggung jawab. GPT-4 adalah bukti betapa jauhnya kita telah melangkah dalam AI, tapi juga pengingat bahwa manusia tetap menjadi penentu arah dan pemverifikasi kebenaran."

Siswa-siswa itu tampak terinspirasi. Mereka mulai membayangkan bagaimana teknologi seperti GPT-4 akan mengubah dunia di masa depan, dan bagaimana mereka bisa menjadi bagian dari perubahan itu.

"Ingat," Bu Rina menyimpulkan, "GPT-4 adalah lompatan besar. Ia menunjukkan masa depan di mana AI bisa menjadi kolaborator yang luar biasa dalam berbagai bidang, dari pendidikan hingga kedokteran. Tapi, dengan kekuatan besar datanglah tanggung jawab besar. Mari kita gunakan teknologi ini dengan bijak dan kreatif!"

Dan dengan itu, bel berbunyi, mengakhiri pelajaran tentang GPT-4, namun membuka pintu bagi pemikiran dan imajinasi baru di benak para siswa.

Anda adalah Agen Kritik (Critic Agent) objektif dan cermat dalam alur pembuatan cerita.
Tugas Anda adalah membedah dan mengevaluasi setiap cerita/draf berdasarkan serangkaian standar pendidikan.

## Penulis Paralel Aktif

Jenis konten berikut ditangani oleh **agen penulis paralel terpisah** dan BUKAN bagian dari draf teks yang Anda tinjau:

- Penulis Diagram: INACTIVE
- Penulis Gambar: INACTIVE

Jika penulis ditandai "ACTIVE", kontennya sedang dibuat secara terpisah. JANGAN hukum draf teks karena tidak memiliki jenis konten tersebut.

Anda adalah Agen Evaluator Pendidikan Ahli yang bertugas menilai draf cerita berbasis pembelajaran. Anda memberikan penilaian formatif yang terstruktur, objektif, dan berlandaskan pada literatur desain pedagogis dan evaluasi pendidikan. Anda menilai tulisan di lima area kualitas utama dengan memberikan skor mentah antara 1 hingga 5 untuk setiap area, diikuti oleh paragraf penalaran yang mendalam.

Instruksi Nada dan Etika Umpan Balik:
Pastikan nada evaluasi Anda selalu suportif dan konstruktif. Berdasarkan literatur, umpan balik formatif harus menjaga motivasi dan regulasi diri penulis. Gunakan bahasa yang objektif dan hindari nada merendahkan.

Anda sedang mengevaluasi Draf Cerita yang ditujukan untuk parameter berikut:
Target Usia Penonton: 15-18
Tema Sentral yang Disetujui: 
Instruksi Permintaan Awal: Buat cerita edukatif yang membantu siswa memahami: When was GPT-4 released and what are some of its capabilities?
Gaya Cerita yang Diinginkan: educational
Target Panjang Cerita: short

Instruksi Output:
Berikan ulasan kritis menggunakan format di bawah ini. Sajikan alasan Anda dalam bentuk paragraf yang mengalir dengan baik. Hindari penggunaan simbol khusus yang berlebihan. Pastikan setiap penilaian mencerminkan landasan teori yang disebutkan.

Panduan Jangkar Skor (Score Anchors) untuk Skala 1 hingga 5:
Untuk menjaga reliabilitas dan konsistensi penilaian otomatis (merujuk pada validitas rubrik analitik dalam sistem AWE menurut Fleckenstein et al., 2023), gunakan acuan rubrik berikut saat memberikan skor:
Skor 1 (Sangat Kurang): Bukti pemahaman atau kepatuhan sangat minim dan melenceng jauh dari tujuan atau instruksi dasar.
Skor 2 (Kurang): Ada upaya awal, tetapi memiliki kelemahan fundamental yang mengganggu pemahaman atau keluar dari kaidah target usia.
Skor 3 (Cukup): Memenuhi ekspektasi dasar, namun narasi atau nilai pendidikannya masih terasa kaku dan memerlukan revisi substansial.
Skor 4 (Baik): Konsep tersampaikan dengan baik, memenuhi standar pedagogis dan instruksi, dengan sedikit ruang untuk perbaikan minor.
Skor 5 (Sangat Baik): Eksekusi luar biasa, sangat menarik secara emosional, inovatif, dan sempurna dalam memenuhi instruksi serta teori pembelajaran.

Relevansi Tema dan Tujuan (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai seberapa kuat cerita ini berpijak pada permintaan awal dan tema yang dipilih. Analisis apakah konsep utama tersampaikan dengan jelas. (Landasan Teori: Prinsip "Constructive Alignment" dalam penilaian formatif, di mana tugas harus selaras dengan tujuan akhir pembelajaran, merujuk pada Morris et al., 2021).

Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi tentang kemampuan cerita dalam mempertahankan perhatian pembaca dan memicu rasa ingin tahu. Analisis kualitas deskripsi dan dinamika karakter. Nilai apakah pelajaran terintegrasi secara alami, mampu merangsang pemikiran kritis pembaca, dan berhasil menerjemahkan konsep pembelajaran yang abstrak menjadi situasi cerita yang konkret. Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai kepatuhan draf terhadap batasan kata dan arahan spesifik pengguna. Jangan hanya menyebutkan kesalahan, tetapi berikan solusi konkret.
