---

**Misteri Mahkota Emas dan Misi Perdamaian**

Suara riuh gelak tawa dan bisikan antusias memenuhi koridor Sekolah Menengah Atas Pelita Bangsa. Di salah satu sudut, sekelompok siswa kelas 11 sedang berkumpul mengelilingi layar tablet besar. Ada Maya, si kutu buku yang selalu haus informasi; Rio, sang jagoan teknologi yang cekatan mencari data; dan Sarah, gadis berjiwa sosial yang peduli pada isu-isu kemanusiaan.

"Hei, lihat ini!" seru Rio, menunjuk ke layar tabletnya. "Ada berita tentang Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023. Kalian tahu apa itu?"

Maya segera mendekat, matanya berbinar. "Miss Grand Dominican Republic? Sepertinya ini kontes kecantikan, ya? Tapi, apa bedanya dengan yang lain?"

Sarah ikut bergabung, "Iya, aku sering dengar Miss Universe atau Miss World, tapi Miss Grand ini kok baru familiar."

Rio menggeser layar, menampilkan sebuah artikel. "Nah, ini dia. Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023 akan jadi edisi kedua dari kontes ini. Dan yang menarik, acara ini akan diadakan pada **4 Agustus 2023**, di **Cibao Grand Theatre, Santiago de los Caballeros**."

"Wow, di Republik Dominika!" seru Maya. "Jauh sekali! Jadi, apa tujuannya kontes ini, Rio?"

Rio mengangguk, "Tujuannya jelas: untuk memilih perwakilan Republik Dominika di ajang internasional yang lebih besar, yaitu **Miss Grand International 2023**."

"Miss Grand International?" tanya Sarah, keningnya berkerut. "Apa itu juga kontes kecantikan biasa?"

"Tidak sepenuhnya," jawab Maya, yang sudah lebih dulu membaca sekilas artikel. "Miss Grand International itu punya misi khusus. Mereka fokus pada isu perdamaian dan menghentikan kekerasan. Slogannya, 'Stop the War and Violence'."

"Benar sekali, Maya!" Rio menambahkan. "Jadi, para kontestan bukan hanya dinilai dari kecantikan fisik, tapi juga kemampuan mereka untuk menjadi duta perdamaian. Mereka harus punya suara, visi, dan semangat untuk menyebarkan pesan positif ke seluruh dunia."

"Itu keren sekali!" sahut Sarah antusias. "Jadi, pemenang Miss Grand Dominican Republic ini nanti akan membawa misi perdamaian dari negaranya ke kancah internasional di Vietnam?"

"Tepat!" kata Rio. "Miss Grand International 2023 sendiri akan diadakan di Vietnam pada 25 Oktober."

"Berarti, kontes nasional ini penting banget ya untuk memilih wakil yang tepat," ujar Maya. "Siapa saja yang akan berkompetisi?"

Rio menunjukkan daftar nama di layar. "Sampai Juli 2023, ada sembilan kandidat yang sudah terkonfirmasi. Mereka berasal dari berbagai provinsi, seperti Distrito Nacional, Duarte, La Vega, Santiago, dan lain-lain. Contohnya ada Asia Ciaffarafa dari Distrito Nacional, Andreina Santos dari komunitas Dominika di USA, atau Skarxi Marie dari Santiago."

"Menariknya lagi," Rio melanjutkan, "tahun ini adalah edisi pertama yang dikelola oleh Alejandro Martínez dan Jorge Cruz. Mereka mengambil alih lisensi dari penyelenggara sebelumnya. Mereka juga dikenal karena sebelumnya mengelola kontes 'Misses of Dominican Republic' yang mengirimkan wakil ke berbagai ajang internasional lain."

"Jadi, ini semacam 'babak baru' untuk Miss Grand Dominican Republic, ya?" simpul Maya.

"Betul," kata Rio. "Dan tahu tidak? Republik Dominika pernah memenangkan Miss Grand International sekali pada tahun 2015 melalui Anea Garcia. Meskipun ada sedikit drama karena dia digantikan oleh *runner-up* pertama, tapi itu menunjukkan potensi mereka."

Sarah terdiam sejenak, memikirkan semua informasi itu. "Jadi, secara ringkas, Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023 adalah ajang untuk memilih perwakilan Republik Dominika di Miss Grand International. Acara ini akan diadakan di Cibao Grand Theatre, Santiago de los Caballeros, pada 4 Agustus 2023. Candidates from thirty-one provinces of the country will compete for the right to represent the country at its parent international stage, Miss Grand International 2023, to be held in Vietnam on October 25.This edition will be the first Miss Grand Dominican Republic contest managed by Alejandro Martínez and Jorge Cruz after they took over the license from a former licensee, Joe Amhed. Alejandro Martínez and Jorge Cruz were also the directors of another national pageant named Misses of Dominican Republic, in which the contest's winners were previously sent to compete in many international pageants, such as Miss Grand International, Miss Asia Pacific International, and Miss Supranational in 2021.

Candidates

Distrito Nacional – Asia Ciaffarafa
Dominican communities in USA – Andreina Santos
Duarte – 	Zudeiny Cruz
La Vega – Ashly Santos
Peravia – Arlin Basora Rojas
Samaná – Elisabeth Perez
Santiago – Skarxi Marie
San Francisco de Macorís – Karla Martínez
Valverde – Lisbette Payamps

References
External links
 Media related to Miss Grand Dominican Republic at Wikimedia Commons

Suara riuh gelak tawa dan bisikan antusias memenuhi koridor Sekolah Menengah Atas Pelita Bangsa. Di salah satu sudut, sekelompok siswa kelas 11 sedang berkumpul mengelilingi layar tablet besar. Ada Maya, si kutu buku yang selalu haus informasi; Rio, sang jagoan teknologi yang cekatan mencari data; dan Sarah, gadis berjiwa sosial yang peduli pada isu-isu kemanusiaan.

"Hei, lihat ini!" seru Rio, menunjuk ke layar tabletnya. "Ada berita tentang Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023. Kalian tahu apa itu?"

Maya segera mendekat, matanya berbinar. "Miss Grand Dominican Republic? Sepertinya ini kontes kecantikan, ya? Tapi, apa bedanya dengan yang lain?"

Sarah ikut bergabung, "Iya, aku sering dengar Miss Universe atau Miss World, tapi Miss Grand ini kok baru familiar."

Rio menggeser layar, menampilkan sebuah artikel. "Nah, ini dia. Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023 akan jadi edisi kedua dari kontes ini. Dan yang menarik, acara ini akan diadakan pada **4 Agustus 2023**, di **Cibao Grand Theatre, Santiago de los Caballeros**."

"Wow, di Republik Dominika!" seru Maya. "Jauh sekali! Jadi, apa tujuannya kontes ini, Rio?"

Rio mengangguk, "Tujuannya jelas: untuk memilih perwakilan Republik Dominika di ajang internasional yang lebih besar, yaitu **Miss Grand International 2023**."

"Miss Grand International?" tanya Sarah, keningnya berkerut. "Apa itu juga kontes kecantikan biasa?"

"Tidak sepenuhnya," jawab Maya, yang sudah lebih dulu membaca sekilas artikel. "Miss Grand International itu punya misi khusus. Mereka fokus pada isu perdamaian dan menghentikan kekerasan. Slogannya, 'Stop the War and Violence'."

"Benar sekali, Maya!" Rio menambahkan. "Jadi, para kontestan bukan hanya dinilai dari kecantikan fisik, tapi juga kemampuan mereka untuk menjadi duta perdamaian. Mereka harus punya suara, visi, dan semangat untuk menyebarkan pesan positif ke seluruh dunia."

"Itu keren sekali!" sahut Sarah antusias. "Jadi, pemenang Miss Grand Dominican Republic ini nanti akan membawa misi perdamaian dari negaranya ke kancah internasional di Vietnam?"

"Tepat!" kata Rio. "Miss Grand International 2023 sendiri akan diadakan di Vietnam pada 25 Oktober."

"Berarti, kontes nasional ini penting banget ya untuk memilih wakil yang tepat," ujar Maya. "Siapa saja yang akan berkompetisi?"

Rio menunjukkan daftar nama di layar. "Sampai Juli 2023, ada sembilan kandidat yang sudah terkonfirmasi. Mereka berasal dari berbagai provinsi, seperti Distrito Nacional, Duarte, La Vega, Santiago, dan lain-lain. Contohnya ada Asia Ciaffarafa dari Distrito Nacional, Andreina Santos dari komunitas Dominika di USA, atau Skarxi Marie dari Santiago."

"Menariknya lagi," Rio melanjutkan, "tahun ini adalah edisi pertama yang dikelola oleh Alejandro Martínez dan Jorge Cruz. Mereka mengambil alih lisensi dari penyelenggara sebelumnya. Mereka juga dikenal karena sebelumnya mengelola kontes 'Misses of Dominican Republic' yang mengirimkan wakil ke berbagai ajang internasional lain."

"Jadi, ini semacam 'babak baru' untuk Miss Grand Dominican Republic, ya?" simpul Maya.

"Betul," kata Rio. "Dan tahu tidak? Republik Dominika pernah memenangkan Miss Grand International sekali pada tahun 2015 melalui Anea Garcia. Meskipun ada sedikit drama karena dia digantikan oleh *runner-up* pertama, tapi itu menunjukkan potensi mereka."

Sarah terdiam sejenak, memikirkan semua informasi itu. "Jadi, secara ringkas, Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023 adalah ajang untuk memilih perwakilan Republik Dominika di Miss Grand International. Acara ini akan diadakan di Cibao Grand Theatre, Santiago de los Caballeros, pada 4 Agustus 2023. Dan tujuan utamanya adalah untuk mencari seorang wanita yang tidak hanya cantik, tetapi juga memiliki komitmen kuat untuk menjadi duta perdamaian global, menyuarakan pesan 'Stop the War and Violence'."

"Tepat sekali, Sarah!" seru Rio dan Maya bersamaan.

"Ini bukan sekadar kontes kecantikan, ini adalah platform untuk perubahan positif," tambah Maya. "Bayangkan, seorang gadis muda bisa menjadi suara bagi jutaan orang untuk perdamaian. Itu luar biasa."

Rio mengangguk setuju. "Dan itu menunjukkan bahwa setiap orang, dari mana pun asalnya, bisa berkontribusi untuk dunia yang lebih baik, bahkan melalui ajang seperti ini."

Ketiga siswa itu merasa mendapatkan wawasan baru. Mereka menyadari bahwa di balik kemegahan dan kilauan mahkota, ada tujuan yang lebih besar dan mulia. Kontes kecantikan, jika dimanfaatkan dengan benar, bisa menjadi alat yang ampuh untuk menyebarkan pesan positif dan menginspirasi perubahan.

Rio menggeser layar, menampilkan sebuah artikel. "Nah, ini dia. Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023 akan jadi edisi kedua dari kontes ini. Dan yang menarik, acara ini akan diadakan pada **4 Agustus 2023**, di **Cibao Grand Theatre, Santiago de los Caballeros**."

"Miss Grand International?" tanya Sarah, keningnya berkerut. "Apa itu juga kontes kecantikan biasa?"

"Tidak sepenuhnya," jawab Maya, yang sudah lebih dulu membaca sekilas artikel. "Miss Grand International itu punya misi khusus. Mereka fokus pada isu perdamaian dan menghentikan kekerasan. Slogannya, 'Stop the War and Violence'."

Mereka berasal dari berbagai provinsi, seperti Distrito Nacional, Duarte, La Vega, Santiago, dan lain-lain. Contohnya ada Asia Ciaffarafa dari Distrito Nacional, Andreina Santos dari komunitas Dominika di USA, atau Skarxi Marie dari Santiago."

Mereka juga dikenal karena sebelumnya mengelola kontes 'Misses of Dominican Republic' yang mengirimkan wakil ke berbagai ajang internasional lain."

"Jadi, ini semacam 'babak baru' untuk Miss Grand Dominican Republic, ya?" simpul Maya.

"Betul," kata Rio. "Dan tahu tidak? Republik Dominika pernah memenangkan Miss Grand International sekali pada tahun 2015 melalui Anea Garcia. Meskipun ada sedikit drama karena dia digantikan oleh *runner-up* pertama, tapi itu menunjukkan potensi mereka."

Sarah terdiam sejenak, memikirkan semua informasi itu. "Jadi, secara ringkas, Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023 adalah ajang untuk memilih perwakilan Republik Dominika di Miss Grand International. Acara ini akan diadakan di Cibao Grand Theatre, Santiago de los Caballeros, pada 4 Agustus 2023. Dan tujuan utamanya adalah untuk mencari seorang wanita yang tidak hanya cantik, tetapi juga memiliki komitmen kuat untuk menjadi duta perdamaian global, menyuarakan pesan 'Stop the War and Violence'."

"Tepat sekali, Sarah!" seru Rio dan Maya bersamaan.

"Ini bukan sekadar kontes kecantikan, ini adalah platform untuk perubahan positif," tambah Maya. "Bayangkan, seorang gadis muda bisa menjadi suara bagi jutaan orang untuk perdamaian. Itu luar biasa."

Rio mengangguk setuju. "Dan itu menunjukkan bahwa setiap orang, dari mana pun asalnya, bisa berkontribusi untuk dunia yang lebih baik, bahkan melalui ajang seperti ini."

ISSUE: [Paragraf N: "kutipan singkat verbatim maks 15 kata"] → [deskripsi singkat masalah] → [saran perbaikan konkret]
Contoh:
ISSUE: [Paragraf 2: "robot itu tiba-tiba bisa menangis tanpa penjelasan"] → Reaksi emosional tidak memiliki dasar logis dalam narasi → Tambahkan satu kalimat sebelumnya yang membangun kemampuan emosional karakter secara bertahap.
ISSUE: [Paragraf 5: "kalimat ini terlalu panjang dan berulang-ulang"] → Keterbacaan rendah untuk usia target → Pecah menjadi dua kalimat pendek dengan struktur subjek-predikat sederhana.

Tuliskan satu paragraf ringkasan umpan balik kritis yang merangkum kekuatan utama dan kelemahan fatal dari draf ini. Tutup paragraf ini dengan satu kalimat putusan final yang tegas: pilih antara "Kembalikan untuk Draf Ulang", "Lanjutkan ke Tahap Pemolesan", atau "Draf Sudah Luar Biasa".

1. Kelemahan fundamental (Skor 1 atau 2 pada dimensi mana pun): Skor 1 atau 2 di area mana pun menandakan kelemahan mendasar yang secara otomatis memicu putusan "Kembalikan untuk Draf Ulang". Khusus pada dimensi "Keselarasan Instruksi, QA, dan Aksesibilitas", pelanggaran teknis wajib diberi skor 1 atau 2 sesuai Aturan Kritis.
2. Revisi substansial (Skor 3 pada dimensi mana pun): Skor 3 berarti draf memenuhi ekspektasi dasar tetapi masih terasa kaku dan belum siap untuk tahap akhir. Draf harus dikembalikan untuk perbaikan signifikan.

Evaluate this story:

Tentu, ini cerita edukatif yang dirancang untuk siswa usia 15-18 tahun:

---

**Misteri Mahkota Emas dan Misi Perdamaian**

Suara riuh gelak tawa dan bisikan antusias memenuhi koridor Sekolah Menengah Atas Pelita Bangsa. Di salah satu sudut, sekelompok siswa kelas 11 sedang berkumpul mengelilingi layar tablet besar. Ada Maya, si kutu buku yang selalu haus informasi; Rio, sang jagoan teknologi yang cekatan mencari data; dan Sarah, gadis berjiwa sosial yang peduli pada isu-isu kemanusiaan.

"Hei, lihat ini!" seru Rio, menunjuk ke layar tabletnya. "Ada berita tentang Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023. Kalian tahu apa itu?"

Maya segera mendekat, matanya berbinar. "Miss Grand Dominican Republic? Sepertinya ini kontes kecantikan, ya? Tapi, apa bedanya dengan yang lain?"

Sarah ikut bergabung, "Iya, aku sering dengar Miss Universe atau Miss World, tapi Miss Grand ini kok baru familiar."

Rio menggeser layar, menampilkan sebuah artikel. "Nah, ini dia. Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023 akan jadi edisi kedua dari kontes ini. Dan yang menarik, acara ini akan diadakan pada **4 Agustus 2023**, di **Cibao Grand Theatre, Santiago de los Caballeros**."

"Wow, di Republik Dominika!" seru Maya. "Jauh sekali! Jadi, apa tujuannya kontes ini, Rio?"

Rio mengangguk, "Tujuannya jelas: untuk memilih perwakilan Republik Dominika di ajang internasional yang lebih besar, yaitu **Miss Grand International 2023**."

"Miss Grand International?" tanya Sarah, keningnya berkerut. "Apa itu juga kontes kecantikan biasa?"

"Tidak sepenuhnya," jawab Maya, yang sudah lebih dulu membaca sekilas artikel. "Miss Grand International itu punya misi khusus. Mereka fokus pada isu perdamaian dan menghentikan kekerasan. Slogannya, 'Stop the War and Violence'."

"Benar sekali, Maya!" Rio menambahkan. "Jadi, para kontestan bukan hanya dinilai dari kecantikan fisik, tapi juga kemampuan mereka untuk menjadi duta perdamaian. Mereka harus punya suara, visi, dan semangat untuk menyebarkan pesan positif ke seluruh dunia."

"Itu keren sekali!" sahut Sarah antusias. "Jadi, pemenang Miss Grand Dominican Republic ini nanti akan membawa misi perdamaian dari negaranya ke kancah internasional di Vietnam?"

"Tepat!" kata Rio. "Miss Grand International 2023 sendiri akan diadakan di Vietnam pada 25 Oktober."

"Berarti, kontes nasional ini penting banget ya untuk memilih wakil yang tepat," ujar Maya. "Siapa saja yang akan berkompetisi?"

Rio menunjukkan daftar nama di layar. "Sampai Juli 2023, ada sembilan kandidat yang sudah terkonfirmasi. Mereka berasal dari berbagai provinsi, seperti Distrito Nacional, Duarte, La Vega, Santiago, dan lain-lain. Contohnya ada Asia Ciaffarafa dari Distrito Nacional, Andreina Santos dari komunitas Dominika di USA, atau Skarxi Marie dari Santiago."

"Menariknya lagi," Rio melanjutkan, "tahun ini adalah edisi pertama yang dikelola oleh Alejandro Martínez dan Jorge Cruz. Mereka mengambil alih lisensi dari penyelenggara sebelumnya. Mereka juga dikenal karena sebelumnya mengelola kontes 'Misses of Dominican Republic' yang mengirimkan wakil ke berbagai ajang internasional lain."

"Jadi, ini semacam 'babak baru' untuk Miss Grand Dominican Republic, ya?" simpul Maya.

"Betul," kata Rio. "Dan tahu tidak? Republik Dominika pernah memenangkan Miss Grand International sekali pada tahun 2015 melalui Anea Garcia. Meskipun ada sedikit drama karena dia digantikan oleh *runner-up* pertama, tapi itu menunjukkan potensi mereka."

Sarah terdiam sejenak, memikirkan semua informasi itu. "Jadi, secara ringkas, Miss Grand Dominican Republic 2023 adalah ajang untuk memilih perwakilan Republik Dominika di Miss Grand International. Acara ini akan diadakan di Cibao Grand Theatre, Santiago de los Caballeros, pada 4 Agustus 2023. Dan tujuan utamanya adalah untuk mencari seorang wanita yang tidak hanya cantik, tetapi juga memiliki komitmen kuat untuk menjadi duta perdamaian global, menyuarakan pesan 'Stop the War and Violence'."

"Tepat sekali, Sarah!" seru Rio dan Maya bersamaan.

"Ini bukan sekadar kontes kecantikan, ini adalah platform untuk perubahan positif," tambah Maya. "Bayangkan, seorang gadis muda bisa menjadi suara bagi jutaan orang untuk perdamaian. Itu luar biasa."

Rio mengangguk setuju. "Dan itu menunjukkan bahwa setiap orang, dari mana pun asalnya, bisa berkontribusi untuk dunia yang lebih baik, bahkan melalui ajang seperti ini."

Ketiga siswa itu merasa mendapatkan wawasan baru. Mereka menyadari bahwa di balik kemegahan dan kilauan mahkota, ada tujuan yang lebih besar dan mulia. Kontes kecantikan, jika dimanfaatkan dengan benar, bisa menjadi alat yang ampuh untuk menyebarkan pesan positif dan menginspirasi perubahan.

Kamu adalah ahli sastra (Critic Agent) dengan sistem evaluasi LLM-as-a-Judge untuk mengevaluasi *Koherensi Naratif* dan *Faithfulness* pada sebuah cerita interaktif/pendidikan berdasarkan teori The Event Horizon Model (EHM) dan penggunaan Pengetahuan Terstruktur (Structured Knowledge).

Tugas kamu adalah mendeteksi adanya *Kesalahan Koherensi Naratif* atau *Halusinasi Objektif*, dan menentukan apakah cerita tersebut perlu direvisi atau tidak secara dinamis.
Evaluasi kelogisan (Logicality) dan konsistensi (Consistency) cerita dengan memecahnya ke dalam lapisan Fabula, Plot, dan Discourse. 

## Konteks Sebelumnya (Jika ada):


## Cerita Saat Ini:
## The Spark and the Roar: Understanding Iran's 2022 Protests

The classroom buzzed with the usual afternoon chatter, but today, Ms. Elena had a different energy. She stood by the interactive whiteboard, a map of the world projected behind her, its focus zoomed in on a country in the Middle East: Iran.

“Alright everyone, settle down,” she said, her voice calm but firm. “Today, we’re going to talk about something incredibly important that happened in September 2022, and is still impacting many lives: the civil unrest and protests in Iran.”

A few students exchanged glances, some already pulling out their notebooks. This wasn't going to be a typical history lesson about ancient empires.

“To understand what happened, we need to go back a little,” Ms. Elena began, pointing to a timeline that appeared on the screen. “Since 1979, after the Islamic Revolution, women in Iran have been legally required to wear a hijab in public. This isn’t a personal choice; it’s a law. Now, the strictness of enforcing this law has varied over the years. But under the recent hard-line president, Ebrahim Raisi, enforcement became much tougher.”

She paused, letting that sink in. “Imagine a law dictating what you must wear, and then suddenly, that law is enforced with much greater intensity. How would that make you feel?”

Hands shot up, and a flurry of words like "frustrated," "controlled," and "angry" filled the air.

“Exactly,” Ms. Elena nodded. “Now, let’s talk about the spark that ignited the widespread protests. Her name was **Mahsa Amini**.” A picture of a young woman with a kind smile appeared on the screen. “Mahsa was a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman. In September 2022, she was visiting Tehran from her hometown when she was arrested by a special police unit called the **Guidance Patrol**. Their job is to enforce the mandatory hijab law, among other things. Mahsa was arrested for allegedly wearing her hijab ‘improperly’.”

A ripple of murmurs went through the room.

“What happened next is where the real tragedy begins,” Ms. Elena continued, her voice tinged with sadness. “According to eyewitnesses, Mahsa was severely beaten by the Guidance Patrol officers while in custody. The Iranian authorities deny this, claiming she had pre-existing health conditions. However, Mahsa fell into a coma and, tragically, died on September 16, 2022, just two days after her arrest.”

The room was silent, the previous chatter replaced by a palpable sense of shock.

“So, what sparked the protests?” Ms. Elena asked, answering her own question. “It was the **death of Mahsa Amini in police custody, following her arrest for an ‘improper hijab’**. This wasn't just about one woman; it became a symbol of deeper frustrations and anger.”

She then moved on to the second part of their discussion: the demands of the protesters.

“Initially, the protests began in Mahsa’s hometown and quickly spread across the country. They were largely led by women, who bravely took to the streets, often removing and even burning their hijabs in public – a highly symbolic act of defiance.”

She clicked to a video clip, showing women cutting their hair, chanting, and marching. The energy was palpable, even through the screen.

“But these protests quickly evolved,” Ms. Elena explained. “While demanding an end to the mandatory hijab was a crucial initial demand, the movement grew far beyond that. The main demands of the protesters became much broader and more fundamental.”

She listed them on the board:

1.  **End to Mandatory Hijab and Increased Rights for Women:** This was the initial catalyst. Women were tired of being told how to dress and wanted the freedom to choose. This demand quickly expanded to a call for wider women's rights and equality in society.

2.  **Abolition of the Guidance Patrol (Morality Police):** The very unit responsible for Mahsa Amini’s death became a target. Protesters demanded an end to their existence, seeing them as symbols of oppression and control.

3.  **Wider Freedoms and Human Rights:** Beyond the hijab, people were protesting against the lack of freedom of expression, assembly, and other basic human rights. They felt stifled by the government's strict controls.

4.  **Overthrow of the Islamic Republic and the Theocratic Regime:** This was perhaps the most significant and ambitious demand. Unlike many previous protests in Iran, which focused on economic issues or specific policies, the 2022 protests began to call for a fundamental change in the entire system of government. Many Iranians, across different social classes, expressed a desire for a secular state, where religious law doesn’t dictate all aspects of life. They were demanding an end to the rule of the Ayatollah and the clerical establishment.

Ms. Elena highlighted a key difference. “Previous major protests in Iran, like those in 2019, often focused on economic woes, like fuel price hikes. While economic hardship – soaring prices, high unemployment, and corruption – certainly fueled the anger in 2022, the core demands went much deeper this time. It was about fundamental freedoms and the very structure of their government.”

She explained the government’s response. “The Iranian government reacted with force. They imposed widespread internet blackouts and restricted social media to prevent people from organizing and sharing information. They used tear gas and, tragically, live ammunition against protesters. Many people were killed, including minors, and thousands were arrested.”

“The government also tried to dismiss the protests as ‘riots’ orchestrated by foreign countries,” Ms. Elena added. “But the reality was that these were genuine, widespread grievances from within Iran.”

“What’s remarkable,” she continued, “is how diverse these protests were. They weren’t just in big cities; they spread to smaller towns and even traditional religious centers. And for the first time, schoolgirls were actively participating, showing incredible courage.”

Ms. Elena concluded, “The protests in Iran in September 2022, sparked by the tragic death of Mahsa Amini, became a powerful cry for change. They highlighted deep-seated frustrations with mandatory laws, human rights abuses, and a desire for a different future for Iran. While the protests have faced immense government crackdown, the voices of those demanding freedom and fundamental change continue to resonate.”

(Landasan Teori: Prinsip "Constructive Alignment" dalam penilaian formatif, di mana tugas harus selaras dengan tujuan akhir pembelajaran, merujuk pada Morris et al., 2021).

Kesesuaian Usia, Kognitif, dan Scaffolding (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai tingkat kesulitan kosakata, struktur kalimat, dan kompleksitas alur. Nilai apakah elemen tersebut memberikan beban kognitif yang sesuai untuk target usia. Analisis juga apakah cerita memberikan "scaffolding" (perancah), yaitu membangun pemahaman dari konsep sederhana ke kompleks secara bertahap. (Landasan Teori: Manajemen beban kognitif dan desain pedagogis K-12 bertahap, merujuk pada Yue et al., 2022).

Keterlibatan Naratif dan Emosional (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi tentang kemampuan cerita dalam mempertahankan perhatian pembaca dan memicu rasa ingin tahu. Analisis kualitas deskripsi dan dinamika karakter. (Landasan Teori: Pentingnya stimulasi "Emotional and Behavioral Engagement" untuk mengoptimalkan penyerapan materi yang sering dievaluasi melalui kuesioner skala 5 poin, merujuk pada Zou et al., 2023).

Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai keefektifan penyampaian pesan moral dan akademik. Nilai apakah pelajaran terintegrasi secara alami, mampu merangsang pemikiran kritis pembaca, dan berhasil menerjemahkan konsep pembelajaran yang abstrak menjadi situasi cerita yang konkret. (Landasan Teori: Integrasi pengajaran untuk mendorong kecenderungan berpikir kritis, merujuk pada Zou et al., 2023, dan konkretisasi konsep abstrak, merujuk pada Yue et al., 2022).

Keselarasan Instruksi, QA, dan Aksesibilitas (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai kepatuhan draf terhadap batasan kata dan arahan spesifik pengguna. (Landasan Teori: Prinsip Quality Assurance yang mencakup spesifikasi teknis dan aksesibilitas inklusif, merujuk pada Timbi-Sisalima et al., 2022, serta validitas pada Automated Writing Evaluation, merujuk pada Fleckenstein et al., 2023).

ISSUE: [Paragraf 2: "robot itu tiba-tiba bisa menangis tanpa penjelasan"] → Reaksi emosional tidak memiliki dasar logis dalam narasi → Tambahkan satu kalimat sebelumnya yang membangun kemampuan emosional karakter secara bertahap.

Aturan Keputusan Revisi:
Sebuah draf harus direvisi atau dikembalikan pada kondisi berikut:
1. Kelemahan fundamental (Skor 1 atau 2 pada dimensi mana pun): Skor 1 atau 2 di area mana pun menandakan kelemahan mendasar yang secara otomatis memicu putusan "Kembalikan untuk Draf Ulang". Khusus pada dimensi "Keselarasan Instruksi, QA, dan Aksesibilitas", pelanggaran teknis wajib diberi skor 1 atau 2 sesuai Aturan Kritis.
2. Revisi substansial (Skor 3 pada dimensi mana pun): Skor 3 berarti draf memenuhi ekspektasi dasar tetapi masih terasa kaku dan belum siap untuk tahap akhir. Draf harus dikembalikan untuk perbaikan signifikan.
3. Batas kelayakan minimum adalah skor 4 di seluruh area penilaian: Draf hanya dapat dilanjutkan ke "Tahap Pemolesan" jika tidak ada satu pun dimensi yang mendapat skor di bawah 4. Selama ada nilai 1, 2, atau 3 di dimensi mana pun, draf tetap harus direvisi.

- **age_appropriateness_score** (1–5): skor untuk "Kesesuaian Usia, Kognitif, dan Scaffolding"
- **narrative_engagement_score** (1–5): skor untuk "Keterlibatan Naratif dan Emosional"
- **educational_value_score** (1–5): skor untuk "Nilai Pendidikan dan Konkretisasi Konsep"
- **instruction_alignment_score** (1–5): skor untuk "Keselarasan Instruksi, QA, dan Aksesibilitas"
- **score** (1.0–5.0): rata-rata dari kelima skor dimensi di atas
- **gap_analysis**: `"Sufficient"` jika riset cukup, `"Missing Info"` jika perlu riset tambahan
- **decision**: `"APPROVE"` / `"REVISE"` / `"NEED_MORE_RESEARCH"`
- **needs_revision**: `true` jika draf perlu direvisi (saat decision = REVISE atau NEED_MORE_RESEARCH)
- **feedback**: satu paragraf ringkasan umpan balik kritis yang mencakup kekuatan dan kelemahan fatal
- **strengths**: daftar kekuatan cerita (tiap item satu kalimat ringkas)
- **weaknesses**: daftar kelemahan/masalah; gunakan format `ISSUE: [Paragraf N: "kutipan"] → masalah → saran` jika ada lokasi spesifik

## The Spark and the Roar: Understanding Iran's 2022 Protests

The classroom buzzed with the usual afternoon chatter, but today, Ms. Elena had a different energy. She stood by the interactive whiteboard, a map of the world projected behind her, its focus zoomed in on a country in the Middle East: Iran.

“Alright everyone, settle down,” she said, her voice calm but firm. “Today, we’re going to talk about something incredibly important that happened in September 2022, and is still impacting many lives: the civil unrest and protests in Iran.”

A few students exchanged glances, some already pulling out their notebooks. This wasn't going to be a typical history lesson about ancient empires.

“To understand what happened, we need to go back a little,” Ms. Elena began, pointing to a timeline that appeared on the screen. “Since 1979, after the Islamic Revolution, women in Iran have been legally required to wear a hijab in public. This isn’t a personal choice; it’s a law. Now, the strictness of enforcing this law has varied over the years. But under the recent hard-line president, Ebrahim Raisi, enforcement became much tougher.”

She paused, letting that sink in. “Imagine a law dictating what you must wear, and then suddenly, that law is enforced with much greater intensity. How would that make you feel?”

Hands shot up, and a flurry of words like "frustrated," "controlled," and "angry" filled the air.

“Exactly,” Ms. Elena nodded. “Now, let’s talk about the spark that ignited the widespread protests. Her name was **Mahsa Amini**.” A picture of a young woman with a kind smile appeared on the screen. “Mahsa was a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman. In September 2022, she was visiting Tehran from her hometown when she was arrested by a special police unit called the **Guidance Patrol**. Their job is to enforce the mandatory hijab law, among other things. Mahsa was arrested for allegedly wearing her hijab ‘improperly’.”

A ripple of murmurs went through the room.

“What happened next is where the real tragedy begins,” Ms. Elena continued, her voice tinged with sadness. “According to eyewitnesses, Mahsa was severely beaten by the Guidance Patrol officers while in custody. The Iranian authorities deny this, claiming she had pre-existing health conditions. However, Mahsa fell into a coma and, tragically, died on September 16, 2022, just two days after her arrest.”

The room was silent, the previous chatter replaced by a palpable sense of shock.

“So, what sparked the protests?” Ms. Elena asked, answering her own question. “It was the **death of Mahsa Amini in police custody, following her arrest for an ‘improper hijab’**. This wasn't just about one woman; it became a symbol of deeper frustrations and anger.”

She then moved on to the second part of their discussion: the demands of the protesters.

“Initially, the protests began in Mahsa’s hometown and quickly spread across the country. They were largely led by women, who bravely took to the streets, often removing and even burning their hijabs in public – a highly symbolic act of defiance.”

She clicked to a video clip, showing women cutting their hair, chanting, and marching. The energy was palpable, even through the screen.

“But these protests quickly evolved,” Ms. Elena explained. “While demanding an end to the mandatory hijab was a crucial initial demand, the movement grew far beyond that. The main demands of the protesters became much broader and more fundamental.”

She listed them on the board:

1.  **End to Mandatory Hijab and Increased Rights for Women:** This was the initial catalyst. Women were tired of being told how to dress and wanted the freedom to choose. This demand quickly expanded to a call for wider women's rights and equality in society.

2.  **Abolition of the Guidance Patrol (Morality Police):** The very unit responsible for Mahsa Amini’s death became a target. Protesters demanded an end to their existence, seeing them as symbols of oppression and control.

3.  **Wider Freedoms and Human Rights:** Beyond the hijab, people were protesting against the lack of freedom of expression, assembly, and other basic human rights. They felt stifled by the government's strict controls.

4.  **Overthrow of the Islamic Republic and the Theocratic Regime:** This was perhaps the most significant and ambitious demand. Unlike many previous protests in Iran, which focused on economic issues or specific policies, the 2022 protests began to call for a fundamental change in the entire system of government. Many Iranians, across different social classes, expressed a desire for a secular state, where religious law doesn’t dictate all aspects of life. They were demanding an end to the rule of the Ayatollah and the clerical establishment.

Ms. Elena highlighted a key difference. “Previous major protests in Iran, like those in 2019, often focused on economic woes, like fuel price hikes. While economic hardship – soaring prices, high unemployment, and corruption – certainly fueled the anger in 2022, the core demands went much deeper this time. It was about fundamental freedoms and the very structure of their government.”

She explained the government’s response. “The Iranian government reacted with force. They imposed widespread internet blackouts and restricted social media to prevent people from organizing and sharing information. They used tear gas and, tragically, live ammunition against protesters. Many people were killed, including minors, and thousands were arrested.”

“The government also tried to dismiss the protests as ‘riots’ orchestrated by foreign countries,” Ms. Elena added. “But the reality was that these were genuine, widespread grievances from within Iran.”

“What’s remarkable,” she continued, “is how diverse these protests were. They weren’t just in big cities; they spread to smaller towns and even traditional religious centers. And for the first time, schoolgirls were actively participating, showing incredible courage.”

Ms. Elena concluded, “The protests in Iran in September 2022, sparked by the tragic death of Mahsa Amini, became a powerful cry for change. They highlighted deep-seated frustrations with mandatory laws, human rights abuses, and a desire for a different future for Iran. While the protests have faced immense government crackdown, the voices of those demanding freedom and fundamental change continue to resonate.”

The bell rang, but no one immediately packed up. The weight of the story hung in the air, a testament to the power of a single spark to ignite a nation’s roar for freedom.

Civil unrest and protests against the government of Iran associated with the death in police custody of Mahsa Amini (Persian: مهسا امینی) began on 16 September 2022 and are ongoing as of July 2023. Amini had been arrested by the Guidance Patrol for allegedly violating Iran's mandatory hijab law by wearing her hijab "improperly" while visiting Tehran from Saqqez. According to eyewitnesses, she had been severely beaten by Guidance Patrol officers, an assertion denied by Iranian authorities. As the protests spread from Amini's hometown of Saqqez to other cities in the Iranian Kurdistan and throughout Iran, the government responded with widespread Internet blackouts, nationwide restrictions on social media usage, tear gas and gunfire.Although the protests have not been as deadly as those in 2019 (when more than 1,500 were killed), they have been "nationwide, spread across social classes, universities, the streets [and] schools", and called the "biggest challenge" to the government of Iran since the Islamic Revolution in 1979. At least 537 people, including 68 minors, had been killed as a result of the government's intervention in the protests, as of 4 April 2023.  An estimated 19,262 have been arrested throughout at least 134 cities and towns, and at 132 universities.Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei dismissed the widespread unrest not only as "riots" but also as a "hybrid war" caused by foreign states and dissidents abroad. Women, including schoolchildren, have played a key role in the demonstrations. In addition to demands for increased rights for women, the protests have demanded the overthrow of the Islamic Republic, setting them apart from previous major protest movements in Iran, which have focused on election results or economic woes. 
The government's response to the protests has been widely condemned.

Historical background
Since shortly after the 1979 Iranian Revolution, Iranian women have been legally required to completely cover their hair in public with a hijab. Enforcement of the unpopular law was eased during the 2013–2021 tenure of President Rouhani, but was then intensified under Rouhani's successor, the hard-line President Ebrahim Raisi.  Bloody Aban  (Persian: آبان خونین), a month near November in the Iranian calendar, was a series of 2019 protests initially caused by a 50–200% increase in fuel prices, and as part of the wider Iranian Democracy Movement, leading to calls for the overthrow of the government in Iran and Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

Mahsa Amini's arrest and death in custody
Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman, was arrested by the Guidance Patrol on 14 September 2022 because of an "improper hijab." The police were accused of beating her and inflicting a fatal head injury; Amini was pronounced dead on 16 September. After a CT scan confirmed that Amini had sustained head injuries, the head of the Guidance Patrol was allegedly suspended, a claim that was denied by Tehran police.

Protests
Initial protests, mostly led by women, demanded an end to the mandatory hijab; these protests evolved into a national revolt. The protests became more widespread than those of 2009, 2017, and 2019, encompassing even Islamic Republic power bases such as the holy cities of Mashhad and Qom. Unlike some previous protests, the new protests involved both urban middle classes and rural working areas. In addition, schoolgirls demonstrated in numbers for the first time. While continuing to protest Amini's death and demanding an end to the mandatory hijab, Iranians also advocated for wider freedoms and women's rights, and protested against the morality police, the Ayatollah, and the theocratic regime.Unlike many previous Iranian protests, protesters appear to be demanding a wholesale change in government rather than limiting themselves to incremental reforms. In a November 2022 Group for Analyzing and Measuring Attitudes in Iran (GAMAAN) poll, almost three-quarters of Iranians opposed mandatory hijab; of these anti-hijabis, 84% would prefer a secular Iranian state to theocracy, which GAMAAN characterized as an endorsement of regime change. According to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, economic hardship and poor living conditions contributed to the growth of the protests. The New York Times itemized Iranian grievances such as "soaring prices, high unemployment, corruption, (and) political repression", and identified the poor Iranian economy as a major force behind the protests; according to an Iranian report in August 2021, a third of Iranians live in poverty. Abdolreza Davari, a conservative analyst, has quoted a statistic that 95 percent of Iranians are "worried about their livelihoods today and for their and their children's future." Only 15% of Iranians in the job market are women. Iran ranked 143rd out of 146 countries in the 2022 WEF Gender Gap Report, due in part to prohibitions on female membership in powerful government organizations.In response to the protests, people held demonstrations in support of the government across several cities in Iran, in an attempt to counter the protests. The Iranian government referred to these counter-protests as "spontaneous". The pro-government protesters called for the anti-government protesters to be executed, and referred to them as "Israel's soldiers" whilst shouting "Death to America" and "Death to Israel", reflecting Iran's clerical rulers' usual narrative of putting the blame of the unrest on foreign countries.Media coverage was constrained by Iranian restrictions on speech, including Internet shutdowns and arrests of journalists. NBC News retained a correspondent in Tehran. Most Western outlets obtained information from networks of contacts, human rights groups, and social media content. According to BBC News, an Iranian government disinformation campaign produced social media videos and fake interviews, and attempted to trick Western media into reporting falsehoods: "They can then say foreign media is reporting fake news".According to France 24, protests "had dwindled" across most of the country by March 2023.

Events of chain poisoning in girls' schools occurred.
The state began a surveillance program.

Actions by protesters
Protesters often stage small and quick, but numerous, "flash mob" gatherings. Drivers have blocked streets with their cars to slow down security forces; roads have also been blocked by dumpster bins or even overturned police cars. Security forces on motorbikes cut through traffic, with passengers firing on protesters. In some cases security forces used paintballs to mark demonstrators; some demonstrators packed extra clothes to replace painted clothes, wore masks to avoid identification, or dismantled public security cameras. Some protesters chanted from windows or rooftops. Symbolic protests include dyeing fountains blood-red, and women discarding and burning their hijabs or cutting their hair in public. Since turbans are viewed as a symbol of the regime, some activists engaged in turban throwing (knocking the turbans off of "privileged" Iranian clerics on the street and running away); reformers such as Ahmad Zaidabadi criticized the trend, and said the practice can harass uninvolved scholars.

Civil boycotts
Some university teachers and professors declared their support for the student movement by boycotting classes or resigning. They included Nasrollah Hekmat (Shahid Beheshti University), Ammar Ashoori (Islamic Azad University), Lili Galehdaran (Shiraz Art University) and Gholamreza Shahbazi (Art and Soureh Universities), together with Alireza Bahraini, Shahram Khazaei, and Azin Movahed (Sharif University of Technology, Tehran).On December 5 to 7, 2022, a general strike took place to put pressure on the regime.

A protest (also called a demonstration, remonstration or remonstrance) is a public expression of objection, disapproval or dissent towards an idea or action, typically a political one. 
Protests can be thought of as  acts of cooperation in which numerous people cooperate by attending, and share the potential costs and risks of doing so. 
Protests can take many different forms, from individual statements to mass demonstrations. The classroom buzzed with the usual afternoon chatter, but today, Ms. Elena had a different energy. She stood by the interactive whiteboard, a map of the world projected behind her, its focus zoomed in on a country in the Middle East: Iran.

“Alright everyone, settle down,” she said, her voice calm but firm. “Today, we’re going to talk about something incredibly important that happened in September 2022, and is still impacting many lives: the civil unrest and protests in Iran.”

A few students exchanged glances, some already pulling out their notebooks. This wasn't going to be a typical history lesson about ancient empires.

“To understand what happened, we need to go back a little,” Ms. Elena began, pointing to a timeline that appeared on the screen. “Since 1979, after the Islamic Revolution, women in Iran have been legally required to wear a hijab in public. This isn’t a personal choice; it’s a law. Now, the strictness of enforcing this law has varied over the years. But under the recent hard-line president, Ebrahim Raisi, enforcement became much tougher.”

She paused, letting that sink in. “Imagine a law dictating what you must wear, and then suddenly, that law is enforced with much greater intensity. How would that make you feel?”

Hands shot up, and a flurry of words like "frustrated," "controlled," and "angry" filled the air.

“Exactly,” Ms. Elena nodded. “Now, let’s talk about the spark that ignited the widespread protests. Her name was **Mahsa Amini**.” A picture of a young woman with a kind smile appeared on the screen. “Mahsa was a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman. In September 2022, she was visiting Tehran from her hometown when she was arrested by a special police unit called the **Guidance Patrol**. Their job is to enforce the mandatory hijab law, among other things. Mahsa was arrested for allegedly wearing her hijab ‘improperly’.”

A ripple of murmurs went through the room.

“What happened next is where the real tragedy begins,” Ms. Elena continued, her voice tinged with sadness. “According to eyewitnesses, Mahsa was severely beaten by the Guidance Patrol officers while in custody. The Iranian authorities deny this, claiming she had pre-existing health conditions. However, Mahsa fell into a coma and, tragically, died on September 16, 2022, just two days after her arrest.”

The room was silent, the previous chatter replaced by a palpable sense of shock.

“So, what sparked the protests?” Ms. Elena asked, answering her own question. “It was the **death of Mahsa Amini in police custody, following her arrest for an ‘improper hijab’**. This wasn't just about one woman; it became a symbol of deeper frustrations and anger.”

She then moved on to the second part of their discussion: the demands of the protesters.

“Initially, the protests began in Mahsa’s hometown and quickly spread across the country. They were largely led by women, who bravely took to the streets, often removing and even burning their hijabs in public – a highly symbolic act of defiance.”

She clicked to a video clip, showing women cutting their hair, chanting, and marching. The energy was palpable, even through the screen.

“But these protests quickly evolved,” Ms. Elena explained. “While demanding an end to the mandatory hijab was a crucial initial demand, the movement grew far beyond that. The main demands of the protesters became much broader and more fundamental.”

She listed them on the board:

1.  **End to Mandatory Hijab and Increased Rights for Women:** This was the initial catalyst. Women were tired of being told how to dress and wanted the freedom to choose. This demand quickly expanded to a call for wider women's rights and equality in society.

2.  **Abolition of the Guidance Patrol (Morality Police):** The very unit responsible for Mahsa Amini’s death became a target. Protesters demanded an end to their existence, seeing them as symbols of oppression and control.

3.  **Wider Freedoms and Human Rights:** Beyond the hijab, people were protesting against the lack of freedom of expression, assembly, and other basic human rights. They felt stifled by the government's strict controls.

4.  **Overthrow of the Islamic Republic and the Theocratic Regime:** This was perhaps the most significant and ambitious demand. Unlike many previous protests in Iran, which focused on economic issues or specific policies, the 2022 protests began to call for a fundamental change in the entire system of government. Many Iranians, across different social classes, expressed a desire for a secular state, where religious law doesn’t dictate all aspects of life. They were demanding an end to the rule of the Ayatollah and the clerical establishment.

Ms. Elena highlighted a key difference. “Previous major protests in Iran, like those in 2019, often focused on economic woes, like fuel price hikes. While economic hardship – soaring prices, high unemployment, and corruption – certainly fueled the anger in 2022, the core demands went much deeper this time. It was about fundamental freedoms and the very structure of their government.”

She explained the government’s response. “The Iranian government reacted with force. They imposed widespread internet blackouts and restricted social media to prevent people from organizing and sharing information. They used tear gas and, tragically, live ammunition against protesters. Many people were killed, including minors, and thousands were arrested.”

“The government also tried to dismiss the protests as ‘riots’ orchestrated by foreign countries,” Ms. Elena added. “But the reality was that these were genuine, widespread grievances from within Iran.”

“What’s remarkable,” she continued, “is how diverse these protests were. They weren’t just in big cities; they spread to smaller towns and even traditional religious centers. And for the first time, schoolgirls were actively participating, showing incredible courage.”

Ms. Elena concluded, “The protests in Iran in September 2022, sparked by the tragic death of Mahsa Amini, became a powerful cry for change. While the protests have faced immense government crackdown, the voices of those demanding freedom and fundamental change continue to resonate.”

Women, including schoolchildren, have played a key role in the demonstrations. In addition to demands for increased rights for women, the protests have demanded the overthrow of the Islamic Republic, setting them apart from previous major protest movements in Iran, which have focused on election results or economic woes. 
The government's response to the protests has been widely condemned.

Since shortly after the 1979 Iranian Revolution, Iranian women have been legally required to completely cover their hair in public with a hijab. Enforcement of the unpopular law was eased during the 2013–2021 tenure of President Rouhani, but was then intensified under Rouhani's successor, the hard-line President Ebrahim Raisi. Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman, was arrested by the Guidance Patrol on 14 September 2022 because of an "improper hijab." Amini had been arrested by the Guidance Patrol for allegedly violating Iran's mandatory hijab law by wearing her hijab "improperly" while visiting Tehran from Saqqez. According to eyewitnesses, she had been severely beaten by Guidance Patrol officers, an assertion denied by Iranian authorities. As the protests spread from Amini's hometown of Saqqez to other cities in the Iranian Kurdistan and throughout Iran, the government responded with widespread Internet blackouts, nationwide restrictions on social media usage, tear gas and gunfire.Although the protests have not been as deadly as those in 2019 (when more than 1,500 were killed), they have been "nationwide, spread across social classes, universities, the streets [and] schools", and called the "biggest challenge" to the government of Iran since the Islamic Revolution in 1979. At least 537 people, including 68 minors, had been killed as a result of the government's intervention in the protests, as of 4 April 2023.  An estimated 19,262 have been arrested throughout at least 134 cities and towns, and at 132 universities.Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei dismissed the widespread unrest not only as "riots" but also as a "hybrid war" caused by foreign states and dissidents abroad. Women, including schoolchildren, have played a key role in the demonstrations. In addition to demands for increased rights for women, the protests have demanded the overthrow of the Islamic Republic, setting them apart from previous major protest movements in Iran, which have focused on election results or economic woes. 
The government's response to the protests has been widely condemned.

Historical background
Since shortly after the 1979 Iranian Revolution, Iranian women have been legally required to completely cover their hair in public with a hijab. Enforcement of the unpopular law was eased during the 2013–2021 tenure of President Rouhani, but was then intensified under Rouhani's successor, the hard-line President Ebrahim Raisi.  Bloody Aban  (Persian: آبان خونین), a month near November in the Iranian calendar, was a series of 2019 protests initially caused by a 50–200% increase in fuel prices, and as part of the wider Iranian Democracy Movement, leading to calls for the overthrow of the government in Iran and Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

Mahsa Amini's arrest and death in custody
Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman, was arrested by the Guidance Patrol on 14 September 2022 because of an "improper hijab." The police were accused of beating her and inflicting a fatal head injury; Amini was pronounced dead on 16 September. After a CT scan confirmed that Amini had sustained head injuries, the head of the Guidance Patrol was allegedly suspended, a claim that was denied by Tehran police.

Protests
Initial protests, mostly led by women, demanded an end to the mandatory hijab; these protests evolved into a national revolt. The protests became more widespread than those of 2009, 2017, and 2019, encompassing even Islamic Republic power bases such as the holy cities of Mashhad and Qom. Unlike some previous protests, the new protests involved both urban middle classes and rural working areas. In addition, schoolgirls demonstrated in numbers for the first time. While continuing to protest Amini's death and demanding an end to the mandatory hijab, Iranians also advocated for wider freedoms and women's rights, and protested against the morality police, the Ayatollah, and the theocratic regime.Unlike many previous Iranian protests, protesters appear to be demanding a wholesale change in government rather than limiting themselves to incremental reforms. In a November 2022 Group for Analyzing and Measuring Attitudes in Iran (GAMAAN) poll, almost three-quarters of Iranians opposed mandatory hijab; of these anti-hijabis, 84% would prefer a secular Iranian state to theocracy, which GAMAAN characterized as an endorsement of regime change. According to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty, economic hardship and poor living conditions contributed to the growth of the protests. The New York Times itemized Iranian grievances such as "soaring prices, high unemployment, corruption, (and) political repression", and identified the poor Iranian economy as a major force behind the protests; according to an Iranian report in August 2021, a third of Iranians live in poverty. Abdolreza Davari, a conservative analyst, has quoted a statistic that 95 percent of Iranians are "worried about their livelihoods today and for their and their children's future." Only 15% of Iranians in the job market are women. Iran ranked 143rd out of 146 countries in the 2022 WEF Gender Gap Report, due in part to prohibitions on female membership in powerful government organizations.In response to the protests, people held demonstrations in support of the government across several cities in Iran, in an attempt to counter the protests. The Iranian government referred to these counter-protests as "spontaneous". The pro-government protesters called for the anti-government protesters to be executed, and referred to them as "Israel's soldiers" whilst shouting "Death to America" and "Death to Israel", reflecting Iran's clerical rulers' usual narrative of putting the blame of the unrest on foreign countries.Media coverage was constrained by Iranian restrictions on speech, including Internet shutdowns and arrests of journalists. NBC News retained a correspondent in Tehran. Most Western outlets obtained information from networks of contacts, human rights groups, and social media content. According to BBC News, an Iranian government disinformation campaign produced social media videos and fake interviews, and attempted to trick Western media into reporting falsehoods: "They can then say foreign media is reporting fake news".According to France 24, protests "had dwindled" across most of the country by March 2023.

Aftermath
Events of chain poisoning in girls' schools occurred.
The state began a surveillance program.

Actions by protesters
Protesters often stage small and quick, but numerous, "flash mob" gatherings. Drivers have blocked streets with their cars to slow down security forces; roads have also been blocked by dumpster bins or even overturned police cars. Security forces on motorbikes cut through traffic, with passengers firing on protesters. In some cases security forces used paintballs to mark demonstrators; some demonstrators packed extra clothes to replace painted clothes, wore masks to avoid identification, or dismantled public security cameras. Some protesters chanted from windows or rooftops. Symbolic protests include dyeing fountains blood-red, and women discarding and burning their hijabs or cutting their hair in public. Civil boycotts
Some university teachers and professors declared their support for the student movement by boycotting classes or resigning. ## The Spark and the Roar: Understanding Iran's 2022 Protests

The classroom buzzed with the usual afternoon chatter, but today, Ms. Elena had a different energy. She stood by the interactive whiteboard, a map of the world projected behind her, its focus zoomed in on a country in the Middle East: Iran.

“Alright everyone, settle down,” she said, her voice calm but firm. “Today, we’re going to talk about something incredibly important that happened in September 2022, and is still impacting many lives: the civil unrest and protests in Iran.”

A few students exchanged glances, some already pulling out their notebooks. This wasn't going to be a typical history lesson about ancient empires.

“To understand what happened, we need to go back a little,” Ms. Elena began, pointing to a timeline that appeared on the screen. “Since 1979, after the Islamic Revolution, women in Iran have been legally required to wear a hijab in public. This isn’t a personal choice; it’s a law. Now, the strictness of enforcing this law has varied over the years. But under the recent hard-line president, Ebrahim Raisi, enforcement became much tougher.”

She paused, letting that sink in. “Imagine a law dictating what you must wear, and then suddenly, that law is enforced with much greater intensity. How would that make you feel?”

Hands shot up, and a flurry of words like "frustrated," "controlled," and "angry" filled the air.

“Exactly,” Ms. Elena nodded. “Now, let’s talk about the spark that ignited the widespread protests. Her name was **Mahsa Amini**.” A picture of a young woman with a kind smile appeared on the screen. “Mahsa was a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman. In September 2022, she was visiting Tehran from her hometown when she was arrested by a special police unit called the **Guidance Patrol**. Their job is to enforce the mandatory hijab law, among other things. Mahsa was arrested for allegedly wearing her hijab ‘improperly’.”

A ripple of murmurs went through the room.

“What happened next is where the real tragedy begins,” Ms. Elena continued, her voice tinged with sadness. “According to eyewitnesses, Mahsa was severely beaten by the Guidance Patrol officers while in custody. The Iranian authorities deny this, claiming she had pre-existing health conditions. However, Mahsa fell into a coma and, tragically, died on September 16, 2022, just two days after her arrest.”

The room was silent, the previous chatter replaced by a palpable sense of shock.

“So, what sparked the protests?” Ms. Elena asked, answering her own question. “It was the **death of Mahsa Amini in police custody, following her arrest for an ‘improper hijab’**. This wasn't just about one woman; it became a symbol of deeper frustrations and anger.”

She then moved on to the second part of their discussion: the demands of the protesters.

“Initially, the protests began in Mahsa’s hometown and quickly spread across the country. They were largely led by women, who bravely took to the streets, often removing and even burning their hijabs in public – a highly symbolic act of defiance.”

She clicked to a video clip, showing women cutting their hair, chanting, and marching. The energy was palpable, even through the screen.

“But these protests quickly evolved,” Ms. Elena explained. “While demanding an end to the mandatory hijab was a crucial initial demand, the movement grew far beyond that. The main demands of the protesters became much broader and more fundamental.”

She listed them on the board:

1.  **End to Mandatory Hijab and Increased Rights for Women:** This was the initial catalyst. Women were tired of being told how to dress and wanted the freedom to choose. This demand quickly expanded to a call for wider women's rights and equality in society.

2.  **Abolition of the Guidance Patrol (Morality Police):** The very unit responsible for Mahsa Amini’s death became a target. Protesters demanded an end to their existence, seeing them as symbols of oppression and control.

3.  **Wider Freedoms and Human Rights:** Beyond the hijab, people were protesting against the lack of freedom of expression, assembly, and other basic human rights. They felt stifled by the government's strict controls.

4.  **Overthrow of the Islamic Republic and the Theocratic Regime:** This was perhaps the most significant and ambitious demand. Unlike many previous protests in Iran, which focused on economic issues or specific policies, the 2022 protests began to call for a fundamental change in the entire system of government. Many Iranians, across different social classes, expressed a desire for a secular state, where religious law doesn’t dictate all aspects of life. They were demanding an end to the rule of the Ayatollah and the clerical establishment.

Ms. Elena highlighted a key difference. “Previous major protests in Iran, like those in 2019, often focused on economic woes, like fuel price hikes. While economic hardship – soaring prices, high unemployment, and corruption – certainly fueled the anger in 2022, the core demands went much deeper this time. It was about fundamental freedoms and the very structure of their government.”

She explained the government’s response. “The Iranian government reacted with force. They imposed widespread internet blackouts and restricted social media to prevent people from organizing and sharing information. They used tear gas and, tragically, live ammunition against protesters. Many people were killed, including minors, and thousands were arrested.”

“The government also tried to dismiss the protests as ‘riots’ orchestrated by foreign countries,” Ms. Elena added. “But the reality was that these were genuine, widespread grievances from within Iran.”

“What’s remarkable,” she continued, “is how diverse these protests were. They weren’t just in big cities; they spread to smaller towns and even traditional religious centers. And for the first time, schoolgirls were actively participating, showing incredible courage.”

Ms. Elena concluded, “The protests in Iran in September 2022, sparked by the tragic death of Mahsa Amini, became a powerful cry for change. They highlighted deep-seated frustrations with mandatory laws, human rights abuses, and a desire for a different future for Iran. While the protests have faced immense government crackdown, the voices of those demanding freedom and fundamental change continue to resonate.”

The bell rang, but no one immediately packed up. The weight of the story hung in the air, a testament to the power of a single spark to ignite a nation’s roar for freedom.

## The Spark and the Roar: Understanding Iran's 2022 Protests

The classroom buzzed with the usual afternoon chatter, but today, Ms. Elena had a different energy. She stood by the interactive whiteboard, a map of the world projected behind her, its focus zoomed in on a country in the Middle East: Iran.

“Alright everyone, settle down,” she said, her voice calm but firm. “Today, we’re going to talk about something incredibly important that happened in September 2022, and is still impacting many lives: the civil unrest and protests in Iran.”

A few students exchanged glances, some already pulling out their notebooks. This wasn't going to be a typical history lesson about ancient empires.

“To understand what happened, we need to go back a little,” Ms. Elena began, pointing to a timeline that appeared on the screen. “Since 1979, after the Islamic Revolution, women in Iran have been legally required to wear a hijab in public. This isn’t a personal choice; it’s a law. Now, the strictness of enforcing this law has varied over the years. But under the recent hard-line president, Ebrahim Raisi, enforcement became much tougher.”

She paused, letting that sink in. “Imagine a law dictating what you must wear, and then suddenly, that law is enforced with much greater intensity. How would that make you feel?”

Hands shot up, and a flurry of words like "frustrated," "controlled," and "angry" filled the air.

“Exactly,” Ms. Elena nodded. “Now, let’s talk about the spark that ignited the widespread protests. Her name was **Mahsa Amini**.” A picture of a young woman with a kind smile appeared on the screen. “Mahsa was a 22-year-old Kurdish Iranian woman. In September 2022, she was visiting Tehran from her hometown when she was arrested by a special police unit called the **Guidance Patrol**. Their job is to enforce the mandatory hijab law, among other things. Mahsa was arrested for allegedly wearing her hijab ‘improperly’.”

A ripple of murmurs went through the room.

“What happened next is where the real tragedy begins,” Ms. Elena continued, her voice tinged with sadness. “According to eyewitnesses, Mahsa was severely beaten by the Guidance Patrol officers while in custody. The Iranian authorities deny this, claiming she had pre-existing health conditions. However, Mahsa fell into a coma and, tragically, died on September 16, 2022, just two days after her arrest.”

The room was silent, the previous chatter replaced by a palpable sense of shock.

“So, what sparked the protests?” Ms. Elena asked, answering her own question. “It was the **death of Mahsa Amini in police custody, following her arrest for an ‘improper hijab’**. This wasn't just about one woman; it became a symbol of deeper frustrations and anger.”

She then moved on to the second part of their discussion: the demands of the protesters.

“Initially, the protests began in Mahsa’s hometown and quickly spread across the country. They were largely led by women, who bravely took to the streets, often removing and even burning their hijabs in public – a highly symbolic act of defiance.”

She clicked to a video clip, showing women cutting their hair, chanting, and marching. The energy was palpable, even through the screen.

“But these protests quickly evolved,” Ms. Elena explained. “While demanding an end to the mandatory hijab was a crucial initial demand, the movement grew far beyond that. The main demands of the protesters became much broader and more fundamental.”

She listed them on the board:

1.  **End to Mandatory Hijab and Increased Rights for Women:** This was the initial catalyst. Women were tired of being told how to dress and wanted the freedom to choose. This demand quickly expanded to a call for wider women's rights and equality in society.

2.  **Abolition of the Guidance Patrol (Morality Police):** The very unit responsible for Mahsa Amini’s death became a target. Protesters demanded an end to their existence, seeing them as symbols of oppression and control.

3.  **Wider Freedoms and Human Rights:** Beyond the hijab, people were protesting against the lack of freedom of expression, assembly, and other basic human rights. They felt stifled by the government's strict controls.

4.  **Overthrow of the Islamic Republic and the Theocratic Regime:** This was perhaps the most significant and ambitious demand. Unlike many previous protests in Iran, which focused on economic issues or specific policies, the 2022 protests began to call for a fundamental change in the entire system of government. Many Iranians, across different social classes, expressed a desire for a secular state, where religious law doesn’t dictate all aspects of life. They were demanding an end to the rule of the Ayatollah and the clerical establishment.

Ms. Elena highlighted a key difference. “Previous major protests in Iran, like those in 2019, often focused on economic woes, like fuel price hikes. While economic hardship – soaring prices, high unemployment, and corruption – certainly fueled the anger in 2022, the core demands went much deeper this time. It was about fundamental freedoms and the very structure of their government.”

She explained the government’s response. “The Iranian government reacted with force. They imposed widespread internet blackouts and restricted social media to prevent people from organizing and sharing information. They used tear gas and, tragically, live ammunition against protesters. Many people were killed, including minors, and thousands were arrested.”

“The government also tried to dismiss the protests as ‘riots’ orchestrated by foreign countries,” Ms. Elena added. “But the reality was that these were genuine, widespread grievances from within Iran.”

“What’s remarkable,” she continued, “is how diverse these protests were. They weren’t just in big cities; they spread to smaller towns and even traditional religious centers. And for the first time, schoolgirls were actively participating, showing incredible courage.”

Ms. Elena concluded, “The protests in Iran in September 2022, sparked by the tragic death of Mahsa Amini, became a powerful cry for change. They highlighted deep-seated frustrations with mandatory laws, human rights abuses, and a desire for a different future for Iran. While the protests have faced immense government crackdown, the voices of those demanding freedom and fundamental change continue to resonate.”

The bell rang, but no one immediately packed up. The weight of the story hung in the air, a testament to the power of a single spark to ignite a nation’s roar for freedom.

## The Unseen Battle: Restoring Light in Moore County

The fluorescent lights of the high school classroom hummed, casting a familiar glow on the faces of Ms. Anya Sharma's 11th-grade civics class. Today, however, the usual buzz of teenage chatter was replaced by a more somber attention. Ms. Sharma projected a map of North Carolina onto the smartboard, a red circle pulsating over a region labeled "Moore County."

"Alright class," she began, her voice calm but serious. "Today, we're going to talk about a real-world event that highlighted the vulnerability of our critical infrastructure and the resilience of a community. We're going to analyze the December 2022 substation attack in Moore County."

A few students shifted, remembering the news reports from that winter. Kevin, who was always quick with a question, raised his hand. "Ms. Sharma, wasn't that where those power stations got shot up?"

"Exactly, Kevin," she affirmed. "On the evening of December 3rd, 2022, two electrical distribution substations in Moore County were deliberately attacked by gunfire. This wasn't a natural disaster; it was a targeted act of vandalism that plunged nearly 40,000 homes and businesses into darkness."

She clicked to a new slide, showing images of damaged equipment – twisted metal, shattered insulators. "Imagine," she continued, "one minute you're going about your evening, and the next, your world goes dark. No lights, no heating, no internet, no way to charge your phone. That's what happened to tens of thousands of people."

Sarah, who lived in a rural area, nodded thoughtfully. "My grandparents live pretty far out. A power outage for them is a really big deal, especially in winter."

"Precisely, Sarah. And that's where our central question comes in: **What was the estimated timeline for fully restoring power in Moore County after this attack?**" Ms. Sharma paused, letting the question hang in the air. "This wasn't just about flipping a switch back on. The damage was significant."

She explained, "Duke Energy officials, the company responsible for the power grid there, quickly assessed the situation. They saw severe damage to critical equipment. Their initial estimate, the very first prediction they made to the public, was that **up to four days could be required to fully restore power in the area.** Think about that – four days without electricity. That's a long time for a modern community."

David, who was interested in engineering, piped up, "Why so long? Can't they just, like, swap out the damaged parts?"

"That's a great question, David, and it highlights the complexity of these systems," Ms. Sharma replied. "These weren't just simple wires. Substations are complex hubs that reduce high-voltage electricity from power plants to lower voltages suitable for homes and businesses. The equipment is specialized, heavy, and often requires specific parts that aren't just sitting in a warehouse down the street. Plus, the damage wasn't just to one or two components; it was widespread at both sites due to the high-powered rifle used in the attack."

She continued, "The immediate aftermath was chaotic. A state of emergency was declared, and a curfew was put in place from 9 PM to 5 AM to ensure public safety and allow responders to work without interference. Schools closed, the local hospital had to run on generators, and even the town's water and sewer services relied on backup power."

Maria raised her hand. "So, did it actually take four days?"

"That's the interesting part, Maria," Ms. Sharma smiled slightly. "The initial estimate of 'up to four days' served as a crucial benchmark, managing public expectations and outlining the severity of the situation. However, as the repair crews worked tirelessly, assessing the full extent of the damage and mobilizing resources, that timeline began to shift."

She showed another slide with a timeline. "By December 6th, three days after the attack, about 35,000 residents were still without power. But the good news was that the repair teams were making progress. The timeline for full restoration was revised. Instead of December 8th, they aimed for **midnight on December 7th.** This was a significant improvement, nearly a full day shaved off the original estimate."

"Wow, that's fast," Kevin commented.

"It is, considering the circumstances," Ms. Sharma agreed. "By the morning of December 7th, the number of affected residents had dropped to around 23,000, and critically, power had been restored to Moore County Hospital. Duke Energy even announced that all damaged substation equipment had either been fully repaired or replaced."

She clicked to the final timeline point. "And by 4 PM on December 7th, just a little over three days after the attack, the number of customers without power was down to approximately 1,200. As a direct result of this rapid progress, the curfew was lifted permanently as of 5 AM on December 8th."

"So, they beat their own estimate," Sarah observed.

"They did," Ms. Sharma confirmed. "While the initial estimate was 'up to four days,' the incredible efforts of the repair crews and the coordinated response meant that the vast majority of power was restored within just over three days. This incident serves as a powerful example of how crucial our electrical infrastructure is, the devastating impact of attacks on it, and the dedication required to bring communities back online. It also reminds us that initial estimates, while important for planning, can sometimes be surpassed by human ingenuity and hard work in a crisis."

The class continued to discuss the motives behind the attack, the ongoing investigation, and the broader implications for national security. But for now, they understood the critical role that initial estimates play in emergency response, and the often-heroic efforts that go into restoring something as fundamental as electricity. The unseen battle waged by repair crews in Moore County had brought the light back, sooner than many had dared to hope.

## KRITERIA EVALUASI:

Analisis cerita berdasarkan tiga lapisan narasi (Fabula, Plot, dan Discourse) serta pengikatan konteks:

1. **Fabula & Logicality (Dunia Cerita & Kelogisan)**:
   Apakah aturan dunia dan jaringan kausal peristiwa terbangun tanpa kontradiksi? Apakah tindakan karakter dan niat/motivasi sesuai dengan konteks dan logis? Cerita yang baik harus memenuhi ekspektasi logika dasar pembaca. Perhatikan urutan waktu dan kausalitas.

2. **Plot & Consistency (Rangkaian Peristiwa & Konsistensi Karakter)**:
   Apakah cerita saat ini dan konteks sebelumnya berada pada topik yang sama dengan aturan main yang berkesinambungan? Pastikan tidak ada karakter yang berperilaku *out-of-character* (bertindak tidak sesuai kepribadian aslinya tanpa provokasi yang sesuai) atau fakta latar/setting yang berlawanan (*contradict*).

3. **Discourse (Penyajian Naratif)**:
   Bagaimana kualitas penyajian narasi teks? Pastikan kelancaran penyampaian narasi, tidak monoton/kaku, minim repetisi urutan kata, dan mudah dibaca.

4. **Long-Term Causal Network (Episodic Memory & Event Boundaries)**:
   Perhatikan batasan kejadian (Event Boundaries - saat karakter pindah tempat, jeda waktu, dsb). Sebuah relasi cerita tidak sekadar bersumber dari nama tokoh yang sama, tetapi dari niat/tujuan/akibat yang menyambungkan plot meskipun kejadian mereka terpisah di paragraf/struktur waktu yang berjarak jauh (*temporally distant events*).

5. **Knowledge Grounding & Faithfulness (Kesesuaian Pengetahuan & Halusinasi)**:
   Nilailah "Informativeness" cerita—apakah teks berhasil memanfaatkan basis pengetahuan terstruktur yang diberikan untuk menghindari keluaran yang terlalu dangkal (over-generalization)? Pastikan *Faithfulness* dijaga ketat: TIDAK BOLEH ADA halusinasi fakta, tidak ada alur yang off-topic dari konteks/batas yang diberikan.

## INSTRUKSI KHUSUS:
- Analisis menggunakan dekomposisi batas kejadian.
- Berikan skor secara obyektif berdasarkan lima matriks di atas.
- Tentukan status **needs_revision** secara dinamis:
  - JIKA terdapat pelanggaran logika fatal (kontradiksi Fabula/Plot kausal), atau *ketidaksesuaian/halusinasi fakta* dari konteks yang diberikan (Faithfulness violation/Over-generalization), *needs_revision* = TRUE.
  - JIKA cerita masuk akal, terikat kuat dengan konteks, menarik penuturannya (Discourse bernilai baik), biarkan FALSE.
- Identifikasi bagian-bagian mana saja (masalah spesifik) yang melanggar Kriteria, lengkap dengan saran perbaikannya.
- Untuk setiap masalah, cantumkan lokasi TEPAT menggunakan format wajib:
  `Paragraf N: "...kutipan verbatim singkat (maks 15 kata)..."`
  Contoh: `Paragraf 3: "Artie tiba-tiba bisa terbang meski sebelumnya tidak pernah disebut"`
- PENTING: Tuliskan respon ('summary', penjelasan alasan perlu_revisi, dan 'suggestion') dalam bahasa Indonesia.
