The Kyzylkum Desert (Uzbek: Qizilqum, Қизилқум, قىزىلقۇم; Kazakh: Қызылқұм, romanized: Qyzylqūm, قىزىلقۇم) is the 15th largest desert in the world. Its name means Red Sand in Turkic languages. It is located in Central Asia, in the land between the confluent rivers Amu Darya and Syr Darya, a region historically known as Transoxania. Today it is divided between Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. It covers about 298,000 km2 (115,000 sq mi).

Geography
The territory consists mainly of an extensive plain at an altitude up to 300 m (980 ft) above sea level, with a number of depressions and highlands (Sultanuizdag, Bukantau). Most of the area is covered with dunes (barchans); in the northwest large areas are covered with takirs (clay coatings); there are also some oases. There are agricultural settlements along the rivers and in the oases. Temperatures can be very high during the summer months, from mid-May to mid-September. Kerki, one extreme inland city located on the banks of the Amu Darya River, recorded 52 °C (126 °F) in July 1983. It is mainly located in Uzbekistan.

Fauna
Desert fauna include the Russian tortoise (Testudo horsfieldii) and a large lizard known as the Transcaspian or desert monitor (Varanus griseus), which can reach lengths of 1.6 m (5.2 ft). The saiga antelope (Saiga tatarica) also occasionally migrates through the northern part of the desert.
Kyzylkum Nature Reserve in Bukhara Region was established in 1971. The area of the reserve amounts to 101,000 km2 (39,000 sq mi) and it is located on flood-land (tugai) drained by the Amudarya close to the settlement Dargan Ata. Fauna include: Bactrian deer (Cervus elaphus bactrianus), wild boar (Sus scrofa), common pheasant (Phasianus colchicus), golden eagle (Aquila chrysaetus).
Djeyran Reserve is located 40 km (25 mi) south of Bukhara. The total area of this reserve is 51,450 km2 (19,860 sq mi). It is a breeding centre for rare species such as goitered gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa), Przewalski's horse (Equus ferus przewalskii), Turkmenian kulan (Equus hemionus kulan) and MacQueen's bustard (Chlamydotis macqueenii). The reserve was founded in 1977 on the enclosed area in 5,131 ha (19.81 sq mi).

Paleontology
The Kyzylkum Desert has exposed rock formations that have yielded a number of fossils.  Of particular interest is the Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan, from the early Late Cretaceous, which has produced several species of early birds: Incolornis martini, Explorornis walkeri, Kizylkumavis cretacea, Kuszholia mengi, Lenesornis kaskarovi, Sazavis prisca, Zhyraornis kaskarovi and Z. logunovi are recognized as valid species. Tyrannosaurid, therizinosaurid, ornithomimosaur, oviraptorosaurian, troodontid, ankylosaur, hadrosaur, and ceratopsian dinosaurs are also known from this rock unit. Other fossils from the Cretaceous rocks of the Kyzylkum include tree trunks, pelecypods, beetles, sharks, rays, bony fish, frogs, salamanders, turtles, crocodylomorphs, pterosaurs, and a varied fauna of small early mammals. Paleontologists that have worked in this area include J. David Archibald, Alexander Averianov, Sergei Kurzanov, Lev Nesov, Anatoly Riabinin, Anatoly Rozhdestvensky, and Hans-Dieter Sues.

Economy
The local population uses the large spaces of the Kyzylkum Desert as a pasture for livestock (mostly sheep, Bactrian camels and dromedaries).
The desert is well known for its deposits of gold, uranium, copper, aluminium and silver, natural gas and oil. The development of the most famous gold-field at Muruntau began in the early 1970s. The centres for the mining and smelting industry at the region are Navoi, Zarafshan, Uchkuduk. The major industrial enterprises are: НГМК (Navoi Mining and Smelting Complex) and the Uzbek U.S.A. Joint Venture "Zarafshan-Newmont". The centres of the gas-production industry are Gazli and Mubarek.

## Rahasia Harta Karun Gurun Pasir Merah

Matahari bersinar terik di atas Gurun Kyzylkum, gurun ke-15 terbesar di dunia. Namanya, "Pasir Merah" dalam bahasa Turkik, benar-benar menggambarkan pemandangan hamparan pasir luas berwarna kemerahan yang membentang sejauh mata memandang. Sarah, seorang siswi SMA yang gemar geografi, melihat peta Gurun Kyzylkum dengan takjub. Gurun ini, yang terbagi antara Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, dan Uzbekistan, dulunya adalah bagian dari Transoxania yang bersejarah.

"Aku selalu berpikir gurun itu hanya pasir dan panas," gumam Sarah pada temannya, Rizky, saat mereka mengerjakan proyek kelompok tentang sumber daya alam. "Tapi, Kyzylkum ini sepertinya menyimpan banyak rahasia."

Rizky, yang lebih tertarik pada ekonomi dan industri, mengangguk. "Betul, Sarah. Gurun ini bukan sekadar hamparan pasir kosong. Justru, Kyzylkum adalah gudang harta karun alam yang luar biasa!"

Sarah mengangkat alisnya penasaran. "Harta karun apa maksudmu?"

Rizky menunjuk ke peta. "Lihat ini. Kyzylkum terkenal dengan **cadangan emasnya yang melimpah**, terutama di ladang emas Muruntau yang mulai dikembangkan sejak awal 1970-an. Bayangkan, salah satu ladang emas terbesar di dunia ada di sini!"

"Wow, emas!" seru Sarah. "Jadi, gurun yang panas dan kering ini menyimpan logam mulia?"

"Tepat sekali!" Rizky melanjutkan, "Bukan hanya emas, Kyzylkum juga kaya akan **uranium**, yang sangat penting untuk energi nuklir. Selain itu, ada juga **tembaga, aluminium, dan perak**. Itu semua adalah logam yang sangat dibutuhkan dalam berbagai industri modern."

Sarah mulai membayangkan truk-truk besar dan alat berat yang bekerja di tengah gurun. "Jadi, ada banyak pertambangan di sana?"

"Tentu saja," jawab Rizky. "Pusat-pusat industri pertambangan dan peleburan di wilayah ini adalah **Navoi, Zarafshan, dan Uchkuduk**. Di sana, sumber daya alam ini diolah dan disiapkan untuk digunakan. Perusahaan-perusahaan besar seperti **Navoi Mining and Smelting Complex (НГМК)** dan usaha patungan Uzbekistan-AS **'Zarafshan-Newmont'** adalah pemain utama dalam industri ini."

"Menarik sekali!" kata Sarah. "Aku tidak menyangka gurun bisa seproduktif ini."

Rizky tersenyum. "Belum selesai, Sarah. Selain logam, Kyzylkum juga memiliki cadangan **gas alam dan minyak bumi** yang signifikan. Ini adalah sumber energi fosil penting yang menggerakkan banyak industri dan kehidupan kita sehari-hari."

"Gas alam dan minyak bumi juga?" Sarah semakin terkejut. "Jadi, gurun ini benar-benar sumber energi dan bahan baku?"

"Ya, dan pusat industri produksi gas di wilayah ini adalah **Gazli dan Mubarek**," jelas Rizky. "Mereka memastikan pasokan energi untuk kebutuhan domestik maupun ekspor."

Sarah meresapi informasi itu. "Jadi, Gurun Kyzylkum dikenal luas karena kekayaan sumber daya alamnya seperti **emas, uranium, tembaga, aluminium, perak, gas alam, dan minyak bumi**. Dan industri-industri besar di sana berpusat pada pertambangan dan pengolahan sumber daya ini, dengan perusahaan seperti **НГМК dan Zarafshan-Newmont** sebagai pemain utama."

"Tepat sekali!" Rizky mengacungkan jempol. "Gurun ini mungkin terlihat tandus di permukaan, tapi di bawahnya tersimpan potensi ekonomi yang luar biasa. Ini menunjukkan bahwa setiap wilayah di bumi, bahkan yang paling ekstrem sekalipun, bisa memiliki nilai dan peran penting dalam perekonomian global."

Sarah tersenyum. Proyek geografi mereka kini jauh lebih menarik. Ia menyadari bahwa di balik keindahan dan tantangan alam, Gurun Kyzylkum adalah contoh nyata bagaimana manusia dapat memanfaatkan sumber daya alam untuk kemajuan, sambil tetap harus menjaga kelestarian lingkungan yang unik di sana. Pelajaran hari itu bukan hanya tentang geografi, tetapi juga tentang pentingnya melihat lebih dalam dan memahami potensi di setiap sudut dunia.

## The Case of the Cenwanglaoshan Canopy: A Scientific Sleuth Adventure

**Characters:**

*   **Dr. Anya Sharma:** A renowned herpetologist, enthusiastic and brilliant.
*   **Leo:** A curious and observant high school student, aspiring biologist.
*   **Maya:** A meticulous and detail-oriented high school student, a budding researcher.

**Setting:** A virtual research lab, then a simulated forest environment.

---

**Scene 1: The Virtual Lab - Decoding the Data**

**(The scene opens in a sleek, virtual lab. Dr. Sharma stands before a large holographic display showing various frog species. Leo and Maya are seated at terminals, reviewing data.)**

**Dr. Sharma:** Alright team, today we're diving into the fascinating world of the *Rhacophorus laoshan*, more commonly known as the Laoshan tree frog. We've been tasked with a crucial mission: to pinpoint its exact "type locality" and understand its physical characteristics. Think of it as a biological treasure hunt!

**Leo:** A treasure hunt! Sounds exciting, Dr. Sharma. So, what exactly is a "type locality"? Is it just… where it was found?

**Dr. Sharma:** Excellent question, Leo! In taxonomy, the "type locality" is incredibly important. It's the specific geographical place where the *type specimen* – the individual specimen upon which the scientific description of a new species is based – was originally collected. It's like the species' birthplace, its official address in the scientific world. Without it, verifying the species and its characteristics becomes much harder.

**Maya:** So, it's not just "China" or "Asia," but a much more precise location, right?

**Dr. Sharma:** Precisely, Maya! And that's where our detective work comes in. Let's look at the data. *(She gestures to the holographic display, which now shows text and images related to the Laoshan tree frog.)* Our records state: "The Laoshan tree frog (*Rhacophorus laoshan*) is a species of frog in the family Rhacophoridae. Scientists know it from the type locality: 1389 meters above sea level in Cenwangloashan Nature Reserve in China."

**Leo:** Cenwangloashan Nature Reserve… that's a mouthful! So, the type locality is within that reserve?

**Dr. Sharma:** Bingo, Leo! And not just within the reserve, but specifically at an elevation of 1389 meters above sea level. Imagine trying to find a specific tree in a vast forest – the elevation gives us a crucial vertical coordinate.

**Maya:** So, if we were to draw a map, we'd mark the Cenwangloashan Nature Reserve in China, and then within that reserve, we'd indicate a specific spot at 1389 meters.

**Dr. Sharma:** Exactly! Now, let's talk about its name. Why do you think it's called the "Laoshan tree frog"?

**Leo:** Well, it says here: "Scientists named this frog after Cenwanglaoshan Natural Preserve, where it was found." So, "Laoshan" must be a shortened version of "Cenwanglaoshan."

**Dr. Sharma:** Very good, Leo! Often, species are named after the location where they were discovered or after a prominent feature of that location. It's a way of honoring the place and making the connection clear.

---

**Scene 2: The Simulated Forest - Meeting the Laoshan Tree Frog**

**(The virtual lab dissolves, and they are now in a lush, simulated forest environment. Tall trees tower above them, and bamboo undergrowth is dense. The air is humid and filled with ambient forest sounds.)**

**Dr. Sharma:** Welcome to a simulated environment of the Cenwangloashan Nature Reserve! This is the kind of habitat where our frog thrives. Now, let's observe its characteristics.

**(A small, brown frog appears on a bamboo stalk, perfectly camouflaged.)**

**Maya:** Wow, it's quite small!

**Dr. Sharma:** Indeed it is. Now, for our second mission: determining its size. The data states: "The adult frog measures about 35 mm in snout-vent length."

**Leo:** 35 millimeters? That's tiny! Let me see… a standard ruler has centimeters. So, 35 millimeters is 3.5 centimeters.

**Maya:** To put that in perspective, that's roughly the length of a paperclip! Or, if you're thinking about a typical human hand, it's shorter than your little finger.

**Dr. Sharma:** Excellent comparisons, both of you! It's crucial to be able to visualize these measurements. This small size allows it to navigate the dense bamboo understory, where it lives.

**(The frog shifts, revealing its underside and inner legs.)**

**Leo:** Look at that! The inner surfaces of its hind legs are bright tangerine orange! That's a beautiful contrast to its brown back.

**Dr. Sharma:** That striking orange is a key identifying feature. Notice how its back, or dorsum, is brown, helping it blend into the bark and leaves. And the ventrum, its belly, is a gray-brown. These color patterns are all part of its survival strategy.

**Maya:** And it says here it lives "in the bamboo understory of forests with tall trees." That makes sense, given its size and camouflage.

**Dr. Sharma:** Absolutely. These frogs are part of the *Rhacophoridae* family, often called "shrub frogs." They're closely related to "true tree frogs" like the Hylidae. Many of them are known as "flying frogs" because of their long, webbed toes.

**Leo:** Flying frogs? Like, they actually fly?

**Dr. Sharma:** Not quite "flying" in the bird sense, Leo. But their long toes with strong webbing allow them to slow their fall to a glide – a form of arboreal locomotion we call "parachuting." It allows them to move between trees with incredible agility. Imagine leaping from a high branch and gently gliding to another!

**Maya:** So, the Laoshan tree frog, though small, is a master of its aerial environment, thanks to those specialized feet.

**Dr. Sharma:** Precisely, Maya. And they have another fascinating reproductive strategy: "aerial foam nests." They lay their eggs in these foamy nests above water. When the tadpoles hatch, they simply drop down into the water below to complete their development.

**Leo:** So, the type locality is the Cenwangloashan Nature Reserve in China, specifically at 1389 meters above sea level. And it's a tiny frog, about 35 millimeters long, with a brown back and bright orange inner hind legs, living in bamboo forests.

**Maya:** And it's named after its discovery location, the Cenwanglaoshan Preserve.

**Dr. Sharma:** You've both summarized it perfectly! You've not only identified the type locality and size of the Laoshan tree frog but also understood the significance of these details in scientific research. This is why precise observation and detailed records are so vital in biology. Every piece of information, from a specific elevation to a tiny measurement, tells a larger story about the incredible biodiversity of our planet. Keep up the excellent work, scientific sleuths!

**(The simulated forest gently fades, returning them to the virtual lab, leaving Leo and Maya with a newfound appreciation for the small but mighty Laoshan tree frog.)**

input.user_message: Create an educational story that helps students understand: What caused the crash of Yeti Airlines Flight 691 in Pokhara, Nepal?
merged_contexts:
Yeti Airlines Flight 691 was a scheduled domestic passenger flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara in Nepal. On 15 January 2023, the aircraft being operated on the route, an ATR 72 flown by Yeti Airlines, crashed while landing at Pokhara, killing all 72 occupants on board. It is the deadliest accident involving an ATR 72.

Accident
The flight took off from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport at 10:33 am NST. It crashed on the bank of the Seti Gandaki River while on final approach to landing at Pokhara International Airport. A video filmed from the ground showed the aircraft banking steeply to the left before crashing 65 metres (213 ft) away. Another video was streamed live on Facebook by Sonu Jaiswal, a passenger on the plane, before and during the crash. The video shows passengers unaware of the situation until seconds before impact.The crash occurred in Gandaki Province between the old Pokhara Airport and the new Pokhara International Airport, which was opened two weeks earlier and also where the aircraft was intending to land. The accident resulted in the deaths of all 72 people on board, and was Nepal's worst aviation accident since the crash of Pakistan International Airlines Flight 268 in 1992, the deadliest aviation accident in Nepalese domestic aviation, and the deadliest accident involving an ATR 72.According to an official at the Pokhara International Airport, air traffic control cleared the flight to land on runway 30 heading from east to west, but the captain requested the opposing runway 12 heading from west to east, minutes before the crash. A Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal spokesperson said: "The weather was clear; according to preliminary information the cause of the crash is the technical issue of the plane."Flight-tracking organisation Flightradar24 noted that during the flight the aircraft had been transmitting inaccurate speed and altitude data.

Aftermath
The airport was closed as authorities launched a rescue operation. The Government of Nepal summoned an emergency cabinet meeting following the crash. Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal said he was deeply saddened by the tragic accident. The Office of the Prime Minister declared 16 January to be a national day of mourning, and the flag of Nepal was flown at half-staff. Yeti Airlines cancelled all regular flights scheduled for the day.

Investigation
Experts noted that the video from the ground taken moments before the crash showed the aircraft's nose noticeably high before the left wing suddenly dropped, probably indicating a stall. Hours after the crash, a five-member committee headed by Nagendra Ghimire was set up to investigate the accident in conjunction with the French Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety.
On 16 January, the flight data and cockpit voice recorders were found; the recorders were examined in Singapore and with assistance from Transportation Safety Board of Canada, Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety, and Transport Safety Investigation Bureau of Singapore. About a month later, on 13 February, a preliminary report was released, which largely reproduced all relevant logs:At 10:56:27, the PF disengaged the Autopilot System (AP) at an altitude of 721 feet Above Ground Level (AGL). The PF then called for "FLAPS 30" at 10:56:32, and the PM replied, "Flaps 30 and descending". The flight data recorder (FDR) data did not record any flap surface movement at that time. Instead, the propeller rotation speed (Np) of both engines decreased simultaneously to less than 25% and the torque (Tq) started decreasing to 0%, which is consistent with both propellers going into the feathered condition...
The flight crew then carried out the "Before Landing Checklist" before starting the left turn onto the base leg. During that time, the power lever angle increased from 41% to 44%. At the point, Np of both propellers were recorded as Non-Computed Data (NCD) in the FDR and the torque (Tq) of both engines were at 0%. When propellers are in feather, they are not producing thrust...
At 10:56:54, another click was heard, followed by the flaps surface movement to the 30 degrees position.

When ATC gave the clearance for landing at 10:57:07, the PF mentioned twice that there was no power coming from the engines. At 10:57:11, the power levers were advanced first to 62 degrees then to the maximum power position. At 10:57:20, the PM (who was previously the PF) repeated again that there was no power from the engines...
The aircraft's propellers had been feathered for a minute prior to the crash, causing the engine to produce no thrust and lead the vehicle into a stall; the condition levers, which control the propellers, were discovered from the wreckage set to the feathered position. Seconds preceding the crash, the pilots discussed a total lack of power and even moved the power lever to the extreme but failed to recognize that the condition levers were wrongly set. That the condition levers and the flap lever are next to each other in an ATR 72, experts speculate that the monitoring pilot (Kamal KC) had inadvertently moved the former in place of the latter, when asked of by the flying pilot; while, about twenty seconds later, he would set the flap lever properly on his own, he failed to account for his previous mistake, implying that the landing checklist was not properly followed.

It was a tragedy that shook the world, and today, we're going to use this difficult event to learn about the complexities of aviation and how seemingly small errors can have devastating consequences."

She projected an image of the ATR 72, a sleek, twin-engine turboprop plane. "This aircraft is like a mini-city in the sky, a marvel of engineering. But even the most advanced machines rely on human precision and communication."

"The flight took off from Kathmandu, heading for the newly opened Pokhara International Airport. The weather was clear, a perfect day for flying. As they approached Pokhara, Air Traffic Control, or ATC, cleared them to land on runway 30. However, the captain requested to land on the opposite runway, runway 12. This isn't unusual, sometimes pilots prefer a different approach due to wind or other factors."

Ms. Sharma then brought up a diagram of the aircraft's cockpit, focusing on the control panel. "Now, here's where things get critical. In an ATR 72, there are two important sets of levers close to each other: the **flap levers** and the **condition levers**. The flap levers control the flaps on the wings, which help the plane slow down and generate lift during landing. The condition levers, on the other hand, control the propellers – specifically, whether they're generating thrust or 'feathered'."

She paused, letting the information sink in. "When propellers are 'feathered,' they are essentially turned sideways to the airflow. Imagine holding your hand flat against the wind versus turning it edgewise. Feathering reduces drag, but crucially, it also means the engine is no longer producing thrust. It’s like putting a car in neutral and letting it coast, except in the air, you need continuous thrust to maintain altitude and control."

"The preliminary investigation revealed a series of events that led to the crash. As the plane was preparing to land, at about 721 feet above the ground, the pilot flying, or PF, disengaged the autopilot. They then called for 'FLAPS 30,' meaning they wanted the flaps extended to 30 degrees for landing."

Ms. Sharma pointed to a timeline on the screen. "Here's the crucial part: the flight data recorder, which records everything happening on the plane, showed that the flaps *didn't* move at that moment. Instead, the propeller rotation speed of *both* engines dropped dramatically, and their torque – the twisting force they produce – went to zero. This is exactly what happens when the propellers are feathered."

A student raised their hand. "So, the pilot asked for flaps, but something else happened instead?"

"Precisely," Ms. Sharma confirmed. "Experts speculate that the monitoring pilot, who was responsible for cross-checking actions, might have inadvertently moved the **condition levers** into the feathered position, mistaking them for the flap levers. Remember, they are located very close together."

"For almost a minute," she continued, "the aircraft's propellers were feathered. This meant the engines were no longer providing thrust. The plane was essentially gliding, rapidly losing airspeed and altitude. The pilots, understandably, were trying to figure out why they had no power."

She showed a short, animated clip of a plane losing thrust and its nose pitching up, then dropping. "The videos from the ground show the aircraft's nose getting noticeably high, a classic sign of a plane losing speed and approaching a 'stall.' A stall isn't when an engine dies; it's when the wings can no longer generate enough lift to keep the plane in the air. When the left wing suddenly dropped, that's a strong indication of a stall."

"Even as ATC cleared them to land," Ms. Sharma explained, "the pilots were heard repeatedly saying there was 'no power coming from the engines.' They advanced the power levers to maximum, but it made no difference because the condition levers, which control the propellers' thrust, were still in the feathered position. They failed to recognize this critical mistake."

"About twenty seconds after the initial error, the monitoring pilot *did* eventually set the flap lever correctly. But by then, it was too late. The aircraft was too low, too slow, and had lost too much energy. The lack of thrust and the subsequent stall led to the plane banking steeply to the left and crashing."

"This tragic accident highlights several key learning points," Ms. Sharma concluded. "Firstly, the importance of **human factors** in aviation. Even highly trained pilots can make errors, especially under pressure. Secondly, the critical role of **crew resource management (CRM)** – effective communication and cross-checking among the pilots. If the mistake with the condition levers had been immediately identified and corrected, the outcome might have been different. Thirdly, it underscores the need for **rigorous checklists** and adherence to procedures, especially during critical phases of flight like landing. And finally, it shows how a seemingly minor confusion between two levers, combined with a lack of immediate recognition, can have catastrophic consequences."

The classroom was silent now, a different kind of quiet. The students had understood. The crash of Yeti Airlines Flight 691 wasn't a simple technical failure, but a complex chain of events, a chilling reminder of the delicate balance between human action and machine precision in the skies.

contexts:
Yeti Airlines Flight 691 was a scheduled domestic passenger flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara in Nepal. On 15 January 2023, the aircraft being operated on the route, an ATR 72 flown by Yeti Airlines, crashed while landing at Pokhara, killing all 72 occupants on board. It is the deadliest accident involving an ATR 72.

Accident
The flight took off from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport at 10:33 am NST. It crashed on the bank of the Seti Gandaki River while on final approach to landing at Pokhara International Airport. A video filmed from the ground showed the aircraft banking steeply to the left before crashing 65 metres (213 ft) away. Another video was streamed live on Facebook by Sonu Jaiswal, a passenger on the plane, before and during the crash. The video shows passengers unaware of the situation until seconds before impact.The crash occurred in Gandaki Province between the old Pokhara Airport and the new Pokhara International Airport, which was opened two weeks earlier and also where the aircraft was intending to land. The accident resulted in the deaths of all 72 people on board, and was Nepal's worst aviation accident since the crash of Pakistan International Airlines Flight 268 in 1992, the deadliest aviation accident in Nepalese domestic aviation, and the deadliest accident involving an ATR 72.According to an official at the Pokhara International Airport, air traffic control cleared the flight to land on runway 30 heading from east to west, but the captain requested the opposing runway 12 heading from west to east, minutes before the crash. A Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal spokesperson said: "The weather was clear; according to preliminary information the cause of the crash is the technical issue of the plane."Flight-tracking organisation Flightradar24 noted that during the flight the aircraft had been transmitting inaccurate speed and altitude data.

Aftermath
The airport was closed as authorities launched a rescue operation. The Government of Nepal summoned an emergency cabinet meeting following the crash. Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal said he was deeply saddened by the tragic accident. The Office of the Prime Minister declared 16 January to be a national day of mourning, and the flag of Nepal was flown at half-staff. Yeti Airlines cancelled all regular flights scheduled for the day.

Investigation
Experts noted that the video from the ground taken moments before the crash showed the aircraft's nose noticeably high before the left wing suddenly dropped, probably indicating a stall. Hours after the crash, a five-member committee headed by Nagendra Ghimire was set up to investigate the accident in conjunction with the French Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety.
On 16 January, the flight data and cockpit voice recorders were found; the recorders were examined in Singapore and with assistance from Transportation Safety Board of Canada, Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety, and Transport Safety Investigation Bureau of Singapore. About a month later, on 13 February, a preliminary report was released, which largely reproduced all relevant logs:At 10:56:27, the PF disengaged the Autopilot System (AP) at an altitude of 721 feet Above Ground Level (AGL). The PF then called for "FLAPS 30" at 10:56:32, and the PM replied, "Flaps 30 and descending". The flight data recorder (FDR) data did not record any flap surface movement at that time. Instead, the propeller rotation speed (Np) of both engines decreased simultaneously to less than 25% and the torque (Tq) started decreasing to 0%, which is consistent with both propellers going into the feathered condition...
The flight crew then carried out the "Before Landing Checklist" before starting the left turn onto the base leg. During that time, the power lever angle increased from 41% to 44%. At the point, Np of both propellers were recorded as Non-Computed Data (NCD) in the FDR and the torque (Tq) of both engines were at 0%. When propellers are in feather, they are not producing thrust...
At 10:56:54, another click was heard, followed by the flaps surface movement to the 30 degrees position.

When ATC gave the clearance for landing at 10:57:07, the PF mentioned twice that there was no power coming from the engines. At 10:57:11, the power levers were advanced first to 62 degrees then to the maximum power position. At 10:57:20, the PM (who was previously the PF) repeated again that there was no power from the engines...
The aircraft's propellers had been feathered for a minute prior to the crash, causing the engine to produce no thrust and lead the vehicle into a stall; the condition levers, which control the propellers, were discovered from the wreckage set to the feathered position. Seconds preceding the crash, the pilots discussed a total lack of power and even moved the power lever to the extreme but failed to recognize that the condition levers were wrongly set. That the condition levers and the flap lever are next to each other in an ATR 72, experts speculate that the monitoring pilot (Kamal KC) had inadvertently moved the former in place of the latter, when asked of by the flying pilot; while, about twenty seconds later, he would set the flap lever properly on his own, he failed to account for his previous mistake, implying that the landing checklist was not properly followed.

Tentu, mari kita selami dunia perfilman dan sejarah dengan cerita edukatif ini!

***

**Misteri di Balik Layar: Proyek Oppenheimer**

Angin sejuk berhembus di koridor SMA Bhinneka, membawa aroma buku-buku lama dan semangat belajar. Di salah satu ruang kelas, Bu Ratna, guru Sejarah yang terkenal dengan metode mengajarnya yang interaktif, tersenyum kepada murid-muridnya. Hari ini, mereka akan membahas sesuatu yang sedikit berbeda: sejarah melalui lensa sinema.

"Baik, anak-anak," Bu Ratna memulai, "siapa di antara kalian yang pernah mendengar tentang J. Robert Oppenheimer?"

Beberapa tangan terangkat. "Dia ilmuwan yang terlibat dalam pembuatan bom atom, Bu!" seru Rio, si kutu buku kelas.

"Tepat sekali, Rio!" Bu Ratna mengangguk. "Dan baru-baru ini, ada film epik yang mengisahkan hidupnya. Judulnya *Oppenheimer*."

Mata para siswa berbinar. Film selalu menjadi topik menarik.

"Nah, Bu," tanya Sinta, siswi yang selalu penasaran, "saya dengar filmnya bagus sekali. Siapa sih yang menyutradarai film sebesar itu? Pasti orang yang sangat berbakat."

Bu Ratna tersenyum misterius. "Pertanyaan bagus, Sinta. Film *Oppenheimer* adalah sebuah karya besar yang membutuhkan visi seorang sutradara jenius. Sutradara yang berhasil membawa kisah kompleks J. Robert Oppenheimer ke layar lebar dengan begitu mendalam dan memukau adalah **Christopher Nolan**."

"Christopher Nolan?" Rendi, si penggemar film, berseru kaget. "Wow! Sutradara yang membuat *Inception*, *The Dark Knight*, dan *Interstellar* itu, Bu? Pantas saja filmnya begitu dinanti!"

"Betul sekali, Rendi," Bu Ratna membenarkan. "Nolan dikenal dengan gaya penyutradaraannya yang unik, alur cerita non-linear, dan visual yang memukau. Ia adalah orang di balik naskah dan penyutradaraan *Oppenheimer*, berdasarkan biografi *American Prometheus*."

"Lalu, Bu," giliran Yoga bertanya, "siapa yang memerankan Oppenheimer sendiri? Untuk peran sepenting itu, pasti aktornya harus benar-benar bisa menjiwai."

"Itu juga pertanyaan yang sangat penting, Yoga," Bu Ratna mengangguk. "Memerankan sosok sekompleks J. Robert Oppenheimer, seorang fisikawan teoretis yang memimpin Proyek Manhattan dan dijuluki 'Bapak Bom Atom', tentu bukan tugas mudah. Aktor yang berhasil menghidupkan karakter tersebut dengan sangat brilian adalah **Cillian Murphy**."

"Cillian Murphy?" beberapa siswa bergumam. "Oh, yang main di *Peaky Blinders* itu ya, Bu?" tanya Dini.

"Tepat sekali, Dini!" Bu Ratna menganggakan. "Cillian Murphy adalah aktor Irlandia yang dikenal dengan aktingnya yang intens dan karismatik. Ia berhasil menangkap esensi dari Oppenheimer, mulai dari kecerdasannya yang luar biasa, dilema moral yang dihadapinya, hingga beban sejarah yang ia pikul."

Bu Ratna melanjutkan, "Dalam film itu, ia tidak sendirian. Ada Emily Blunt yang berperan sebagai istrinya, Katherine 'Kitty' Oppenheimer. Lalu ada Matt Damon sebagai Jenderal Leslie Groves, direktur Proyek Manhattan, dan Robert Downey Jr. sebagai Lewis Strauss, anggota senior Komisi Energi Atom Amerika Serikat."

"Jadi, film ini bukan hanya tentang Oppenheimer saja, tapi juga tentang orang-orang di sekelilingnya yang membentuk sejarah," kata Rio, merangkum.

"Persis!" Bu Ratna tersenyum puas. "Film *Oppenheimer* adalah contoh bagaimana sinema bisa menjadi jembatan menuju pemahaman sejarah yang lebih mendalam. Dengan mengetahui siapa sutradaranya, Christopher Nolan, dan siapa aktor utamanya, Cillian Murphy, kita bisa lebih menghargai kerja keras dan visi di balik layar yang menghadirkan kisah ini kepada kita."

"Bu, kalau begitu, saya jadi ingin menonton filmnya!" seru Sinta bersemangat.

"Saya juga!" tambah Rendi dan Yoga.

"Bagus sekali!" Bu Ratna tersenyum. "Ingat, film bukan hanya hiburan, tapi juga bisa menjadi sumber belajar yang luar biasa. **Misteri di Balik Layar: Proyek Oppenheimer**

Angin sejuk berhembus di koridor SMA Bhinneka, membawa aroma buku-buku lama dan semangat belajar. Di salah satu ruang kelas, Bu Ratna, guru Sejarah yang terkenal dengan metode mengajarnya yang interaktif, tersenyum kepada murid-muridnya. Hari ini, mereka akan membahas sesuatu yang sedikit berbeda: sejarah melalui lensa sinema.

"Baik, anak-anak," Bu Ratna memulai, "siapa di antara kalian yang pernah mendengar tentang J. Robert Oppenheimer?"

Beberapa tangan terangkat. "Dia ilmuwan yang terlibat dalam pembuatan bom atom, Bu!" seru Rio, si kutu buku kelas.

"Tepat sekali, Rio!" Bu Ratna mengangguk. "Dan baru-baru ini, ada film epik yang mengisahkan hidupnya. Judulnya *Oppenheimer*."

Mata para siswa berbinar. Film selalu menjadi topik menarik.

"Nah, Bu," tanya Sinta, siswi yang selalu penasaran, "saya dengar filmnya bagus sekali. Siapa sih yang menyutradarai film sebesar itu? Pasti orang yang sangat berbakat."

Bu Ratna tersenyum misterius. "Pertanyaan bagus, Sinta. Film *Oppenheimer* adalah sebuah karya besar yang membutuhkan visi seorang sutradara jenius. Sutradara yang berhasil membawa kisah kompleks J. Robert Oppenheimer ke layar lebar dengan begitu mendalam dan memukau adalah **Christopher Nolan**."

"Christopher Nolan?" Rendi, si penggemar film, berseru kaget. "Wow! Sutradara yang membuat *Inception*, *The Dark Knight*, dan *Interstellar* itu, Bu? Pantas saja filmnya begitu dinanti!"

"Betul sekali, Rendi," Bu Ratna membenarkan. "Nolan dikenal dengan gaya penyutradaraannya yang unik, alur cerita non-linear, dan visual yang memukau. Ia adalah orang di balik naskah dan penyutradaraan *Oppenheimer*, berdasarkan biografi *American Prometheus*."

"Lalu, Bu," giliran Yoga bertanya, "siapa yang memerankan Oppenheimer sendiri? Untuk peran sepenting itu, pasti aktornya harus benar-benar bisa menjiwai."

"Itu juga pertanyaan yang sangat penting, Yoga," Bu Ratna mengangguk. "Memerankan sosok sekompleks J. Robert Oppenheimer, seorang fisikawan teoretis yang memimpin Proyek Manhattan dan dijuluki 'Bapak Bom Atom', tentu bukan tugas mudah. Aktor yang berhasil menghidupkan karakter tersebut dengan sangat brilian adalah **Cillian Murphy**."

"Cillian Murphy?" beberapa siswa bergumam. "Oh, yang main di *Peaky Blinders* itu ya, Bu?" tanya Dini.

"Tepat sekali, Dini!" Bu Ratna menganggakan. "Cillian Murphy adalah aktor Irlandia yang dikenal dengan aktingnya yang intens dan karismatik. Ia berhasil menangkap esensi dari Oppenheimer, mulai dari kecerdasannya yang luar biasa, dilema moral yang dihadapinya, hingga beban sejarah yang ia pikul."

Bu Ratna melanjutkan, "Dalam film itu, ia tidak sendirian. Ada Emily Blunt yang berperan sebagai istrinya, Katherine 'Kitty' Oppenheimer. Lalu ada Matt Damon sebagai Jenderal Leslie Groves, direktur Proyek Manhattan, dan Robert Downey Jr. sebagai Lewis Strauss, anggota senior Komisi Energi Atom Amerika Serikat."

"Jadi, film ini bukan hanya tentang Oppenheimer saja, tapi juga tentang orang-orang di sekelilingnya yang membentuk sejarah," kata Rio, merangkum.

"Persis!" Bu Ratna tersenyum puas. "Film *Oppenheimer* adalah contoh bagaimana sinema bisa menjadi jembatan menuju pemahaman sejarah yang lebih mendalam. Dengan mengetahui siapa sutradaranya, Christopher Nolan, dan siapa aktor utamanya, Cillian Murphy, kita bisa lebih menghargai kerja keras dan visi di balik layar yang menghadirkan kisah ini kepada kita."

"Bu, kalau begitu, saya jadi ingin menonton filmnya!" seru Sinta bersemangat.

"Saya juga!" tambah Rendi dan Yoga.

"Bagus sekali!" Bu Ratna tersenyum. "Ingat, film bukan hanya hiburan, tapi juga bisa menjadi sumber belajar yang luar biasa. Setelah menontonnya, kita bisa berdiskusi lebih lanjut tentang implikasi sejarah dan etika di balik Proyek Manhattan. Siapa tahu, kalian juga bisa menemukan inspirasi untuk menjadi pembuat film atau sejarawan di masa depan!"

Para siswa mengangguk, dengan pemahaman baru tentang kekuatan sinema dan tokoh-tokoh penting di baliknya. Misteri di balik layar *Oppenheimer* kini terungkap, membuka gerbang menuju diskusi yang lebih kaya dan mendalam.

The Inter Expo Center (IEC) is a multi-purpose convention center in Sofia, Bulgaria. It consists of six exhibition halls, eight congress halls, and outdoor exhibition spaces. The center is the biggest convention and exhibition venue in the city.

History
The Inter Expo Center opened in 2001, initially featuring two exhibition halls and outdoor exhibition spaces alongside leasable office and trade spaces in an office tower above the halls and in public areas around the main entrance facing the street.The center had its first expansion in 2003, adding a congress center featuring eight congress halls, as well as an additional exhibition hall. In 2008, the center was expanded again with the opening of further exhibition halls. The Inter Expo Center – Tsarigradsko shose Metro Station, part of the Sofia Metro, opened in April 2012. Originally named the Tsarigradsko shose Metro Station, it was renamed to bear the convention center's name less than two months later.The congress halls were renovated in 2019, which was considered the biggest update to the center since its last expansion.

"Paman, aku sedang mengerjakan proyek sekolah tentang infrastruktur penting di Bulgaria," kata Anya, menutup buku catatannya. "Aku tertarik dengan Inter Expo Center. Dimitar tersenyum. "Ah, Inter Expo Center (IEC)! Itu adalah salah satu kebanggaan Sofia, Anya. Tempat itu bukan hanya sekadar gedung, tapi jantung kegiatan bisnis dan budaya."

"Jantung?" Anya mengangkat alisnya. "Kedengarannya dramatis sekali, Paman."

"Memang begitu," jawab Dimitar. "Bayangkan, sebelum ada IEC, Sofia kekurangan tempat yang representatif untuk pameran besar dan konferensi internasional. Jadi, pembangunannya adalah langkah maju yang sangat penting bagi kota ini."

"Jadi, kapan langkah maju itu dimulai?" tanya Anya, siap mencatat.

"**Inter Expo Center pertama kali dibuka pada tahun 2001**," kata Dimitar. "Waktu itu, fasilitasnya lebih sederhana dari yang kamu lihat sekarang. Awalnya, hanya ada dua aula pameran dan beberapa area pameran di luar ruangan. Di atas aula-aula itu, ada juga menara perkantoran yang disewakan, dan area komersial di sekitar pintu masuk utama."

Anya mencatat dengan cepat. "Jadi, dua aula pameran dan area perkantoran. Itu permulaan yang cukup sederhana untuk tempat sebesar sekarang."

"Tepat sekali. Tapi sebuah visi besar tidak pernah berhenti berkembang," lanjut Dimitar. "Tidak butuh waktu lama, IEC menyadari potensi dan kebutuhan yang terus meningkat. Jadi, hanya dua tahun kemudian, **pada tahun 2003, mereka melakukan perluasan pertama mereka.**"

"Perluasan apa, Paman?"

"Mereka menambahkan sebuah pusat kongres baru yang dilengkapi dengan delapan aula kongres," Dimitar menjelaskan. "Ini sangat penting, karena memungkinkan IEC untuk tidak hanya menjadi tempat pameran, tetapi juga menjadi tuan rumah konferensi, seminar, dan pertemuan bisnis berskala besar. Selain itu, mereka juga menambah satu aula pameran lagi."

Anya mengangguk. "Jadi, dari dua menjadi tiga aula pameran, dan delapan aula kongres. Itu peningkatan yang signifikan."

"Tentu saja. Dan pertumbuhan itu tidak berhenti di situ," kata Dimitar. "Kebutuhan akan ruang pameran terus meningkat, sehingga **pada tahun 2008, IEC diperluas lagi dengan pembukaan aula-aula pameran tambahan.** Sayangnya, aku tidak ingat persis berapa banyak, tapi yang jelas, itu menambah kapasitas mereka secara drastis."

"Wow, jadi berkembang terus-menerus," kata Anya, mulai memahami skala proyek ini. "Paman, apakah ada hal lain yang menarik tentang perluasannya?"

"Ada, dan ini sangat penting untuk aksesibilitas," jawab Dimitar. "Bayangkan sebuah pusat konvensi besar, tapi sulit dijangkau. Itu akan mengurangi efektivitasnya. Jadi, pada **April 2012, sebuah stasiun metro baru dibuka sebagai bagian dari Sofia Metro, tepat di dekat IEC.** Awalnya dinamai Tsarigradsko shose Metro Station, tapi kurang dari dua bulan kemudian, namanya diubah menjadi Inter Expo Center – Tsarigradsko shose Metro Station. Ini menunjukkan betapa pentingnya pusat ini bagi kota."

"Itu cerdas sekali!" seru Anya. "Membuatnya mudah diakses adalah kunci."

"Betul," Dimitar setuju. "Dan yang terakhir, tapi tidak kalah penting, adalah pembaruan yang terjadi baru-baru ini. Meskipun bukan perluasan fisik dengan menambah gedung baru, **pada tahun 2019, aula-aula kongres direnovasi secara menyeluruh.** Ini dianggap sebagai pembaruan terbesar bagi pusat ini sejak perluasan terakhirnya di tahun 2008. Renovasi ini memastikan fasilitas tetap modern, nyaman, dan mampu memenuhi standar internasional."

Anya menutup buku catatannya dengan senyum puas. "Jadi, dimulai pada tahun 2001 dengan dua aula, lalu perluasan di tahun 2003 dengan delapan aula kongres dan satu aula pameran lagi. Kemudian perluasan aula pameran lagi di tahun 2008. Lalu stasiun metro di tahun 2012, dan renovasi besar di tahun 2019. Itu adalah perjalanan yang luar biasa!"

"Memang begitu, Anya," kata Dimitar. "Dari dua aula pameran sederhana, sekarang IEC memiliki enam aula pameran, delapan aula kongres, dan area pameran luar ruangan. Ditambah lagi menara perkantoran, restoran, dan akses metro yang mudah. Ini adalah bukti bagaimana sebuah visi bisa tumbuh dan beradaptasi untuk menjadi pusat konvensi dan pameran terbesar di Sofia."

## The Countdown to Singapore's Eyes in the Sky: A PSLV-C56 Story

The hum of excitement was palpable in the corridors of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). Rohan, a bright-eyed intern in his final year of astrophysics, felt a thrill course through him as he reviewed the mission brief for PSLV-C56. He’d always been fascinated by rockets, but being on the ground, even as an intern, made it all feel incredibly real.

His mentor, Dr. Anya Sharma, a veteran in satellite operations, noticed his focused gaze. "Penny for your thoughts, Rohan?" she asked, a warm smile on her face.

Rohan looked up. "Just trying to absorb all the details for PSLV-C56, Dr. Sharma. It's… a lot of information, but so exciting!"

Dr. Sharma chuckled. "It certainly is. Every launch is a symphony of science, engineering, and sheer determination. Let's break it down, shall we? Think of it as a story, Rohan. Every story needs a beginning – a time and a place."

She pulled up a holographic display, showing a sleek rocket standing tall against a blue sky. "So, Rohan, when is this particular story, this PSLV-C56 mission, scheduled to begin?"

Rohan's eyes scanned the brief. "Ah, yes! It's scheduled for **Sunday, July 30th, 2023**."

"Excellent! And what about the precise moment of liftoff? We need to be very specific with rocket launches, don't we?" Dr. Sharma prompted.

"Absolutely! It's at **06:30 IST – Indian Standard Time**. Or, for our international partners, that's **01:00 UTC, Coordinated Universal Time**," Rohan replied, feeling a surge of confidence.

"Precisely," Dr. Sharma nodded. "Now, every story also needs a setting, a stage where the magic happens. Where will this magnificent rocket, our PSLV-C56, begin its journey to the stars?"

Rohan zoomed in on the holographic map. "It's launching from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, India**." He then added, remembering a detail from the briefing, "More specifically, from the **First Launch Pad, or FLP**."

"Very good, Rohan! You're paying attention to the finer points," Dr. Sharma praised. "Now, let's put this into context. Do you remember what PSLV stands for, and why this particular mission is significant?"

Rohan thought for a moment. "PSLV is the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle**. This is the **58th mission of ISRO's PSLV** program, and the **17th flight of the PSLV-CA variant**. It's a dedicated commercial mission through NSIL, carrying DS-SAR as the primary satellite, and VELOX-AM as a co-passenger, along with five other satellites. All of them, I believe, are from Singapore."

"Spot on!" Dr. Sharma beamed. "This mission is a testament to India's growing capabilities in providing reliable and cost-effective launch services to other nations. Singapore is entrusting us with their eyes in the sky, so to speak, to help them with various applications like disaster monitoring, urban planning, and maritime safety."

Rohan felt a renewed sense of purpose. "It's incredible to think about the journey these satellites will take, all starting from that specific time and place. From the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, on Sunday, July 30th, 2023, at 06:30 IST, these satellites will embark on a mission to gather vital data for a whole other country."

Dr. Sharma placed a hand on his shoulder. "That's the beauty of space exploration, Rohan. It's about pushing boundaries, fostering international cooperation, and ultimately, using technology to benefit humanity. And you, even as an intern, are a part of this incredible story."

As Rohan continued to study the mission brief, the once-daunting information had transformed into a vivid narrative. He could almost hear the roar of the engines, see the plume of smoke, and feel the ground tremble as PSLV-C56, carrying Singapore's hopes, ascended into the dawn sky from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre. He knew now, with absolute clarity, when and where this significant chapter in space exploration was set to begin.

merged_contexts:
The Zubaydah Trail (Al-Kufi pilgrimage route) is among the seven major pilgrimage routes in the Arabian Peninsula, dating back over 1000 years. A crucial trade route during the Abbasid era, it is a strong candidate for the UNESCO World Heritage List. This historical trail was constructed to serve pilgrims from Iraq, neighbouring Islamic countries, and East Asian countries.
Its construction was completed during the Abbasid Caliphate, specifically between 132 AH (750 CE) and 656 AH (1258 CE). 
The trail's history dates back to the pre-Islamic era, when it was used by tribes, travellers, and commercial caravans to move between Iraq and Western Arabia. Over time, its usage became regular and easier as the water centres, grazing areas, and mining locations along the route transformed into major stations.
During the Abbasid era, the trail served as an important link between Baghdad, the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, and the rest of the Arabian Peninsula. The Abbasid caliphs took great interest in the trail, enhanced it with various benefits and facilities, as well as undertook an expansion of the road to make it suitable for use by pilgrims, travellers, and their animals.Historical, geographical, and archaeological sources show that the trail route was designed in a practical and meticulous manner. Along its length from Kufa to Mecca, stations, houses, and resting areas were established. Its surface was paved with stones in sandy and muddy areas. In addition, it was equipped with necessary amenities and facilities such as wells, ponds, and dams. Signages, lighthouses, beacons, and stoves were also set up to mark its path and guide travellers.The Zubaydah Trail stretches over a distance of 1,300 kilometres and is connected to 27 main stations, most of which are concentrated in Saudi Arabia. Furthermore, 58 subsidiary stations called Muta'asha, which are rest stops, were established between every two main stations. The average distance between each main station and the next is approximately 50 kilometres.

The desert wind whipped around Tariq, stinging his eyes with fine sand. He adjusted the brim of his keffiyeh, his gaze fixed on the horizon. Ahead, a mirage shimmered, teasing him with the promise of water. This was his first pilgrimage, and the journey from Baghdad to Mecca was proving to be a grueling test of endurance.

"Hard work, isn't it, young one?" A weathered voice broke his thoughts. An older man, his face etched with the sun and wisdom of many journeys, sat beside him. "The desert cares little for the comfort of man."

Tariq nodded, his throat dry. "Indeed, sir. I can only imagine what it must have been like centuries ago, before… well, before there were even clear paths."

The old man chuckled, a dry, raspy sound. "Ah, but there *were* paths, Tariq. And one of the most remarkable was built precisely to ease the suffering of pilgrims like us. Have you ever heard of the Zubaydah Trail?"

Tariq shook his head. "I don't think so."

"Then let me tell you a story," the old man began, leaning back against a sun-baked rock. "A story of perseverance, faith, and a queen who left an enduring legacy."

"Imagine, Tariq, a time over a thousand years ago. The Abbasid Caliphate was at its peak, and Baghdad was a dazzling center of learning and trade. But even then, the journey to the holy cities of Mecca and Medina was fraught with peril. Tribes and traders had always crisscrossed these lands, following ancient routes to find water and sustenance. These were informal paths, often difficult to navigate, especially for large groups of pilgrims."

"So, when was this Zubaydah Trail constructed, then?" Tariq asked, intrigued.

"It wasn't a single event, like building a house," the old man explained. "Think of it more as a grand project that unfolded over many centuries. The Abbasid Caliphate itself began in **132 AH, which is around 750 CE**. And this monumental undertaking, the construction and enhancement of the Zubaydah Trail, continued throughout their reign, right up until **656 AH, or 1258 CE**. So, we're talking about a period of over 500 years where this trail was meticulously developed and maintained."

"Five hundred years!" Tariq exclaimed. "That's incredible. But who was Zubaydah, and why is it named after her?"

"Ah, now we come to the heart of the story," the old man said, a glint in his eye. "The trail is named after **Queen Zubaydah**, a woman of extraordinary compassion and influence. She was the daughter of Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur and, crucially, the wife of the legendary Caliph Harun al-Rashid. You see, in **176 AH**, Queen Zubaydah herself embarked on the Hajj pilgrimage. And let me tell you, Tariq, she experienced firsthand the immense hardships of that journey."

"She saw the suffering of pilgrims, the lack of reliable water, the scorching sun, and the treacherous terrain. It deeply moved her. And unlike many, she didn't just lament the situation; she acted. She, along with her husband, dedicated a significant portion of their immense wealth to improving the pilgrimage route. She ordered the construction of well-organized rest areas, strategically placed ponds to collect precious rainwater, and even canals to channel water. She understood that a safe and accessible path was not just a convenience, but a necessity for the faithful."

"So, the trail existed before her, but she transformed it?" Tariq clarified.

"Precisely!" the old man affirmed. "The route itself had been used for centuries, even before Islam, by various tribes and merchants. It was a natural corridor between Iraq and Western Arabia. Over time, as those ancient water sources and grazing lands became more established, they naturally became stopping points. But it was during the Abbasid era, and largely thanks to Queen Zubaydah's vision and dedication, that this informal path became a meticulously planned and engineered highway of faith."

"The Abbasid Caliphs, recognizing the importance of the Hajj, took a keen interest in this route. They weren't just building a road; they were building a lifeline. They expanded it, making it suitable not just for people, but for their animals too. Imagine, Tariq, a path stretching **1,300 kilometers** from Kufa in Iraq all the way to Mecca! Along this vast distance, they established **27 main stations**, like small towns, providing shelter and supplies. And between these main stations, every 50 kilometers or so, they built **58 subsidiary stations, called Muta'asha**, which were essential rest stops."

"They didn't just build a path, Tariq. They engineered a wonder. In sandy and muddy areas, they paved the surface with stones. They dug wells, built dams, and constructed ponds to ensure a constant supply of water. They even put up signposts, lighthouses, beacons, and stoves to mark the way and guide travelers, even at night."

Tariq looked around at the barren landscape, then back at the old man. "It's hard to imagine such a sophisticated infrastructure in such a remote area, so long ago."

"That, my boy, is the genius of it," the old man said with a smile. "The Zubaydah Trail, also known as the Al-Kufi pilgrimage route, is one of seven major pilgrimage routes in the Arabian Peninsula. It served not only pilgrims from Iraq, but also from neighboring Islamic countries and even as far as East Asia. It was a crucial trade route as well, connecting Baghdad to the holy cities and the wider Arabian Peninsula."

"And even today," the old man continued, "this historical trail is recognized for its incredible significance. It's a strong candidate for the UNESCO World Heritage List, a testament to its enduring legacy. It stands as a powerful reminder of human ingenuity, faith, and the desire to make the world a better, more accessible place for all."

Tariq felt a new sense of awe. The discomfort of the journey seemed to lessen, replaced by a profound respect for those who had come before him, and especially for the queen whose compassion had paved the way. He realized he wasn't just walking across a desert; he was walking along a living testament to history, a path shaped by faith and foresight, a path that still whispers the name of Zubaydah in the desert winds.

The Roanoke and Tar River Railroad was fully merged into the Seaboard Air Line in 1911. The CSX Corporation initially operated the Chessie and Seaboard Systems separately until 1986, when they were merged into CSX Transportation.
The southernmost five miles of the line from Kelford to Lewiston was abandoned sometime after 1986.  The remaining line from Boykins to Kelford was sold to the North Carolina and Virginia Railroad in 1987, who operates the line today.

## The Vanishing Rails of the Roanoke and Tar River: A Railway Saga

**Characters:**

* **Professor Anya Sharma:** A history and railway enthusiast, engaging and insightful.
* **Lena:** A curious and observant student.
* **Marcus:** A strategic thinker, always looking for connections.
* **Chloe:** A detail-oriented student, good at remembering dates.

**(Scene: A classroom, filled with maps and old railway photographs. Professor Sharma stands by a whiteboard, a timeline sketched across it.)**

**Professor Sharma:** Good morning, aspiring historians! Today, we’re embarking on a journey through time, following the tracks of a rather intriguing, though often overlooked, piece of railway history: the Roanoke and Tar River Railroad. Lena, Marcus, Chloe, ready to explore?

**Lena:** Always, Professor! Railways always have such fascinating stories.

**Marcus:** Especially when they involve mergers and corporate shifts. It’s like a game of strategic alliances.

**Chloe:** And I’m ready to keep track of all the important dates!

**Professor Sharma:** Excellent! Let’s start at the beginning. Imagine North Carolina in the late 19th century. The need for better transportation to move goods and people was growing. In 1871, the North Carolina State Legislature chartered the Roanoke and Tar River Railroad. But, as often happens with big projects, it sat dormant for a while.

**Marcus:** So, a charter doesn’t always mean immediate construction?

**Professor Sharma:** Precisely. It wasn't until 1885 that the charter was reissued, breathing new life into the project. This time, it wasn't just a hopeful idea. The Roanoke and Tar River Railroad was designed to operate as a subsidiary of a larger, more established player: the Seaboard and Roanoke Railroad. Think of it like a smaller company being supported by a bigger one, sharing resources and connections. Their goal was to build a 36-mile line from Boykins, Virginia, south to Lewiston, North Carolina.

**Lena:** So, it was connected to a bigger network right from the start?

**Professor Sharma:** Yes, that connection at Boykins was crucial. Construction finally began in 1887 and, remarkably, was completed just a year later. They were efficient! Now, things get a little more complex. In 1892, another small railway, the Murfreesboro Railroad, was built. It branched off our Roanoke and Tar River line at a place called Pendleton and ran to Murfreesboro.

**Chloe:** So, a branch off a subsidiary? That’s getting nested!

**Professor Sharma:** Indeed! And in 1893, the Roanoke and Tar River Railroad acquired the Murfreesboro Railroad, operating it as its own branch line. It seemed like a good expansion, connecting more towns. However, this branch line’s story takes a rather dramatic turn. By 1897, the Roanoke and Tar River decided to discontinue service on the Murfreesboro branch.

**Marcus:** Why would they do that? Was it unprofitable?

**Professor Sharma:** Likely. Operating and maintaining a railway is expensive. The town of Murfreesboro was, understandably, quite upset. They tried to prevent the abandonment. But, in a move that sounds like something out of a suspense novel, in the late evening of May 7, 1897, the company removed the branch's tracks... in the dark of the night!

**Lena:** Wow! That’s a pretty bold move. No one could stop them if they did it at night.

**Professor Sharma:** A very effective, if somewhat underhanded, tactic. It highlights the power dynamics at play in those days. But let’s fast forward a bit. The railway landscape was constantly shifting. By the end of the 1800s, the larger parent company, the Seaboard and Roanoke Railroad, became part of a much bigger entity: the Seaboard Air Line Railway network.

**Chloe:** So, the Roanoke and Tar River was now a subsidiary of a subsidiary of a much bigger railway?

**Professor Sharma:** You’ve got it, Chloe! This brings us to a key question: **When was the Roanoke and Tar River Railroad fully merged into the Seaboard Air Line Railway network?**

**(Professor Sharma pauses, looking at the students expectantly.)**

**Marcus:** So, the Seaboard Air Line was forming its larger network… it makes sense they’d want to consolidate their holdings.

**Lena:** And the Roanoke and Tar River was already connected to them through the Seaboard and Roanoke.

**Chloe:** I remember seeing that date in our readings! It was quite a while after the Seaboard Air Line itself was established.

**Professor Sharma:** Give us the date, Chloe!

**Chloe:** The Roanoke and Tar River Railroad was **fully merged into the Seaboard Air Line in 1911.**

**Professor Sharma:** Excellent! That’s the answer to our first question. From that point on, the Roanoke and Tar River Railroad ceased to be an independent entity, even as a subsidiary. It operated as the Seaboard Air Line's **Lewiston Subdivision**. It was no longer a separate company, but a designated segment within the larger Seaboard Air Line system.

**Lena:** So, it lost its original name and identity, in a way?

**Professor Sharma:** In a corporate sense, yes. But its tracks, its route, continued to serve the same communities, just under a new banner. Now, for the second part of our story: **what happened to the line after that?**

**(Professor Sharma gestures to the later part of the timeline.)**

**Marcus:** Well, mergers didn’t stop there, did they? Railways were constantly evolving and consolidating.

**Professor Sharma:** You’re absolutely right, Marcus. The mid-20th century saw even more massive railway mergers. In 1967, the Seaboard Air Line, our main player here, merged with its long-time rival, the Atlantic Coast Line Railroad, or ACL. This created a new giant: the Seaboard Coast Line Railroad, or SCL.

**Chloe:** So, the Lewiston Subdivision, which used to be the Roanoke and Tar River, was now part of the SCL.

**Professor Sharma:** Exactly. And interestingly, the Lewiston Subdivision connected with an ex-ACL line in a place called Kelford. These mergers often led to rationalization of routes, keeping the most efficient ones and abandoning redundant or less profitable segments.

**Lena:** Did the SCL last long? Or did it get absorbed too?

Fremantle Octopus is an Australian octopus fishery business based in Fremantle, Western Australia. It was founded by former rock lobster fishermen Ros and Craig Cammilleri.The company catches and processes Octopus djinda. The species of octopus is regarded as having a relatively high grade based on size, texture, and taste; thought in part to be a result of its natural diet in the local environment. Products made by the fishery include frozen raw tentacles, steamed tentacles, and marinated octopus.The business processes octopus catch from various independently owned boats, and has a processing plant in the suburb of O'Connor. The business' founder Craig Cammilleri has been credited as the inventor of the 'octopus trigger trap', a method for catching octopus that uses a plastic grab with an in-built LED light to lure octopus. Baby octopus and fish are not strong enough to trigger the trap. The business operates in a fishery with Marine Stewardship Council certification, one of only two octopus fisheries in the world where that is the case. The total catch of Octopus djinda in WA is around 300 tonnes per year, of which Fremantle Octopus processes around 70%. Estimates have placed the sustainable catch rate for the fishery at around 1-2 thousand tonnes per year. Prior to being a valuable commodity, octopus were an annoyance for rock lobster fisherman as a predator of their catch.Around 80% of the fishery's catch is sold domestically in Australia, with 20% exported to foreign markets including the US, Singapore, Hong Kong and Dubai. In 2019 the business expanded its exports to the Chinese market.In 2017 the company explored a float on the ASX.

---

**Misteri Gurita Fremantle: Sebuah Perjalanan Rasa dan Keberlanjutan**

"Oke, semuanya, perhatikan!" Bu Dewi, guru Ekonomi dan Bisnis, mengetuk papan tulis dengan spidolnya. "Hari ini kita akan menyelami dunia bisnis makanan laut. Ada yang tahu apa itu 'Fremantle Octopus'?"

Ruangan kelas 11 IPA 3 hening sejenak. Beberapa siswa saling berbisik, mencoba mengingat-ingat.

"Bu, apakah itu semacam gurita yang hidup di Fremantle?" tanya Bima, si paling suka berhipotesis.

Bu Dewi tersenyum. "Hampir tepat, Bima. Fremantle Octopus bukan hanya gurita, tapi juga nama sebuah perusahaan. Dan pertanyaan intinya adalah: **apa produk utama Fremantle Octopus dan di mana lokasi bisnisnya?**"

Siswa mulai mencatat. Bu Dewi melanjutkan, "Bayangkan kalian adalah konsultan bisnis yang sedang meneliti perusahaan ini. Mari kita bedah informasi yang ada."

"Fremantle Octopus adalah bisnis perikanan gurita dari Australia. Mereka berbasis di **Fremantle, Australia Barat**," jelas Bu Dewi sambil menunjuk peta Australia yang terpampang di dinding. "Tepatnya, pabrik pengolahannya ada di pinggiran kota O'Connor. Jadi, pertanyaan kedua sudah terjawab, kan?"

"Berarti dia di Australia, Bu!" seru Dina.

"Betul sekali, Dina. Sekarang, tentang produk utamanya. Apa yang mereka tangkap dan jual?" Bu Dewi menatap siswa-siswanya, menunggu jawaban.

"Gurita, Bu!" jawab beberapa siswa serempak.

"Tepat! Tapi gurita jenis apa?" Bu Dewi menantang. "Mereka secara spesifik menangkap dan memproses spesies gurita bernama **Octopus djinda**."

Risa, yang gemar kuliner, mengangkat tangan. "Bu, apakah gurita ini enak? Maksud saya, kenapa harus jenis itu?"

"Pertanyaan bagus, Risa!" Bu Dewi mengangguk. "Octopus djinda ini dianggap memiliki kualitas yang sangat baik. Ukurannya, teksturnya, dan rasanya, semuanya istimewa. Konon, ini karena pola makan alaminya di lingkungan lokal sana. Jadi, mereka tidak hanya menjual 'gurita', tapi gurita berkualitas tinggi."

"Lalu, bagaimana mereka menjualnya? Apakah hanya gurita utuh?" tanya Kevin, yang lebih tertarik pada aspek pengolahan.

"Nah, ini bagian menariknya," Bu Dewi melanjutkan. "Produk utama mereka bukan hanya gurita mentah. Mereka mengolahnya menjadi beberapa bentuk yang siap dikonsumsi atau dijual ke restoran. Produk-produk yang dihasilkan antara lain **tentakel gurita mentah beku, tentakel gurita kukus, dan gurita marinasi**. Jadi, produk utamanya adalah **berbagai olahan dari gurita Octopus djinda**."

"Jadi, intinya, mereka menjual olahan gurita Octopus djinda, Bu, dan lokasinya di Fremantle, Australia Barat, tepatnya di O'Connor?" Bima merangkum dengan cepat.

"Persis!" Bu Dewi tersenyum puas. "Tapi ada hal lain yang membuat perusahaan ini istimewa. Bisnis ini didirikan oleh Ros dan Craig Cammilleri, mantan nelayan lobster. Mereka bahkan menciptakan metode penangkapan gurita yang inovatif, yaitu 'octopus trigger trap' yang ramah lingkungan. Perusahaan ini juga memproses sekitar 70% dari total tangkapan Octopus djinda di WA, yang mencapai sekitar 300 ton per tahun."

"Wow, banyak juga ya, Bu!" komentar Sita.

"Ya, dan yang lebih penting, perikanan mereka memiliki sertifikasi Marine Stewardship Council (MSC). Ini artinya, mereka menangkap gurita dengan cara yang bertanggung jawab dan berkelanjutan, memastikan populasi gurita tetap terjaga. Hanya ada dua perikanan gurita di dunia yang punya sertifikasi ini, dan Fremantle Octopus adalah salah satunya!" Bu Dewi menjelaskan dengan bangga.

"Jadi, produk utama mereka bukan hanya enak, tapi juga ramah lingkungan?" tanya Risa takjub.

"Benar sekali, Risa. Sekitar 80% dari hasil tangkapan mereka dijual di Australia, dan 20% lainnya diekspor ke berbagai negara seperti AS, Singapura, Hong Kong, Dubai, bahkan China. Jadi, Fremantle Octopus bukan hanya bisnis lokal, tapi juga pemain global di pasar makanan laut berkualitas tinggi."

Bu Dewi menatap siswa-siswanya. "Dari pelajaran hari ini, apa yang bisa kalian simpulkan tentang Fremantle Octopus?"

"Produk utamanya adalah berbagai olahan gurita Octopus djinda, Bu!" jawab Kevin.

"Dan lokasinya di Fremantle, Australia Barat, di pabrik O'Connor!" tambah Dina.

"Plus, mereka sangat peduli keberlanjutan dan kualitas!" seru Bima.

"Tepat sekali, anak-anak!" Bu Dewi tersenyum. "Fremantle Octopus adalah contoh bagus bagaimana sebuah bisnis bisa menghasilkan produk berkualitas tinggi, berinovasi, dan tetap menjaga kelestarian lingkungan. Ini adalah pelajaran penting dalam dunia bisnis modern."

Para siswa mengangguk, mencatat poin-poin penting. Mereka tidak hanya belajar tentang sebuah perusahaan, tetapi juga tentang pentingnya keberlanjutan dan inovasi dalam dunia bisnis. Misteri Gurita Fremantle telah terpecahkan, dan meninggalkan inspirasi baru.

## Penulis Paralel Aktif

Instruksi Output:
Berikan ulasan kritis menggunakan format di bawah ini. Sajikan alasan Anda dalam bentuk paragraf yang mengalir dengan baik. Hindari penggunaan simbol khusus yang berlebihan. Pastikan setiap penilaian mencerminkan landasan teori yang disebutkan.

Panduan Jangkar Skor (Score Anchors) untuk Skala 1 hingga 5:
Untuk menjaga reliabilitas dan konsistensi penilaian otomatis (merujuk pada validitas rubrik analitik dalam sistem AWE menurut Fleckenstein et al., 2023), gunakan acuan rubrik berikut saat memberikan skor:
Skor 1 (Sangat Kurang): Bukti pemahaman atau kepatuhan sangat minim dan melenceng jauh dari tujuan atau instruksi dasar.
Skor 2 (Kurang): Ada upaya awal, tetapi memiliki kelemahan fundamental yang mengganggu pemahaman atau keluar dari kaidah target usia.
Skor 3 (Cukup): Memenuhi ekspektasi dasar, namun narasi atau nilai pendidikannya masih terasa kaku dan memerlukan revisi substansial.
Skor 4 (Baik): Konsep tersampaikan dengan baik, memenuhi standar pedagogis dan instruksi, dengan sedikit ruang untuk perbaikan minor.
Skor 5 (Sangat Baik): Eksekusi luar biasa, sangat menarik secara emosional, inovatif, dan sempurna dalam memenuhi instruksi serta teori pembelajaran.

Relevansi Tema dan Tujuan (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai seberapa kuat cerita ini berpijak pada permintaan awal dan tema yang dipilih. Analisis apakah konsep utama tersampaikan dengan jelas. (Landasan Teori: Prinsip "Constructive Alignment" dalam penilaian formatif, di mana tugas harus selaras dengan tujuan akhir pembelajaran, merujuk pada Morris et al., 2021).

Kesesuaian Usia, Kognitif, dan Scaffolding (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai tingkat kesulitan kosakata, struktur kalimat, dan kompleksitas alur. Nilai apakah elemen tersebut memberikan beban kognitif yang sesuai untuk target usia. Analisis juga apakah cerita memberikan "scaffolding" (perancah), yaitu membangun pemahaman dari konsep sederhana ke kompleks secara bertahap. Keselarasan Instruksi, QA, dan Aksesibilitas (Skor 1 hingga 5)

Saran Perbaikan Terarah (Feed-Forward)
Tuliskan satu paragraf yang berisi instruksi perbaikan spesifik yang dapat langsung ditindaklanjuti oleh penulis untuk draf selanjutnya. Jangan hanya menyebutkan kesalahan, tetapi berikan solusi konkret. Daftar Masalah Terindeks (Wajib diisi jika ada kelemahan):
Untuk setiap kelemahan yang ditemukan, cantumkan dalam format berikut — SATU baris per masalah:
ISSUE: [Paragraf N: "kutipan singkat verbatim maks 15 kata"] → [deskripsi singkat masalah] → [saran perbaikan konkret]

ISSUE: [Paragraf 2: "robot itu tiba-tiba bisa menangis tanpa penjelasan"] → Reaksi emosional tidak memiliki dasar logis dalam narasi → Tambahkan satu kalimat sebelumnya yang membangun kemampuan emosional karakter secara bertahap.

"Ecobasic, huh?" Maya murmured, clicking on the accompanying article. Her eyes widened as she read the opening paragraph.

"Professor Anya," Maya exclaimed the next day, her laptop open to the Ecobasic's page. "I found something amazing! It’s called the Fiat Ecobasic, and it was a concept car from 1999. But the article says its purpose was to prove something really ambitious."

Professor Anya, a woman with a gentle smile and an encyclopedic knowledge of automotive history, adjusted her glasses. "Ah, the Ecobasic! A fascinating project indeed, Maya. Tell me, what did you learn about its core mission?"

Maya leaned forward, her enthusiasm palpable. "The article says Fiat wanted to prove it was possible to design and build a car that could carry four adults, but with a structure made entirely of *recyclable composite materials*. And get this – its production and operating costs were supposed to be *ultra-low*."

Professor Anya nodded approvingly. "Precisely, Maya. In the late 1990s, the automotive industry was grappling with a growing awareness of environmental impact and the need for more affordable transportation. The Ecobasic was Fiat's bold answer to these emerging challenges. Think of it as a whispered question to the future: 'Can we build a car that's both practical and profoundly responsible?'"

"So, it wasn't just about making a cool-looking car?" Maya clarified.

"Far from it," Professor Anya explained. "The 'purpose' of the Ecobasic was multi-faceted, almost like a scientific experiment on wheels. Let's break it down." She gestured to the projector, and the image of the Ecobasic filled the screen.

"**First, the 'four adults' part.** This wasn't just a random number. It demonstrated a commitment to practicality. Many ultra-compact or 'eco' concepts at the time sacrificed passenger space. Fiat wanted to show that even with radical new approaches, a car could still fulfill its primary function: comfortable transportation for a small family or group of friends. They weren't just thinking about a single commuter; they were thinking about everyday life."

"That makes sense," Maya mused. "You wouldn't want an eco-car that was too small for your friends."

"Exactly," Professor Anya continued. "**Then came the groundbreaking part: 'a structure made of fully recyclable composite materials.'** This was revolutionary for its time. Traditional car manufacturing relies heavily on steel, which is energy-intensive to produce and recycle. Composites, like advanced plastics reinforced with fibers, offered the potential for lighter weight, which directly translates to better fuel efficiency. But the 'fully recyclable' aspect was the real game-changer. Imagine a car that, at the end of its life, doesn't become a heap of waste, but rather a source of new materials for other products. It’s the ultimate closed-loop system, a dream for circular economy advocates even today."

Maya's eyes gleamed. "So, they were thinking about the *entire lifecycle* of the car, not just when it was being driven?"

"Precisely! And that leads us to the third crucial element: **'whose production and operating costs were ultra-low.'** This was about accessibility. If you want sustainable transportation to be widespread, it can't be exclusive. Fiat envisioned a car that was affordable to build, meaning less energy and fewer expensive resources were needed in its creation. And 'ultra-low operating costs' meant it would be cheap to run – fuel-efficient, easy to maintain, and perhaps even with parts that were simpler and cheaper to replace. This was about democratizing eco-friendly driving."

Professor Anya then pointed to some details on the Ecobasic's image. "Look at the design. The Ecobasic wasn't just *styled* to be aerodynamic; it was meticulously *studied in the wind tunnel*. A drag coefficient of just 0.28 was exceptional for its time. Why do you think that was important for 'ultra-low operating costs'?"

"Less drag means less fuel needed to push the car through the air!" Maya replied instantly. "So, it would be more fuel-efficient."

"Bingo!" Professor Anya beamed. "And what about that transparent hatch on the front grille, giving direct access to fluids and battery terminals?"

Maya thought for a moment. "That would make maintenance easier, right? You wouldn't need a mechanic for simple checks, which would save money on repairs."

input.question_raw: Question: What is the purpose of the Rainbow Plaque programme in the UK, and how does it compare to other plaque programmes?
input.question: What is the purpose of the Rainbow Plaque programme in the UK, and how does it compare to other plaque programmes?
input.user_message: Create an educational story that helps students understand: What is the purpose of the Rainbow Plaque programme in the UK, and how does it compare to other plaque programmes?
merged_contexts:
The Rainbow Plaque programme is a UK scheme installing commemorative plaques to highlight significant people, places and moments in LGBTQIA+ history. Emulating established UK blue plaque programmes run by English Heritage, local authorities and other bodies, the first permanent rainbow plaque (a blue circular plaque with six rainbow colours around the circumference) was unveiled in York in July 2018. Some UK LGBT locations are denoted by pink plaques, an idea that predated rainbow plaques.

History
The rainbow plaque programme was initiated in 2018 by York Civic Trust and the York LGBT Forum to honour lesbian diarist Anne Lister (1791–1840) and her partner Ann Walker, with the first version of a plaque unveiled on 24 July 2018, replaced with amended wording including the word 'lesbian' in February 2019. Temporary cardboard plaques were also placed on key sites during LGBT pride campaigns in York in 2018 and Leeds in 2019.The permanent plaque initiative then extended nationally through the Wandsworth LGBTQ+ Forum and Studio Voltaire, unveiling permanent plaques for Oscar Wilde at Clapham Junction railway station on 24 July 2019, and for the 1980s film My Beautiful Laundrette on Wilcox Road in South Lambeth on 10 September 2021.In 2023, five further rainbow plaques were announced for London, supported by the Mayor of London's Untold Stories Fund and Wandsworth Oasis.
Greenwich Tavern - Then a well-known gay bar, the Gloucester Arms (today the Greenwich Tavern) in Greenwich was the location of a key scene in the 1996 film Beautiful Thing which was set and filmed in Thamesmead and Greenwich in southeast London. The plaque was unveiled at the Greenwich Tavern on 23 July 2023.
Black Lesbian and Gay Centre - Originally established in Haringey in 1985, the centre moved to a converted railway arch in Peckham in 1992. London Lighthouse - Founded in 1986 and based in Ladbroke Grove, the London Lighthouse was a centre and hospice for people with HIV/AIDS.
Haringey Council - Haringey was a pioneer in the LGBTQIA+ rights movement in the 1980s, establishing a Lesbian and Gay Unit in 1986, while the local Positive Images group - formed to increase lesbian and gay visibility - was established in the same year.

Pink plaques
Predating rainbow plaques, pink triangle plaque memorials have memorialised gay people killed in the Holocaust and victims of anti-gay violence. In the UK, the idea of pink plaques to more generally commemorate and celebrate LGBT heritage was promoted in a 1986 book, The Pink Plaque Guide to London, written by Michael Elliman and Frederick Roll and published by Gay Men's Press. Pink plaques were also discussed in Brighton in 2006, and a mobile phone app was later (2020) created to guide users to Brighton pink plaque locations.Pink plaques have been unveiled in some UK locations to celebrate LGBT heritage.
